NOT REPRODUCED: the call structure is established, but no test raises a post-mount rejection, so which of `loadFontAssets` (`:316`), `reviveThemeEnvelope` (`:324`) or the direct `refresh()` (`:359`) can actually reject is unmeasured -- the reading shows the path exists, not that anything walks it. Filed rather than fixed because the answer is a design decision about what a wall display should do when it breaks late, and because the behaviour predates plan 8, which merely widened it.

title: No e2e fixture raises a data gap and a composition gap together, so the pair section 97 describes is measured as two transport-side strips instead
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08, correcting plan 8 Task 2.3 before dispatching it, while checking whether the theme its ceiling test uses could actually raise the two strips the test's own comment named. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the seeded packages rather than assumed: `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-missing-sensor/theme.json` has artboard `{width:640,height:360,contentFit:contain}` and ONE object, a `Textbox` at `40,140` sized `420x60` -- entirely inside the artboard. `.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-hosted/theme.json` has the same 640x360 artboard and four objects, the lowest a `Textbox` at `40,300` sized `420x60`, whose bottom edge is exactly 360. Neither bleeds, so neither raises `#vigilia-crop`, and `showCropNotice` (`packages/player/src/chrome.ts:121`) is the only writer of that strip. THE PAIR THAT DOES NOT EXIST: a theme that both bleeds and binds a key no provider reports. The bleed fixtures (`HOST_BLEED_THEME_ID`, `HOST_BLEED_ALL_THEME_ID`, `e2e-bleed-*`) bind real keys, so they raise a composition gap and no data gap; the missing-sensor fixture binds an unreportable key and raises a data gap and no composition gap. SECTION 97's rationale -- that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as different things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once -- is therefore not exercised as a pair by any browser test. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT IN THE PLAN RATHER THAN HERE: Task 2.3's second test keeps its two-strip assertion, because the chrome ceiling is about total chrome height and not about which notices make it up, and its comment now says the pair is a data gap beside a TRANSPORT gap (`#vigilia-connection`, drawn because the test aborts `**/ws`) instead of claiming a composition gap. Filed rather than fixed because closing it means adding a fixture to `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts` that is both bleeding and missing-sensored, which is a decision about fixture inventory rather than a change to the code under test.

RULED 2026-10-12: ADD the fixture — one document that both bleeds and binds a key the host cannot report. §97's rationale is that an unreadable sensor and a cropped object must be legible as DIFFERENT things, which is why two strips may be on screen at once, and no browser test exercises that pair today: Task 2.3's two-strip assertion passes with a transport gap standing in for the composition gap, which is a different pair. Fixture inventory is the test suite's own decision and this is the entry it is missing, against a requirement that already exists rather than a new one. It is a change to the evidence and not to the code under test, which is why the row was filed rather than fixed.

title: No tsconfig includes tests/e2e, so a type error in any browser spec is checked by nothing
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08 while running plan 8 Task 2.3's gates on a new spec file (`src/web/tests/e2e/host-chrome.spec.ts`, commit 1e52b8da), and it is repo-wide rather than this task's. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the configuration rather than assumed: `cd src/web && npm run typecheck` runs `npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present`, and `package.json`'s workspaces are `packages/renderer-core`, `packages/theme-package`, `packages/scene-fabric`, `packages/player`, `packages/editor`, `packages/fake-source` and `packages/host` -- `tests/` is not among them, so no workspace tsc program can see it. There is no `src/web/tsconfig.json` and no `tests/tsconfig.json` (`ls tsconfig*.json tests/tsconfig*.json` finds only `tsconfig.base.json`). Of the seven package tsconfigs, `renderer-core` includes `src/**/*.ts` and `theme-package` includes `src/**/*.ts`; the other five carry no `include` at all and fall back to TypeScript's default, which is `**/*` relative to the config's own directory -- so every one of them is scoped inside its own package. The one config that mentions tests, `packages/editor/tsconfig.json`, mentions them in a comment about `src/core`'s architecture tests and includes only `src/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.tsx`. WHAT STILL RUNS: `./node_modules/.bin/biome lint tests/...` checks syntax and style but is not a type checker, and Playwright transpiles specs with esbuild, which strips types without checking them -- so a spec that reads a property which does not exist on a fixture, or passes the wrong shape to a helper, fails only at runtime and only in the branch that reads it. NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT BLOCKING: this is the state every existing browser spec has always been in, and it cost nothing in this task because the new file's helpers are copies of a spec that runs. It is filed because the absence is invisible -- a green `npm run typecheck` reads as coverage of the whole workspace, and it is not -- and because the fix is a decision rather than a one-liner: adding `tests/` to a program pulls `@playwright/test` and both DOM and Node libs into one project, which is the conflict the editor's tsconfig already documents for `@types/node`. NOW LOAD-BEARING (2026-10-09, plan 3's close): plan 3 rewrote three tests/e2e/ specs (author-journey-rebuild, inspector-sections and editor-canvas) and added four parity captures, and none of that is typechecked by any tsconfig - which the close's own reviews kept re-learning, since the standing trap 'tests/e2e/ belongs to no tsconfig' had to be stated in briefs to stop a mis-typed locator passing review. The risk is no longer theoretical.

RULED 2026-10-12: YES — `tests/e2e/` joins a tsconfig program, as its OWN project rather than by folding into the editor's. The absence is invisible and now load-bearing: plan 3 rewrote three specs and added four parity captures with no typechecker anywhere, and briefs had to carry a standing warning so a mis-typed locator would not pass review — an error class that only review catches is the state `npm run typecheck` exists to prevent. Its own `tsconfig.e2e.json` rather than a shared program, because the DOM/Node lib conflict is exactly what TypeScript solves by separating projects: the e2e project needs Playwright's types and the DOM, and pulling those into the editor's program would trade one missing check for a weaker one. Wire it into the typecheck script in the same commit, or the project exists and nothing runs it.

title: A theme install that loses the staging rename to EPERM fails a spec outright, and the cascade reads as unrelated defects
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY, where it was the single largest reason a full browser-suite run was unreadable. THE MECHANISM: the e2e host installs a fixture by writing into `.e2e-host-app/themes/.staging-<random>.<fixture>` and renaming it onto the fixture's own directory. Under parallel load that rename intermittently loses with `EPERM: operation not permitted` on Windows, and the spec fails at the install: `the host accepted the fixture: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...\.staging-muzerquni8dhlraixl.e2e-clip-parity' -> '...\.e2e-host-app	hemes\e2e-clip-parity'`. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG IS THE BLAST RADIUS, not the race. In one full-suite run that failure accounted for 17 of 21 unexpected results without appearing 17 times: every spec whose fixture did not install then fails somewhere else - five on a missing object (`no object with id authoring`, `no object with id mover`, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'groupContext')`), three on `#status` never reaching the text the spec waits for - so ONE filesystem race presented as five unrelated defect classes across glass, clip, snapping and appearance specs. That is precisely the shape that gets misattributed to whatever diff happens to be in the tree, and it very nearly was here. THE SAMPLE THAT CLASSIFIES IT: re-running the same spec set with the box quiet left 4 unexpected, and `clip-parity` run entirely alone is 2 expected / 0 unexpected. So it is load- or handle-dependent and NOT a standing red; the remaining 4 were `vg-151` (known open) and `vg-196` (filed separately). The staging directory is left clean - no `.staging-*` survived either run - so nothing is wedged between runs. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the handle belongs to the host's own file watcher on the themes directory, to an indexer or scanner on this box, or to a previous run's host process that had not fully exited is not measured, and no other session's Chromium is implicated because none was on the box for the classifying run. THE FIX IS PROBABLY SMALL AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE: a bounded retry around the rename is the obvious repair, since the staging directory is the host's own and a lost race currently fails the spec outright with no attempt to recover. Worth pairing with whatever owns `themes/store.ts`'s install path, because `vg-174`'s LAN move work is in the same neighbourhood. RUN TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, --workers=1): `npx playwright test clip-parity --workers=1` is 2 expected / 0 unexpected / 2 skipped, no EPERM and no `.staging-*` left behind - the same quiet-box reading the row already records, so it adds nothing to it. The bounded retry the row names as the repair was NOT implemented: the row own cause is unestablished (the handle holder is not measured), so a retry would be a guessed fix under the closing rule rather than a repair with a named owner. The row stays open.

title: The docs map sent architecture decisions to `adr/` while the live decision register is `decisions/`: the map is fixed, and whether `docs/adr/` is merged into `decisions/`, kept as a second class of record, or removed is still open
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT while adding a row to docs/README.md for the new design language, so this is a doc-map defect spotted in passing rather than the task being done. MEASURED: docs/README.md's table has the row 'Why major architecture choices were made | adr/'. Two directories exist and they are not the same register: docs/adr/ holds 0002-0010 plus its own README, and docs/decisions/ holds 0019-0039 plus its own README. AGENTS.md's *Reuse before build* section names the live one plainly - 'Land a note at docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md' - and scripts/reuse-gate.mjs enforces writes against that directory, so the gate and the map disagree about where a decision note goes. The numbering is contiguous when the two are read together (0002-0010, then 0019-0039) and there is a gap at 0011-0018, which is consistent with decisions/ having replaced adr/ at 0019 rather than with two registers running in parallel. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether adr/ is deliberately kept for a different class of decision - nothing in either README says it is, and both READMEs describe the same thing, one file per decision where the way something is built was not obvious. That is the same text in both places, which is what a superseded directory looks like when it was copied and then diverged. The cost is that the canonical map - the file AGENTS.md points a fresh session at for durable project truth - sends a reader to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010. The fix is a judgement rather than a lookup, which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit: either the map points at decisions/, or adr/ is the live one and decisions/ is the mistake, or the two are merged and the gap at 0011-0018 is explained. Nothing here changes either directory. AMENDED 2026-10-12 by the dead-code sweep's Task 6 (`f7900f5c`) and retitled by Task 7 to what survives. THE MAP HALF IS DONE: `docs/README.md`'s row now reads "`decisions/` - the live register, and the one `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` enforces; the earlier set stopped at 0010 in `adr/`", so the disagreement this row's old title stated - the map sending readers to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010 - no longer holds, and the map is no longer one of the three candidates. WHAT SURVIVES is the half the row raised and Task 6 explicitly did not settle: whether `docs/adr/` (0002-0010, last commit `36f141b1`, 2026-09-25) should be merged into `decisions/`, kept as a deliberate second class of record, or removed. The two directories' numbers still collide (both hold a `0004`), the gap at 0011-0018 is still unexplained, and nothing rules between the three. Retitled rather than closed for that reason, exactly as `vg-266` was.

RULED 2026-10-12: KEEP `docs/adr/` as a CLOSED series and make its citations explicit — do not merge, do not remove, do not renumber. Merging is not available at a price anyone should pay: the two series collide across 0001-0010 (both hold 0001-0005, and both hold a 0004 on a different decision), so a merge renumbers one of them and breaks every citation to the other, and this repo's citation discipline is what makes that cost real rather than theoretical. Removing is rejected because 0002-0010 still bind the architecture — `0002-fabric-is-the-single-renderer` is the decision the whole product is built on, and `0010` is the dispatch-record rule `AGENTS.md` cites by number — and deleting a decision that still governs is not housekeeping. What the row needs is legibility, which is cheap: a header in `docs/adr/README.md` saying the series closed at 0010 on 2026-09-25 and its numbers are its own, a citation convention that always writes the directory (`adr/0004` against `decisions/0004`), and one line in `docs/decisions/README.md` accounting for the 0011-0018 gap so the next reader does not go looking for it.

title: `--shell-warm` stayed a pastel in ember, moss and plum while those palettes' paper is light, so every `--warn` text reads at 1.4-2.0:1
detail:
FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run. title: A well's horizontal padding is 6px, where bible section 3's table assigns 4px to inside-a-control and the mockup draws 8px
detail:
FOUND BY THE MOCKUP COMPARISON this plan's task 4 owes (the difference list beside `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html`). MEASURED: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-well.tsx:54` pads every well `px-[var(--space-6)]` = 6px, and the same 6px carries through the select trigger, the swatch well and the number wells. Bible section 3's spacing table is an assignment as well as a set: `4` is 'Inside a control (well padding, icon button)' and `6` is 'Between the rows of one section', so 6px here is a step that belongs to a different place. The checked target disagrees with itself: `docs/design/mockups/inspector-controls.html` draws the select and range wells at `padding:5px 8px` and the slider's value well at `4px 6px`, so it offers 8, 6 and an off-scale 5 for the same job. Three sources, three answers, which is why this is a row rather than an edit - the value is contested, not merely unspecified. WHY THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH IT: `design-language.spec.ts` asserts that every authored spacing value is a step from section 3, which 6px is; it cannot see that the table assigns that step elsewhere, and no closed assertion can without the table becoming code. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design ruling between three authorities and it moves the width of every control, including the 36px value well and the 246px pane's own gutters. SEVERITY: low - the chrome reads correctly today and only the step assignment is wrong.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: 6px. The product ships 6 and the drawing's own value well draws 4px 6px for the same element, so the mockup agrees with the product where it draws a well; section 3's 4px is the step inside a control rather than this row's horizontal padding, and the mockup's 5px 8px wells are the half that is corrected.

title: A pane's title bar and footer scroll with its body, against bible section 7.7, because the aside is the only scroller
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's task review. editor-shell.css:782-787 puts overflow:auto on aside.editor-shell-panel, and that aside contains the pane header, the body and the footer, so scrolling a long list takes the title bar and the toolbar off screen with it. Bible section 7.7 requires a pane's title and footer to stay outside the scrolling body, and layer-panel.tsx:809-810 carries a comment asserting exactly that property - "the toolbar stays put while the list scrolls beneath it" - about a structure that does not have it. The comment is corrected in Task 2's fix round; THIS ROW IS ABOUT THE STRUCTURE, not the comment. NOT FIXED THERE because the plan's own Global Constraint makes the aside the single scroller deliberately: choosePane restores each pane's scroll offset through it and shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts pins that, so moving to a scrolling body inside a fixed frame is a layout decision spanning the plan and the bible rather than a task. OWNER: unassigned - the plan that next restructures the pane frame. SEVERITY: low for behaviour (nothing becomes unreachable; the footer is still reachable by scrolling) and medium as a bible conformance gap.

RULED 2026-10-12: The STRUCTURE is the defect and DESIGN.md §7.7 wins. §7.7 is intact and says *Chrome stays still. Pane title and footer stay outside the scrolling body* (DESIGN.md:332), which is design intent recorded from the drawing; the plan's Global Constraint that made the aside the single scroller was an implementation shortcut taken so `choosePane` could restore a per-pane offset through one element, and a shortcut taken for a mechanism does not outrank the intent it broke. The rule for the next pane-frame restructure is therefore settled here: the BODY element owns the scroll, the title bar and footer sit outside it, and the per-pane offset and disclosure state are restored through the body — `shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts` pins the shortcut, so it changes in the same commit as the structure it pins. The row stays open with its owner named as that restructure, because none of it is cheap and none of it is a one-line fix; the severity stays low for behaviour, since the footer is still reachable by scrolling, and that low severity is the reason this is a ruling rather than a task in the current phase.

title: The Add pane's data-vigilia-panel now scopes every add-pane locator to the whole pane, so a future asset control named with a shape word would collide
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's fix round and confirmed by its scoped re-review. The fix round deleted new-object-panel.ts:182's duplicate attribute and moved pane naming onto the pane itself (pane.tsx writes data-vigilia-panel={id} unconditionally), which is the right resolution - but it widens what that attribute's descendants mean. Spec locators rebuild-driver.ts:139 (addButton, hasText /^label$/), editor.spec.ts:31/789/838, composition-panel.spec.ts:1064 and author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:73 now scope the Add pane, which also holds the asset host's buttons (asset-manager/panel.ts:30-35, labelled Import, Replace, Remove). MEASURED BENIGN TODAY: the shape filters match exact shape words and the getByRole name matches (Text, Gauge, Clock, Shape) are absent from the asset labels, and no case became ambiguous in the runs. NO CSS SCOPE CHANGED: no rule keys on a [data-vigilia-panel] button descendant, and every CSS rule on the attribute is ="layers", which sat on the pane before the fix too. NOT FIXED because nothing is broken to fix - the hazard is that a future asset control whose label is a shape word becomes ambiguous in rebuild-driver.ts:139, silently, and only in that spec. SEVERITY: low; the trigger is future work and the failure would be a strict-mode ambiguity rather than a wrong assertion.

RULED 2026-10-12: TAKE THE SPEC CHURN NOW and give the Add pane's shape controls their own scope. The row's measurement is that today's locators are benign, and the hazard is that a future asset control labelled with a shape word makes one spec ambiguous in strict mode — silently, and only in the spec that happened to scope the whole pane. A locator that any unrelated surface can invalidate by gaining a label is the flake class this repo has already paid for; the fix is one stable scope hook on the shapes section and the four locators pointing at it, which is cheaper than the first misdiagnosed ambiguity. title: No gate runs biome check, so organizeImports is never enforced and import order drifts unchecked
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review, which noticed two files it was reviewing carried unapplied import ordering and that nothing in the repo would ever have said so. MEASURED: src/web/package.json defines format (biome format --write ..), format:check (biome format ..), lint (biome lint ..) and lint:fix, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:38 and :41 run format:check and lint - but no npm script and no CI step runs biome check. In Biome 2.x organizeImports is an assist action that biome check runs and that neither biome format nor biome lint does, so a file whose imports are out of order passes every gate the repo has. The concrete instance: publish-control.tsx:7-8 and shell-layout.tsx:1 at 2eeb4516 were both unorganised. NOT FIXED because adding a step to the repo's verification surface is a decision about the gates rather than about a task, and the two files were ordered by hand in Task 3's fix round instead. OWNER: unassigned. SEVERITY: low - style debt rather than a defect, and nothing downstream reads import order.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded.

title: HostingStore never polls, so an out-of-band host change leaves the editor's live indicator stale until a reload
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review as a caveat, then MEASURED by the controller against the source. HostingStore (packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:201-282) reads the host once in its constructor (:207-209) and re-emits only from its own actions - toggle() emits on the success path (:273-280) and on the refusal path (:261-270), and read() is public. So the review's phrasing 'read() runs only in the constructor' overstates it: the store does follow its own writes. What is genuinely missing is any poll or host-pushed update, so a change made outside the editor - the host CLI's own setLan (packages/host/src/cli/hosting.ts:29), or a host restart - is not observed until the page is reloaded or the control is pressed in-editor, and the live indicator renders a stale claim meanwhile. OWNER: Task 4's status bar owns the live indicator (its brief names PublishIndicator reading this store), so the fix belongs there if it is judged worth making; the alternative is to accept that the editor is the only in-session writer and close this as by-design. NOT FIXED in Task 3 because polling policy is the indicator's concern, not the header control's. SEVERITY: low - needs an external writer against the same host while the editor is open to be reachable at all.

RULED 2026-10-12: NO POLL — the host pushes, or the editor is the session's only writer. An editor polling the host for out-of-band changes is a timer the host owns, per this repo's own boundary (providers acquire; the host owns scheduling), and it would race the editor's own writes for no benefit the author can see. The channel already exists: the editor holds a live connection to the host, and the host is the only process that can observe its own `setLan` or a restart. So the ruling is a direction, not a feature: when the stale indicator is judged worth fixing, the host announces the change on that connection and the store re-reads; the editor never polls. Until then the row's own alternative stands — the editor is the only in-session writer by design — and that must be stated wherever the indicator's contract is written, so the staleness reads as a boundary rather than as a bug.

title: The theme document schema gives metadata.name no minLength, so an empty name validates
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5's task review and CONFIRMED by the controller against the schema. schema/theme-document.schema.json defines the theme's name as $defs/metadata/properties/name = {type: string, maxLength: 200} - there is NO minLength, so an imported or hand-edited envelope carrying metadata.name: "" is schema-valid. That reaches the identity chip as an empty name: editor-main.ts:294 reads metadata?.name ?? envelope.id, and ?? falls back only on null/undefined, so "" passes through and DocumentIdentity (which hides only on undefined) renders a nameless frame - the bible section 9 failure its own comment promises cannot happen. The code side was fixed in Task 5's fix round by switching to ||; THIS row is the schema side, filed rather than fixed because adding minLength: 1 would start rejecting documents that validate today, which is a compatibility decision rather than a bug fix. Evidence it is an oversight rather than a decision: the sibling $defs/fontAssetReference/properties/license/name and the palette and typePreset group names all carry minLength: 1, and the theme's own top-level name is the one that does not. OWNER: unassigned - whoever owns document validation; the decision is whether a nameless theme is legal at all. SEVERITY: low once the read site is defensive - no data is lost, and the worst case is a chip showing an id instead of a name.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: name GAINS minLength 1, AND THE LOADER NAMES WHAT IT FINDS UNNAMED. A theme with an empty name cannot be presented in the library, so the schema refuses it -- but a stored document that validates today is not allowed to become unloadable, so the migration supplies a name at load (from the file or a generated label) and the schema holds for anything written from now on. COST IF WRONG: a theme saved without a name gains one the author did not choose, which is visible and renameable, where the alternative is a document that cannot be opened at all.

title: The identity chip has no rule for what happens once the name is fully truncated: the fixed edited marker overflows and is clipped mid-word
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 6's completion round, from the collision assertion the controller required. At 640x360 CSS px - which is 1280x720 at the 200% browser zoom section 7.7 requires be checked - .editor-shell-identity's min-width: 0 let the chip shrink below the floor its non-shrinkable children set, so the trailing "Unsaved changes" painted from x=399 to x=483.6 while the chip's own box ended at 465 and the view cluster began at 473: a 10.6px overlap, with elementFromPoint answering SPAN where it should answer CANVAS. A comparison of the chip's BOX could never see it, which is why the assertion compares painted geometry and a point between the corners. Fixed in Task 6 with one declaration, overflow: hidden on .editor-shell-identity (editor-shell.css:1639), and that fix stands - it is containment, not surface, and R3's "do not touch the chip" ruling was about the panel/glass/elevation treatment. WHAT THIS ROW ACTUALLY IS, corrected after reading the chip's own rules rather than filing the round's framing: it is NOT that the wrong element is degraded. .editor-shell-identity-name is min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis, so the name IS the only child that can shrink and it ellipsises first; the dot and the edited marker are both flex: none. So at 640x360 the name has already been truncated to nothing and the fixed marker still overflows by 10.6px - the arithmetic matches the measurement, since the chip's floor is its padding plus the 7px dot plus two gaps plus a fixed "Unsaved changes" that cannot shrink. The gap in the design language is therefore the state PAST a fully truncated name: section 7.7 licenses truncating identity's name, and says nothing about what the chip should do once the name is gone and a fixed part still does not fit. The landed behaviour is a mid-word clip with no ellipsis, which is the one presentation section 7.7 explicitly reserves for refusals and numeric edits. A future owner should NOT "make the name ellipsise instead" - it already does. The open choices are dropping or shortening the edited marker at compact widths, allowing it to wrap, or accepting the clip and saying so. OWNER: the identity chip's presentation, or Task 10's difference list; adjacent to but distinct from vg-219, which lists the chip's three mockup differences. SEVERITY: low - cosmetic, at one breakpoint, with no data, reachability or focus lost.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: REMOVE THE UNSAVED-CHANGES MARKER FROM THIS CHIP AND KEEP ONLY THE COLOURED INDICATOR DOT. The marker was the fixed part that overflowed once the name truncated, and the dirty state is already carried by the status bar at the bottom right, so the chip loses the text rather than dropping, shortening, wrapping or accepting a clip. Neither vg-219 nor vg-230 is absorbed by this: the chip's mockup differences and the status bar's reads stand on their own rows.

title: The zoom readout opens a list without section 5's well-and-chevron vocabulary
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 6's task review (informational) and RULED to stand by the controller rather than treated as a nit. Bible section 5 states its control vocabulary is CLOSED - 'A control is one of these, or it is not a control' - and the entry for a control that opens a list is 'Well with chevron: a well, plus a small chevron in --faint - opens a list'. The view cluster's readout (.editor-shell-view-readout, editor-shell.css) DOES open a list: it is the display chooser's trigger, and the menu behind it holds Fit, the six lenses in their two orientation groups, zoom-to-selection and actual size. It renders as a bare percentage - min-width 56px, tabular-nums, transparent background, no well, no chevron. The tension is real in both directions, which is why it is filed rather than changed: the readout is genuinely ALSO a readout, and the closed vocabulary has no entry for a control that is a value display and a trigger at once, so the honest fix might be a design-language amendment adding that entry rather than a UI change. Deliberately not changed in Task 6 for a second reason: the readout must stay the chooser's trigger, because editor-display.spec.ts's chooseDisplay() helper clicks exactly that element and then picks a menuitemradio. OWNER: Task 10's difference list, with docs/design/mockups/ as the reference for how the display chooser should present. SEVERITY: low - every choice stays one gesture away and nothing is unreachable; this is about how the trigger is presented, not about what it can do.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: SECTION 5 GAINS THE ENTRY. A control that is a value display and opens a list becomes a named member of the closed vocabulary, so the zoom readout keeps its bare percentage with no well and no chevron and stops being an unnamed exception. The readout stays the display chooser's trigger, which is what editor-display.spec.ts's helper clicks.

title: The gated list's dom-test membership is two of fifteen: which of a converted surface's tests the ratchet covers is whichever task happened to add it
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 8's task review as an observation rather than a defect, and deliberately left unfixed there — the right scope for a measurement task, since its union rule is 'each task's additions' and that rule holds. The list has 23 entries of which exactly TWO are dom test files, display-switch.dom.test.tsx and pane.dom.test.tsx, while packages/editor/src/editor-shell/ holds fifteen .dom.test.tsx files. The reviewer's own wording: 'the dom.test membership rule is genuinely inconsistent, but the report declares it inherited and out of scope.' The sharpest case is a single task: Task 2 CREATED pane.dom.test.tsx, which is gated, and MODIFIED layer-panel.dom.test.tsx (65.8 kB), which is not — and Task 8 has since gated layer-panel.tsx itself, so that surface's component is covered while the test beside it is not, and its sibling's test is. Why this is worth a row rather than a shrug: a ratchet's value is that its coverage can be trusted to mean something uniform, and today it means 'the files their own tasks chose to name'. A reader cannot tell from the list whether a missing dom test was a decision or an omission, which is the same failure mode as a vacuous gate. NOT FIXED IN TASK 8 because closing it requires choosing a rule first, and the choice is the guard owner's to make once: either every converted surface's dom test joins (which would add layer-panel.dom.test.tsx, canvas-dock.dom.test.tsx, document-identity.dom.test.tsx, publish-indicator.dom.test.tsx, publish-control.dom.test.tsx, rail.dom.test.tsx, save-state.dom.test.tsx and shell-layout.dom.test.tsx — Task 8's report measures all of them clean, so the additions cannot fail the guard), or none does (which removes the two current members and changes what plan 1's list has meant since it landed). Task 8's brief scopes this out explicitly, so it is a decision rather than an oversight. OWNER: whoever owns scripts/design-tokens.gated.json. SEVERITY: low — no value goes unchecked today; the finding is about what the list guarantees, not about a violation it misses.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: this row carries D5's ruling and the plan carries no task that lands it. The plan's own closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) says a ruled row closes only 'when the change the ruling authorises lands, on the work phase that did it', and measured over both documents **none of D5's five -- this row, `vg-267`, `vg-271`, `vg-274`, `vg-286` -- appears in any work phase's list**. W3 is the phase that owns `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and its row list is `vg-166`, `vg-199`, `vg-323`, `vg-327`, `vg-329`, `vg-332`, `vg-340`, `vg-384`, `vg-385`; the other four rows appear in no phase list at all, and `vg-274`'s only later appearance is the same recording step's §8.9 drift correction. **So the ratchet's membership ruling of 2026-10-12 produced work no task took**, which is why all five are still open. **What the work needs before it can be adopted, which is where the second half of the finding sits**: the criterion. The ruling's membership test, 'a test file that renders the shell', is not one a text scanner can evaluate -- measured at `vg-286`, a literals-keyed rule gates 275 of 289 test files and 732 violations (mostly chart and fixture data in `renderer-core` and `scene-fabric`, the failure mode ADR-0040 names), while an imports-keyed rule finds the two dom tests and misses the six `tests/e2e/` specs that are most of `vg-286`'s own measured violators. One sentence from the ruling's owner pins the reading; then the work is a checker rule plus the files the row already measured.

title: The status bar renders no object or selection counts, though the bible, the spec and Task 4's own outcome all put counts on the left
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 10 (the parity capture's difference list, row 22), REPORTED to the controller rather than filed because Task 10 files no row, and VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER against the code before filing, because it is a claim about what the product does not do. Bible section 7.6 is normative and explicit: the status bar is '26px, mono, --faint, readouts only: object and selection counts on the left, save state and the live indicator on the right.' The spec's section 3.4 repeats it ('readouts only: counts, save state, live indicator'), bible section 7's own diagram prints `status bar   counts ... saved - live`, and plan 2's Task 4 made it its first Outcome line - 'a 26px full-width strip, mono, carrying counts on the left' - and named `hosts.status` as 'the span `editor-main` writes counts and messages into'. THE PRODUCT RENDERS NO COUNT. title: Renaming an object is written in two places, they refuse differently, and the validity guard lives in a module the ownership map does not name
detail:
FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. Verified from source. The validity RULE has one owner and is shared correctly — renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts:33 isObjectName — but that module has NO row in ownership.md, and by the map's own preamble a module owning a concept while appearing nowhere in the map is invisible, so nothing warns a reader not to decide it elsewhere. The two writers of the FACT disagree on the refusal path: editor-shell/bridge.ts:323-324 (layer-row rename) returns silently at :329, while selection-inspector/appearance.ts:339 reports through errorManager.warn('controls', uiCopy.inspectorFields.invalidName) at :319-325. They notify differently too: bridge fires nothing and relies on the session subscription (bridge.ts:148), while appearance.ts:345-350 fires object:modified itself. So typing a refused name has two outcomes depending on which surface it was typed in — one author action, two behaviours. NOT ESTABLISHED: neither writer was traced past the refusal branch. OWNER: unassigned; the name write belongs with the object's identity, and both surfaces should call it. SEVERITY: low — the name is refused either way, and the divergence is in what the author is told. CONFIRMED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12), after a review forced it to apply one standard in both places: this row's complaint stands. The code half is exactly as described -- the guard is now shared (bridge.ts:346 and view.ts:456 both call isObjectName), and the second writer moved from selection-inspector/appearance.ts to selection-inspector/index.ts:384. The unnamed-module half also stands: object-name.ts sits in renderer-core/src/theme/, and the registry's row for that names a DIRECTORY ("Theme semantic types/validation"), which does not name a module: the census states the rule as a row names a module when the file holding the guard is fixed by the row, which a *-manager/ directory does by pointing at its index.ts entry and which renderer-core/src/theme/ does not do for any of its eleven modules. The census applies that same standard to selection-inspector's own files too, so it is one standard rather than two, and not this row being right by luck. Consequence beyond this row, and the reason to keep it: several registry rows name directories, so the map's module-level coverage is thinner than its row count suggests.

READING 2026-10-13: the unnamed-module half is discharged — the ownership map now names renderer-core/src/theme/object-name.ts as the object-name rule's owner (dd308143). The divergence half stands and the row stays open against it: a refused rename returns silently at editor-shell/bridge.ts:341-352 and reports "invalid" at selection-inspector/view.ts:440-450.

title: A text run has no identity in the persisted model, so the inspector's row keys must come from content — an edit or a same-shape middle removal changes the key and costs the row its caret
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 3, during its fix loop. The run editor keys each row by a derived identity because `vigiliaText.runs` is a plain array with no per-run id. Two attempts were made and each trades one failure for another, which is the evidence that the model is the cause rather than the key. (1) Positional index keys: the row survives an edit, but removing a MIDDLE run shifts every later index, so React reconciles a row holding a draft onto the next run's data — the draft is displayed against the wrong run and the next blur can commit it there (filed as M1 in the task review). (2) Content-derived identity `` `literal:${typePreset}\u0000${text}` ``: a middle removal is then safe, because survivors keep their keys, but `ControlText` commits on ENTER (`components/ui/control-text.tsx:74`), so committing a typed reading changes the key, remounts the row, destroys the focused input and drops focus to `document.body` (N1). The shipped fix excludes the mutable TEXT from the identity, which removes the Enter failure and leaves a residual, recorded in `runs.tsx` rather than hidden: two literal runs sharing a type preset can still shift on a middle removal, and changing a run's preset or its source binding still remounts that row. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK. Task 3a's brief requires it to preserve 'repeat-row identity' for chart series rows, which is the same problem over the same kind of array, so it will be met again before the plan closes. PRECEDENT, NOT A GUESS. The same class was already found and fixed once: vg-044 (archived, verified) — 'A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours' — and its fix was NOT an id. It reconciles at mutation time, carrying each surviving series' own paint through the removal before the array-length repair runs. So the cheap path here is probably the same shape: carry the surviving rows' state through the removal (or hold drafts outside the row), rather than adding a persisted id. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether reconciliation is sufficient for the caret case, since a lost draft and a misplaced draft are different harms, or whether the model should simply gain a per-run id — that is a persisted-schema decision (existing documents hold runs without one) and is not a task-level call. NOT CLAIMED: that the shipped fix is wrong; it is the best of the three shapes available without a model change, and its residual is disclosed in code and in the task report. OWNER: whoever owns the persisted text-run model with whoever owns the inspector's row rendering.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: THE PERSISTED TEXT-RUN MODEL GAINS NO PER-RUN ID, AND THE INSPECTOR RECONCILES SURVIVORS AT MUTATION TIME AS vg-044 DID. An id added to persisted runs is editor bookkeeping written into the theme file, which is the line AGENTS.md draws -- persist authored state only -- and the reconciliation at mutation time is the precedent this repo already has. COST IF WRONG: the inspector carries reconciliation logic it would not need with ids; that logic already exists for vg-044.

title: isTextEntryTarget counts a range input as a text-entry target, so every shortcut the manager owns is swallowed while a slider has focus
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 7 (fix round 1, commit 4bf29bf6), which added it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. `isTextEntryTarget` (src/web/packages/editor/src/shortcut-manager/index.ts:192-213) returns true for any HTMLInputElement whose type is not in a small exclusion set - button, checkbox, color, file, image, radio, reset, submit (:202-211). `range` is not in that set, so a focused input[type=range] is treated as a text-entry target, the handler at :143-147 sets `deferred`, and the manager returns before preventDefault() and before the bound handler. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE TRAILER AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE SAY: both name Ctrl+Z (undo swallowed while a slider has focus), but the predicate gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too. The controller verified the cause at source rather than taking the trailer's word for it. WHY THE FIX IS NOT JUST ADDING range TO THE SET: the same predicate guards the bare-key canvas listeners (camera keys), so a range was presumably left in deliberately - an unmodified arrow on a focused slider must move the slider, not the camera. Ctrl+Z is a modifier chord with no native meaning on a range, so it should reach the manager while an unmodified arrow should not. That makes the repair a decision about which keys a non-text control still defers, not a one-line set edit. AUTHOR-FACING AND REACHABLE: click the slider, press Ctrl+Z, nothing happens. BLAST RADIUS: every ControlSlider the plan-1 control set renders, which after this plan is polygon sides, the shape sweep pair and glass blur. NOT FIXED HERE because the owner is shortcut-manager and the task that found it is the inspector, and the correct behaviour is a ruling rather than a patch.

RULED 2026-10-12: The predicate is wrong in KIND, not in membership: it answers "is this target a text-entry target" where the question is "does this target consume this key". A text field consumes everything printable, so the coarse question happens to work there; a range consumes its own navigation keys and nothing else, so a modifier chord must reach the manager while an unmodified arrow stays with the slider. The repair is a consumption rule per target shape, enumerated as data beside the control set that owns those shapes: a text-like target consumes printable keys, a range consumes exactly the keys it natively handles (the four arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down), and every other control consumes nothing. That keeps the camera keys on a focused slider — which is why a range was in the set deliberately — and gives Ctrl+Z back, which is the half the row measured as broken. Enumerated rather than inferred so a control the set gains later states what it consumes instead of inheriting a default nobody chose.

title: A slider in the selection column gives no live preview while dragging, so the value only moves on release
detail:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING PLAN 3 TASK 9 (the parity capture), in the built editor at 1ab06ad2, by the task reviewer and verified at source by the controller while filing. MEASURED: with the Layer Opacity slider focused, a pointer drag to roughly 50% and then 25% left aria-valuenow AND the well reading 99 throughout, and the value jumped to 26 only on mouse-up - so an author dragging a bounded number sees nothing change until they let go. CAUSE, read rather than guessed: selection-inspector/column.tsx:183-192 renders ControlSlider with onCommit and no onPreview, although the control supports a preview callback (components/ui/control-slider.tsx:30 and :112, described in its own docblock at :17) and components/ui/control.dom.test.tsx:659-676 exercises it. The field funnel has no preview half to call: SelectionEdits exposes only commit, where the sibling CropEdits (selection-inspector/view.ts:269-274) has begin/setAspect/apply/cancel. NOT A BIBLE VIOLATION, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: design-language.md section 5 says a slider MAY preview through the existing imperative write funnel, so preview is permitted and not required, and release committing one changed value is satisfied as it stands. SHARED, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: the same field renderer draws the glass blur and panel radius sliders, so every slider in the column behaves this way and the behaviour predates plan 3's Task 9. WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A PATCH: giving sliders a preview means adding a preview/cancel path to the field funnel and deciding how a preview that writes nothing interacts with the one-undo-boundary rule the same section states, across the control set, the funnel and the history boundary - a design decision with more than one owner, not a missing prop.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. A SLIDER PREVIEWS WHILE DRAGGING AND COMMITS ON RELEASE. Section 5 permits preview through the imperative write funnel; the field funnel gains a preview and a cancel path, and the preview writes no history entry -- the release commits exactly one value, which is what the one-undo-boundary rule asks. A control that shows nothing until release is a control whose value the author cannot see while choosing it, and the same renderer draws every slider in the column, so the fix is one path rather than one field. COST IF WRONG: every slider in the selection column gains a code path, and the funnel gains a state it did not have; the undo rule is the invariant this must not break.

title: writeOpacity is the selection column's sole 0-100 enforcement and has no test
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 3'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-09) as the sharpest residual of the close, and descended from Ruling AH in the plan's ledger. selection-inspector/index.ts:469-482 refuses a value outside 0-100 and warns; plan 3 Task 9 converted the Layer Opacity field from a text box to a slider (appearance.ts opacityField, control 'slider', min 0, max 100, integer true), which DELETED the only route by which an author could produce an out-of-range value - so the two text-box tests that drove the refusal had nothing left to drive and were replaced by a slider test that exercises the control's own bound. NO CONTRIVED ROUTE EXISTS, checked rather than assumed: Base UI clamps inside handleInputChange -> getSliderValue (SliderRoot.mjs:177-190) before onValueCommitted fires, SelectionInspector exposes no seam (index.ts:67-75 - root, render, setGlobals, setLocale only), writeOpacity is not exported, and editRefusal can never produce 'invalid' for this field because view.ts:380 types the opacity kind as 'number'. WHY IT STILL DESERVES AN OWNER: the guard is now the column's SOLE enforcement, so a future control reusing the 'opacity' field id with a bad value is caught in production rather than in CI. Fixing it means either a public test seam added for a test's sake or a contrived injection that would prove Base UI's clamping rather than this guard.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE GUARD STAYS AND NO TEST SEAM IS ADDED. writeOpacity is the selection columns sole 0-100 enforcement, the row established that no route reaches it except production (Base UI clamps before the commit, SelectionInspector exposes no seam, the function is not exported, the kind is typed number), so adding a public export purely so a test can call it widens a modules public surface for the tests benefit rather than the products. The guard is named in the code as production-only defence with the reason it is unreachable from a test, so its absence from CI is a recorded fact rather than an unnoticed gap. COST IF WRONG: a regression in the guard is caught in production rather than in CI; the comment is what makes that a decision rather than a hole.

title: At the bible's 246px the Composition row fits its role column by one pixel, and the attended row clips its name and key, and no test can see either
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 1'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - that is the finding. Plan 4 moved the Composition pane to the bible section 7.3 width of 246px (editor-shell.css:96, grid-template-columns: 46px 246px minmax(0, 1fr) 276px), superseding the 360px plan 2 had measured. At that width the worst name in the starter is group-trends-card, whose uiCopy role reads "Performance trends": it overflowed the row by 11px, so the implementer re-cut the row's mark slot from 40px to 28px (editor-shell.css:145) and it now fits with ONE PIXEL of slack on the one font stack measured. THE ROLE IS flex:none and is the only statement of what a row is on four rows in five, so a font stack or DPI that renders a hair wider clips it mid-word. NOTHING CATCHES IT: tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:205-206 asserts directions only (the role costs names; the shipped column clips at least as many as the superseded one) and never a pixel, so the case stays green while the role clips. WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the 246px is bible-mandated so the constraint is not negotiable here; the reviewer offered 26px as a one-number fix, but that does not remove a clip, it moves it from the role to the mark - the column the row is designed to give up - and nothing measured which loss is worse, so the correct behaviour needs a design decision. Plan 4 Task 2 RE-CUT AND RE-MEASURED IT (2026-10-10, commit f94f0f7a), and the answer is worse than the one-pixel fit this row was filed on. It is the SELECTED or ATTENDED row that loses its name, not the resting one, and the controls that cost it are the 26px boxes bible section 5 mandates, so the plan is not free to shrink them and bible section 173 wants the name readable - the two constraints meet here. The accessibility half is discharged separately and in this task (the tile now discloses its full name on hover/focus, proved by a case that fails without it); the CLIPPING remains this row's design decision. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-10 (built bundle at 788f1448, default Composition pane): the role column does NOT fit by one pixel - .vigilia-layer-role's right edge is 291 with the row's clip at 295 and the pane column at 308, so it has 4px to the row and 17px to the column; the element that gives up width is the NAME (.vigilia-layer-name is flex: 1 1 auto with min-width 43.3px and ellipsises in nine of the ten starter rows, its glyph run reaching 256 against a box ending at 246). The role's real problem at this width is not its own slack but the 4px the absolutely-positioned .vigilia-layer-state overlaps it by - see vg-265, which owns that measurement.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: NARROW THE MARK SLOT FURTHER. The left glyph column gives way rather than the name, the role copy or the reserve, so the selected row keeps its name and its key readable at the design languages 246px. The rows own requirement rides this ruling: the choice is pinned by a MEASUREMENT rather than a direction -- the worst row (all four 26px controls plus a bound key) is re-measured after the change, and the number is recorded on this row, because the current test asserts directions and never a pixel. COST IF WRONG: the mark is the column the row is designed to give up, so the loss moves there; if the narrower mark turns out to be the worse loss, the measurement this ruling requires is what shows it. MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND THE RULING'S LEVER IS DISPROVED BY THE MEASUREMENT IT ASKED FOR. The ruling was implemented on a built bundle at the floor the column's own contents set — 20px, against the 28px it shipped — and re-measured. THE ATTENDED ROW'S OWN NUMBERS ARE IDENTICAL AT BOTH WIDTHS: on the worst row (all four 26px controls plus the bound key, in a 205-row document at the 246px pane) the name is 28px short of readable and the key 41px short at 28px and at 20px alike; the one figure that moves is the role's coverage by the slot, 58px → 50px, which is `vg-447`'s symptom rather than this row's. THE REASON IS ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE: the row is 206px with 126px reserved and 6px of left padding, so its content box is 74px, while the line's natural width is twisty 20 + mark 20 + name 71 + role 31 + key 41 + four 4px gaps = 199px — and both shrinkable columns are already at their floors (the name at its `6ch` minimum, the key at zero, the role held at full width by `flex: none`), so the freed 8px only shortens how far the line overruns into the reserved strip. NO WIDTH OF THE MARK REACHES THE SHORTFALL: zeroing the whole slot would still leave the line 36px over the content box. WHAT THE NARROWING DOES INSTEAD IS A TRADE, AND IT IS NOW TWO COUNTS TAKEN IN ONE RUN (`composition-panel.spec.ts`, the shipped-column case): of the starter's 60 names 2 unclip (31 → 29) and of its 28 specimens 5 more lose their last letters (7 → 12 clipped), where at 20px the marks read `V…`, `R…`, `G…` — a column whose whole job is to be recognised at a glance and says nothing. WHAT THE ROW NOW NEEDS IS A LEVER THE ARITHMETIC CAN HONOUR, and the row already names the four: the mark (disproved here), the role copy, the reserve, and accepting the clip on the attended row. Each of the remaining three moves an invariant a ruling has already fixed — the role is `flex: none` by design, the reserve is what this ruling forbade shrinking, and 246px is DESIGN.md §7.3 — so the next move is the user's. `vg-447` is the same arithmetic seen from the other end (the role painted over rather than the name clipped) and should be ruled with this row rather than after it.

title: Sixty-seven organizeImports findings sit in the tree invisible to every gate, because nothing in the repo ever runs biome check
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE MEASURING TASK 5 OF PLAN 4 (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST. THE MEASUREMENT: from src/web, npx biome check .. reports 67 errors over 605 files, and all 67 are assist/source/organizeImports (Sort these imports) in 67 distinct files, from packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-select.tsx to packages/host/src/main.ts. npx biome lint .. over the same tree reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. THE GAP: src/web/package.json wires lint to biome lint .. and format:check to biome format .., and neither subcommand runs the assist category - assist is a third mode that only biome check reaches. biome.json carries no assist key at all, so organizeImports is on by default and fires only under check, which no npm script invokes. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the only biome steps the repo has (format:check at line 38, lint at line 41) and neither is a check. So the rule is enabled, the tree violates it 67 times, and no local gate, no CI step and no hook will ever say so. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: import order in this tree is authored by hand and drifts, and the drift is invisible in both directions - the gate cannot fail, and an implementer who runs npx biome check on the files they touched sees findings that no gate will ever surface or fix, which reads as pre-existing noise. Plan 4 Task 4 report hit exactly that and recorded an organizeImports finding on card-insert-surfaces.dom.test.tsx as pre-existing and untouched rather than as a signal. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED because the fix is a decision with a blast radius, not a patch: running biome check in CI, or wiring assist into the lint script, turns 67 pre-existing findings into a red gate in the commit that does it, and whether this repo wants import order enforced at all is a call nobody has made. The two candidate shapes - add check to the gates and fix the 67 in the same commit, or leave check out and delete the expectation - each need a ruling first. NOT URGENT: nothing is pushed, so no CI is red today.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded. This row's count is corrected as it is ruled: 60 organizeImports findings, not the 67 the line reads.

title: A refused colour in the Tokens pane is announced to nobody, and the control set has no channel for an invalid-but-still-editable field
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 5 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10, commit ebe1743b), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that is half the finding. THE REGRESSION: before Task 5 the pane relied on the platform's own refusal, `reportValidity()` on the colour input, which announced itself to assistive technology for free. Task 5 replaced it with a local error state rendered as a bare `

` (paint-list.tsx:254-258) that is a SIBLING of the field it belongs to (the ControlText at paint-list.tsx:232-253) and is associated with nothing: no `aria-describedby`, no `aria-invalid`, no live region. A screen-reader user types an unpaintable colour, the edit is refused, and the refusal is silent. WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE: the control set already has this mechanism - control-well.tsx renders a reason element and control-text.tsx:70-71 wires `aria-describedby` to it - but it is reachable only through the `refused` prop, and `refused` also sets `readOnly` (control-text.tsx:68) and `aria-disabled`. That is right for a value the DOCUMENT refuses (a locked object) and wrong here: this value is refused because the author just typed something the engine cannot paint, and the field has to stay editable so they can type a different one. Using `refused` would trap them on the stale-but-valid value. Nor can the pane wire it itself: `ControlProps.data` is typed `Readonly>` (control-well.tsx:24-32), so there is no aria pass-through, and the pane does not own the input element. THE REAL FIX IS A CONTROL-SET CONCEPT - a channel for invalid-but-still-editable, distinct from `refused`, carrying `aria-invalid` plus a described-by reason without `readOnly`. That is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a new concept in a different owner - the control set, built and closed in plan 1 - it spans subsystems, and it needs a design decision about how many refusal shapes the control set should carry. It is not Task 5's to invent, and a second ad-hoc `

` in the next pane would make three. THE TEST GAP THAT LET IT THROUGH: tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:672-697 proves the refusal HAPPENS (not-a-colour is refused, the field stays on #123456, rgb(1, 2, 3) clears it) but never that it is announced, and jsdom cannot see platform bubbles either - so neither layer could have gone red. CLOSE THIS by adding the editable-invalid channel to the control set, wiring the Tokens pane's colour field to it, and pinning that a refused value carries `aria-invalid` and a described-by reason while remaining editable. RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE CONTROL SET GAINS THE CHANNEL. A value that is invalid but still editable becomes a named member of the control set rather than the platform's reportValidity() carrying it, so the state is expressed and reviewed the way every other control state is, instead of being whatever the browser does.

title: The React control set prints its refusals in hardcoded English, so a pane's own invalid-value copy became unreachable
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 8 (2026-10-10, commit 9f6252a8) IN TASK REVIEW, AND FIRST FILED WRONGLY - this row replaces a framing that was measured false, and the correction is the reason it reads as narrowly as it does. THE FINDING: `ControlNumber` (components/ui/control-number.tsx:94,99,103,107,111) writes its five refusal sentences as hardcoded English - "a value is required", "not a number", "a whole number", "at least 1", "at most 16384" - while every other user-visible string in the editor comes from `uiCopy`. The control it replaced took its message as a parameter defaulting to `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` (number-field.ts:88), so the artboard size pair used to say "That value cannot be applied. Enter a number in range." (ui-copy.ts:650) and now says "at most 16384". That key is not dead - it is still read by number-field.ts:88, reachable only from the settings path (settings-field.ts:115 is `numberField`'s only shipped caller) - so one editor now carries two vocabularies for one refusal depending on which numeric control a surface happens to use. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ON THE FLY (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a design decision in a different owner - the copy rules are plan 6's and the control set is plan 1's, built and closed - and neither side obviously moves: `ControlNumber` could take its message from `uiCopy` (a new key, and a copy dependency the control set does not have today), or `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` could be retired and the hardcoded strings promoted into it (the copy module acquiring keys only one control uses). WHY THE FIRST FILING WAS WRONG, because the mistake is the useful part: I filed this as "a number field no longer says what it will accept until after a value is refused", asserting the old pane printed its bound (1-16384) at rest. It did not. `boundLine` is rendered only by `numberField` (number-field.ts:53-59), and the artboard pane used `linkedPair` (artboard-panel.ts:19,150 at 21a5135e), which calls `numberInput` directly (linked-pair.ts:1,55,66) - so no artboard author ever saw that line and the discoverability loss described did not occur. The task reviewer measured it three ways (`git log -S` over the file's whole history finds no `numberField`/`boundLine`/`field-bound`; the pane's own old tests never mention them; settings-field.ts is `numberField`'s only caller) and the controller re-read linked-pair.ts to confirm. The implementer's report Deviation 4 made the same claim, so a subagent's description of code it had already replaced became a register row unmeasured - a verify-the-claim failure, not a reasoning one, and the check that catches it is one grep of the base commit. Related: vg-113 (unit display options hardcoded English), vg-263 (a refused colour announced to nobody - the other half of the same question, what the control set owes an author whose value it will not take).

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE CONTROL SET TAKES ITS REFUSAL COPY FROM uiCopy. uiCopy is the repos one owner for user-visible strings and it carries a copy census, so a shared control printing hardcoded English is the drift that census exists to prevent; the control set gains a copy dependency and each consumer supplies its strings through the locale the shell already sets. The rows other half is corrected rather than ruled: the panes own invalid-value copy was never unreachable because it never existed -- the task reviewer measured it three ways -- so the live question is this one only.
