title: editor-shell.css is in no gate and no plan: the ratchet parses CSS but its list names no .css file, and 94 violations sit behind that
detail:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 5 TASK 1 (2026-10-10, commit 13984ab9), CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT, AND MATERIALISED HERE WITH THE MEASUREMENT THE TRAILER ONLY SAMPLED. The trailer named the `.editor-shell-dialog*` rules' off-scale px; the file's exposure is larger. MEASURED at 13984ab9: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`'s `gated` array (51 entries) names NO `.css` file (`grep -c '.css'` over it returns 0), while the guard itself parses CSS - `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:181`'s `const isCss = /.css$/.test(path)` selects a declaration-property parser for off-scale px, and eight of its self-test cases are CSS (:235-264, including "an off-scale px spacing is a violation" over `a.css`). Run with `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css` as its only gated file, the guard reports 94 violations across 1 file and exits 1: 23 spacing-property values (padding 11, margin 4, margin-right 3, gap 3, right 1, margin-top 1 - 2px, 3px, 7px, 9px, 11px, 13px, 18px, 62px, 92px, 122px among them), 11 hex literals outside the `@theme` definition block (`#ffffff1f`, `#7dd3fc`, `#0009` ...), and 60 off-scale px in properties that are not spacing (the 246px rail column, 276px, 340px, 560px, 720px, 980px). THE SECOND INSTRUMENT DOES NOT CLOSE IT: `tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts:10-11` asserts that every gated element's resolved spacing is on the bible's scale, but it reads `[data-fixture-root] *` (:452), and that root is the control fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`control-fixture.tsx:60`) - so a rule reaching a fixture element is enforced from the browser and a shell-only rule is not. NEITHER REMAINING PLAN OWNS IT: `settings-and-appearance.md:529` and `iconography-and-copy.md:501` both record only the file's *hex* count as "the before-state for whatever follows the redesign", and neither adds the file to `gated`, so the conversion has no task - and whether the file should be gated at all, against a per-element browser assertion being the better instrument for a stylesheet whose values are mostly layout dimensions, is a design decision rather than a task. Not fixed in Task 1: adding the file would fail the guard over 94 pre-existing values, which is a plan's worth of work and not this task's. OWNER: whoever owns `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` and the Acceptance section's "no off-scale spacing in a surface". PLAN 7 TASK 6 MEASURED IT AND NARROWED IT (2026-10-11, artefact 45ede8e4, gate work at 43e24bc5; the task review re-measured independently and the numbers held). The title's 94 is superseded - the file holds **61** violations today: 7 hex-literal, 30 off-scale px and 24 spacing px. Task 6 arrived at 67 and fixed the six whose fix is a verifiable no-op (`--shadow-raised` for `0 12px 28px #0000003d` at `editor-shell.css:358`, three `13px` for `var(--text-md)` at `:352`, and a dead `var(--shell-accent, #7dd3fc)` fallback whose token is declared on `:root` and all five palette blocks), each checked against the declaration rather than against the built output alone. THE FILE IS NOT CLEANABLE BY SUBSTITUTION, and that is why this row is still open: 24 of the 61 are spacing values whose section 3 substitution moves pixels, which is a design pass and not a task, and three of them (`margin-right: 62px/92px/122px`, `editor-shell.css:1932/1937/1942`) cannot be expressed as any section 3 step at all. The path was added to `design-tokens.gated.json`, the gate run, and the path withdrawn in the same pass - the list's contract is the files already converted (`design-tokens.mjs:9`) and ADR-0040:12 gives the reason, that a gate which starts red and stays red is turned off. OWNER: unchanged, and now with a measurement rather than an estimate. PLAN 8 TASK 9 (2026-10-11) RE-MEASURED IT AND CAPPED THE COUNT, AND THE COUNT DID NOT FALL. Measured at HEAD: **61** violations - 6 hex-literal, 31 off-scale px, 24 spacing px - so the classes moved while the total held. The two edits that moved them: the overlay's `#0009` scrim became `var(--elev-scrim)` (one hex gone, plan 8 Task 3, `51245173`) and the modal's navigation column became `width: 150px` (one off-scale added, plan 8 Task 2, `5e8ba2b0`), and a diff of the two violation sets against `43e24bc5` shows exactly those two and nothing else. NO NO-OP REMAINED TO FIX: all 61 violation literals were compared with the 114 custom-property values this file declares and none equals one, so plan 7 Task 6's substitution rule - which closed six of the 67 it arrived at - has nothing left to convert here. THE CEILING NOW LIVES IN `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` AS `CEILINGS`, a second instrument over this one file: `max: 58` (the 61 less the three named exemptions), failing when the counted violations rise above it, so it is green at HEAD and can only fall; the comparison is strict, so a count at 58 passes and 59 fails. THE THREE INEXPRESSIBLES ARE EXEMPT BY NAME AND REASON in that constant rather than in a comment: `margin-right: 62px`, `92px` and `122px` are one class - the layer row's reserved slot for n controls, `6 + 26n + 4(n-1)`, which is section 3's own 26px row rhythm plus its 6px and 4px steps and so lands off the step table by construction (`n=1` reaches the step 32 only because its gap term is zero, so 62 is not a value a step can spell). No section 3 step can express any of the three, and correcting one would move the reserved width and let the icons cover the key again. An exemption that matches nothing is itself a failure, so a licence nobody needs reddens the gate rather than sitting there silently. FOUR OF `vg-325`'s SIX DIVERGENCES ARE COUNTED BY THE CEILING, AND NAMED HERE AT `file:line` - A COUNT NAMES NOTHING, AND THE CEILING'S OWN *NAMED* VALUES ARE ITS THREE EXEMPTIONS, NOT THESE: the Close's `margin-top: 18px` (`editor-shell.css:1400`), the rail's `gap: 3px` (`:872`) and the asset buttons' `padding: 4px 7px` at `:1148` and `:1189`; the other two are not violations here (the asset-button text is a role disagreement and the nav column's `padding: 0` is off no scale). NO CLAIM OF FIXED IS MADE for the 24 spacing values or the three inexpressibles, in the commit or here. THE INSTRUMENT THIS TASK ADDED HAS ITS OWN CEILING: a count sees a rise and not a swap, so correcting one violation while another arrives leaves it green - filed as `vg-327`.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: `vg-228` carries the full measurement. In short: none of D5's five rows appears in any work phase's list, and the plan's closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) lets a ruled row close only on the phase that lands its change, so this row is ruled and unclosable until a task adopts it. The blocker is its criterion rather than its scope -- see `vg-228` for the two readings and their measured costs. D9'S FOURTH VALUE IS THE ONE STILL LIVE, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHAT BLOCKS IT IS AN INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A VALUE. Plan 8's completion report (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-settings-parity/task-10-report.md`, the D6-D10 block) lists four values under D9 as `fix` with no predating licence: the Close's `margin-top: 18px`, the rail's `gap: 3px`, the asset buttons' `padding: 4px 7px`, and the plain-DOM control buttons' text inheriting 13px. **Three are fixed on the tree**: the Close's `margin-top` is 16px, the drawing's own value (this is `vg-316`'s row); the rail's `gap` is `4px` (`editor-shell.css:1027`), which is `vg-325`'s verified work; and the asset-button rule states `padding: 4px 8px` (`:1323`). **The fourth is live.** `.editor-shell-panel [data-vigilia-asset-import]` (`:1317-1328`) and `.editor-shell-inspector [data-vigilia-run-add]` (`:1353-1363`), the two boxes that `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:112` draws as one, state no `font-size` at all, so they inherit the shell root's `font: var(--text-md) / 1.4` (`:687-689`), which is 13px where section 2 gives control text `--text-sm` 12px. The drawing draws that box at 12px in both of its own instances and states it as the longhand there (`docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:137` and `:140`: `font-size:12px`). **A third instance of the same shape is in no census**: `.editor-shell-panel .vigilia-layer-rename` (`:1332`) also states no size, so the pane's rename field inherits 13px too. **WHY IT IS STILL NOT A FIXER'S DECLARATION.** The value is settled - section 2's role table, the drawing and this census all say 12px - and the change is one pair on each rule, but no instrument reaches it and each route is guarded: (1) the declared-versus-drawn block (`src/web/tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts`, the `productRows` comparison) compares literal declaration strings, and the drawing writes its type as the `font` shorthand `font:400 12px system-ui`, which `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:392-399` refuses to answer a `font-size` question with by design ('this row reads the longhand, so a shorthand is a value it cannot see and would read as the drawing's silence'), while the product's idiom is a scale token - so neither string comparison reaches the pair; (2) the scale route (`design-language.spec.ts:2846-2862`) compares a rendered value against a declared scale token and would carry the row, but the element renders only with the Add pane open, and the surfaces that test reads are a whitelist in the spec itself (`:2790-2795`: the shell, `settings`, `settings-keyboard`, `settings-about`, `sheet`, `fixture`), so reaching it means extending the instrument rather than using it. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: the two declarations (`font-size: var(--text-sm)` and `line-height: var(--text-sm--line-height)`, whose pair the contract in `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` then holds) plus whichever comparison the parity owner wants; the instrument half is filed as `vg-442`. NEAR ROWS: `vg-442`, `vg-316` (the same rules' fill), `vg-325` (three of the four values above). **D9 IS DISCHARGED, 2026-10-13, AND THE LAST VALUE WAS RED FIRST IN A BROWSER.** The fourth value this row's previous entry left live - the plain-DOM control boxes' text, which no rule stated and which therefore took the shell root's `--text-md` 13px (`editor-shell.css:687-689`) where section 2 gives control text `--text-sm` 12px - is now stated on all three rules of that shape: `.editor-shell-panel [data-vigilia-asset-import]` with its two siblings, `.editor-shell-inspector [data-vigilia-run-add]` with its seven, and `.editor-shell-panel .vigilia-layer-rename`; each states `font-size: var(--text-sm)` and `line-height: var(--text-sm--line-height)`. The first two are the box `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:112` draws for both plain-DOM groups, and `shell.html:137`/`:140` draw this pane's own instances at 12px; the third is in no drawing, so section 2's control-text role is its only authority and is stated as such. `tests/e2e/add-pane.spec.ts` gains 'the pane's file controls take control text, not the shell's 13px base', which reads `[data-vigilia-asset-import]`'s resolved `font-size` and `line-height`: against the pre-fix bundle it failed `Expected: "12px", Received: "13px"` (exit 1), and against the rebuilt one it passes (exit 0). Focused proof after the fix: 47 test files / 696 tests green over `packages/editor/src/panes`, `.../selection-inspector` and `.../editor-shell`, which includes `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts`'s pair contract now holding all three rules. **So plan 8's D9 block has no surviving value and this row no longer carries a live parity difference**; its own subject, the file's gate membership, is untouched and stays open.

title: The design-language fixture proves the shell's global focus rule, not the portalled control's own, because it nests the row inside `.editor-shell`
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 2'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 64fea389..eba81b2a), WHICH CORRECTED THE FINDING ITS OWN FIX ROUND HAD FILED. WHAT THE COMMIT TRAILER CLAIMED (commit eba81b2a): that `components/ui/control-choice-row.tsx:54`'s `focus-visible:outline-*` classes are inert, because `editor-shell.css:1048`'s `.editor-shell :is(button, …):focus-visible` out-specifies them. MEASURED: the specificity half is true only for an element INSIDE `.editor-shell` - the shell rule is unlayered while the Tailwind utility lands in `@layer utilities` (built CSS: `.focus-visible\:outline-2:focus-visible` at offset 20264 inside `@layer utilities{` @7990, the shell rule unlayered at 39365) and its specificity (0,3,0) beats the class's (0,2,0). But the Appearance tab does not ship inside `.editor-shell`: the modal is a Base UI Dialog portalled to `document.body` (`components/ui/dialog.tsx:44-60`), a sibling of `#app` rather than a descendant of `.editor-shell` (`palette.ts:93-99`, `shell-layout.tsx:699`), so there the shell rule cannot match at all and the control's own classes are the SOLE focus treatment. The CSS author knew: `.editor-shell-settings-tab:focus-visible` and `.editor-shell-settings-panel:focus-visible` (`editor-shell.css:1246,1250`) exist precisely because the dialog is portalled, and no equivalent rule exists for the choice row. ACTING ON THE TRAILER WOULD HAVE BEEN A DEFECT - deleting those classes as redundant strips the shipped product's focus ring, while the design-language fixture stays green because there the shell rule paints the outline. THE REAL FINDING IS THE PROOF-CONTEXT GAP: `control-fixture.tsx:145-175` mounts `ControlChoiceRow` inside the fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`:62`), and `design-language.spec.ts`'s new §4e case (`~:866-1030`) asserts a `solid` outline of at least 2px there - which the shell's global rule supplies. So §4e passes even when the control's own focus classes paint nothing, and cannot detect a regression in the treatment that actually ships on the portalled modal. The implementer's own red proof demonstrates exactly this: removing the shell focus rule reddened the case with `paints the browser's auto ring, not §5's solid outline`, while the classes were the thing under test. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix is a decision about how a portalled surface is measured (a second fixture outside `.editor-shell`, or a browser case on the real modal) rather than a one-line change, and this plan's Task 6 owns the capture. OWNER: whoever owns `components/ui/` and the design-language fixture's context.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`'s fixture case, and the second half is the shipped portalled modal): the fixture case passes in the same run (`the control set renders in the design language`, 4156ms), and on the shipped Appearance tab a focused palette card - a `ControlChoiceRow` - computes `:focus-visible` true, `outline-style: solid`, `outline-width: 2px`, `outline-color: rgb(114, 224, 192)`, `outline-offset: 2px`, while `closest(".editor-shell")` on it is null (its only dialog ancestor is the portalled `.editor-shell-dialog`). So the ring that ships is painted by the control's own classes, and the fixture's green reads that same visual fact through the shell's global rule instead. What §4e cannot see is the control's own classes going missing.

title: The editor bundle has no product-version source, so the About tab can name no version for Vigilia itself
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4'S STEP 1 (2026-10-10), BY READING, NOT BY TESTING. Measured with `grep -rn version packages/editor/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v .test. | grep -vi canvas`: the only hits are the theme's own release version (editor-session.ts:1092 bumpSemanticVersion; panes/document/metadata-fields.tsx:101 metadata?.version) and unrelated words (Fabric's scene version 7.4.0 in new-fabric-theme.ts:188, the qr-symbol.tsx version, storage-key prose) - not one product version. `grep -rn 'VERSION|SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION' packages/host/src/main.ts packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts` finds the host's const VERSION = "0.1.0" at packages/host/src/main.ts:34, Node-side and logging Vigilia v${VERSION} at :250 and not in the editor bundle, and SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2 at packages/renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope.ts:16 (it was 1 in theme/document.ts, which schema v1's retirement deleted on 2026-10-11), a schema number this build can read but which is not the product's version. packages/editor/package.json is 0.0.0 and packages/editor/vite.config.ts injects no define. So the About tab (landed in the same commit) renders the schema version and the open document's release version, and nothing claiming to be Vigilia's own version. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: giving the product one version string both the host CLI and the editor bundle import is a host change that needs a decision rather than a task, and more than one owner could fix it, so it sits outside plan 5's scope.

RULED 2026-10-12: ONE OWNER: the workspace manifest's `version` field is the product's version, and both readers take it from there rather than from a new module. The host already runs Node and can read `src/web/package.json`; the editor bundle is built by Vite, which injects it through `define` at build time. That keeps one number, written in the place a release already has to change it, with no new exported constant and no second file to forget. Two things the fix must not do: it must not make the schema version carry the product's meaning — `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays a separate fact, and the About tab keeps labelling it as what it is — and it must not present the open document's release version as Vigilia's own. The About tab gains one line naming the product version; the other two lines keep their own labels.

title: The layer row's attended state slot can intercept a press meant for the row, so a click on a name may reach its visibility or lock control
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over 50797965..b3805273). MEASURED, in the test harness: `tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:206-222` presses a layer row through `.vigilia-layer-name` at the element's LEFT END rather than at its default centre, and its own comment records why - the centre is intercepted, and five cases of `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts` hung on it. The comment names the interceptor: the attended row's absolutely-positioned state slot (`editor-shell.css:1707-1712`, `position: absolute; right: 2px; top: 0; height: 26px`), which sits over the name because the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` (`editor-shell.css:1658`). WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is a product-side hazard or only a Playwright fixed-point problem. A real pointer that hovers a row to click it has already revealed that row's state slot, so a press aimed at the row can land on the slot's own controls (visibility, lock) instead of selecting the layer - but nobody has measured the slot's width against the row's, or what a press at the name's centre actually hits in a browser. The CSS author calls the related shift deliberate: the attended row's name narrows by whatever its key does not take, "charged to the one row the pointer is on, and it is deliberate" (`editor-shell.css:1700-1708`). That states the SHIFT is intended; it does not say the slot may swallow a press aimed at the row. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and the fix, if needed, is a layout decision about the attended row rather than a test edit; the harness works around it, which also means nothing reddens if the layout changes. OWNER: whoever owns the layer row's layout (`selection-inspector/` and `editor-shell.css`'s `.vigilia-layer-*` rules). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the pointer measurement this row owed is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the hazard is REAL at the desktop viewport. With a layer row attended (hovered) and its four-control slot drawn, the name's box reads left 120 / right 240.6 while the slot reads left 155 / right 277 — the slot overlaps the name by 85.6px — and document.elementFromPoint at the name's centre returns an SVG inside the slot's first button, where the same read 6px inside the name's left edge returns the name's own span. The cause is named: the room the :has rules reserve is written on .vigilia-layer-bound (editor-shell.css:2188-2206), this row draws no bound at all, so nothing reserves it and the absolutely-positioned .vigilia-layer-state (:2121-2134) covers the name. Three citations on this line corrected by re-measurement, as symbols and lines: the slot is .vigilia-layer-state at editor-shell.css:2121, not :1707-1712; the name is .vigilia-layer-name at :2072, not :1658; the deliberate-shift comment is at :2115-2120. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a layout decision about the attended row, which the row already says.

title: Two editor specs claim a fresh starter trips the dirty guard, which the session mechanism contradicts, while a third records the opposite sample
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART I'S SECOND SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-10, over b3805273..846e451c), which retired the same claim from a fourth file. THE CONTRADICTION: `tests/e2e/author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235` and `tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558` both assert that a fresh starter "counts as unsaved work", so opening another theme asks the dirty guard. The mechanism says otherwise: `editor-session.ts:1004-1020` asks only when `isDirty`, and `persistence-manager/index.ts:34,42` compares the current key against `#savedDocument` - the snapshot the session opened on, built at `editor-session.ts:498-501`. `editor-main.ts:233-238`'s `onNew` mounts a fresh session, so a document that has just been created IS its own baseline. MEASURED, by the implementer, against the built bundle during round 2: after Create a fresh editor shows zero `[role="dialog"]`, and Open library opens the chooser with no question - which is why the fourth file's comment (`tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts:132-138`) was corrected in `bdce766e`. WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN A TYPO: `tests/e2e/reference-theme.spec.ts:490-492` records the OPPOSITE sample - five prompts in six save-then-Ctrl+N rounds on an unchanged starter. So at least one of the three is wrong, they disagree about product behaviour rather than wording, and nobody has measured which path differs (Ctrl+N against the menubar's New is the obvious candidate, and neither the session nor the specs distinguish them). WHY THE SPECS SURVIVE: `answerDialogIfShown` tolerates the absence of a dialog, so a spec asserting a prompt that never comes still passes - the tolerant call was the right one: the driver's absolute "asks nothing on the path every caller takes" is not what `reference-theme` observed. NOT FIXED HERE because establishing which claim is true needs a browser run per path, and the fix is to the claim rather than to behaviour. OWNER: whoever owns the editor's browser journeys (`tests/e2e/`) and the dirty-guard's own contract (`persistence-manager/`). TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the runs are taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, and the fresh-starter half of the contradiction is settled against the two specs. The dialog read is [role=dialog] — Base UI portals a div, not a native dialog[open], which is why a first pass read nothing from every path. A fresh editor, Control+n then Create: the size chooser opens and NO replacement question follows. A fresh editor, File then New theme then Create: same. A fresh editor, File then Open package: no dialog at all, and the file chooser fires, which is the guard having passed. So on a fresh starter the guard asks nothing on any of the three paths, and author-journey-display.spec.ts:231-235 and composition-panel.spec.ts:556-558 — both of which state that the starter, being unedited, counts as unsaved work — carry a premise this run refutes. reference-theme.spec.ts's five-prompts-in-six sample is a save-then-Ctrl+N state, which this run did not reproduce either way; the cell's --grep New collects TWO cases and not one, because Playwright compiles the pattern as a case-insensitive regexp: the unpiped --list exits 0 with four entries, reference-theme.spec.ts:380 (a fresh document is the reference composition, and New never touches the saved one -- the case that presses Control+n) and :2444 (a new background image is imported, and the artboard is repointed at it), each under desktop-chromium and phone-chromium, so neither case presses the menubar's New and the menubar path stays measured here rather than by the cell. STAYS OPEN: the fix is a claim correction in two spec files outside this task's file list, and correcting one side of a two-sided contradiction would leave the register claiming a disagreement the tree no longer carries.

title: FontPicker has no production mount in any package, so its 357 lines and 984-line test are kept alive by tests alone while the live font surface is FontControls
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4A PART II (2026-10-10, over 8c666ea1..9fa7b7b4). The implementer raised it as its own concern and the controller confirmed it independently. MEASURED at head 9fa7b7b4: `grep -rn 'FontPicker' packages/*/src` returns exactly two consumers, both tests - `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts:19,238` (which mounts it because a copy literal inside it would otherwise be invisible to the copy audit) and `packages/editor/src/font-picker/font-picker.dom.test.tsx`. title: A browser run at playwright.config.ts's default worker count reports 30s locator timeouts as failures at a clean HEAD, on this box
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (commit 4698f233), while taking a browser baseline at 7d31622c with nothing broken. The same four specs, same commit, same built bundle: 4 failed / 23 passed at the default 10 workers, every failure a 30s locator timeout or `no control matches [data-vigilia-palette-token]`; 27 passed at --workers=2. The four: keyboard.spec.ts:18 (locator.evaluate timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:136 (locator.count timeout), panel-labels.spec.ts:208, shell-appearance.spec.ts:85 (locator.click waiting for visible/enabled/stable). CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED beyond "the machine": another session was busy on this box at the time (AGENTS.md, a long run holds the machine), and a single sample proves nothing about load or concurrency. It matters because a green suite read as red at the default worker count costs a false fix round: plan 5 Task 5's first browser baseline read exactly this way. ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT MECHANISM: vg-216 is two configs sharing test-results/ and deleting each other's traces; this is one run under load. What would settle it: run the same specs at 10 workers on an otherwise idle box, and if they still time out, bisect the worker count. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-11, WHICH NARROWS THE CAUSE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING THE ONE OFFERED: running the palette sweep (shell-appearance.spec.ts:97) ALONE at the default worker count, on an otherwise idle box at 7309eb1d, takes 8.6s and 8.5s in two consecutive runs, a whole run 12.1s - roughly 3.5x inside the 30s limit. So that test's own runtime is NOT what tips it over, and the most plausible inherent explanation is now falsified rather than merely untested. Plan 7 Task 2's fix round reported the same test timing out at 30,722ms with durations of 26.8s, 28.2s and 33.3s, and those figures did NOT reproduce: they were taken while this session was itself running Playwright against the same built bundle, which is exactly the contention this row's first paragraph names. The cause is therefore CONCURRENT BROWSER RUNS ON ONE BOX AND ONE BUNDLE, and two things follow - a red at the default count is worth nothing until the spec is re-run alone at the same commit (AGENTS.md already asks this, and this is the measurement that makes it cheap to obey), and raising this spec's timeout would not fix it, because on an idle box there is nothing to fix. TASK 2.3B'S READING ON AN IDLE BOX, 2026-10-12, WHICH IS THE GATE THIS ROW NAMES: the same three files (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`, `panel-labels.spec.ts`, `keyboard.spec.ts`) on the same built bundle, with no other suite, build or browser driving it, FAILED at `--workers=10` - this box's default, its 20 logical cores halved, which is what the absent `workers` key in `playwright.config.ts` leaves in force. 4 of the 19 desktop-chromium cases were unexpected, every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded` reading 30.7-34.1s: the keyboard modal-trap row, `no control is unnamed`, the palette sweep and the treatment-boundary row. THE FINDING REPRODUCES, so the three timeouts this row already carried are the same shape rather than another session's artifact. BISECT, same three files and the same built bundle on the same idle box, one count per run: 8 workers 3 failed (33.4s, 33.2s, 30.8s), 6 workers 1 failed (the keyboard trap, 31.4s), 5 workers none failed (19 passed, 19 skipped, 59.5s, reproducing the dead attempt's reading). Every failure sits 1-14% over the 30s limit, so the count is a load threshold on this box rather than a stable boundary, and the threshold is in the worker count rather than in one spec: this row's own controller measurement had the palette sweep at 8.6s alone, and it reads 34.1s here. THE CLAUSE THE READING FALSIFIES: the sentence above saying raising a timeout would not fix it because on an idle box there is nothing to fix is half wrong - the idle box DOES redden at the default count - so what remains is a decision about which count this suite is run at here, and a decision rather than a patch because `playwright.config.ts`'s own comment defends leaving `workers` to the default (a hardcoded count oversubscribes a small CI runner). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT NOW: that decision, on this line - pin a count for this box, or accept the default and re-run the named spec alone at the same commit before believing a red. ONE CAVEAT ON THE LIST ABOVE, which this row does not otherwise carry: the treatment-boundary row IS one of the four, and Task 2.3b rewrote that row's own setup in the very commit that took this reading -- its member sets are now derived from the stylesheet rather than named. So the row does not claim the derivation is innocent of those four reds. What rules it out is arithmetic rather than a measurement: one extra `page.evaluate` per test rather than per palette, per-palette work unchanged, and the arm reading 12.2 s alone against a 30 s limit. One sample of that arm alone at 10 workers on the BASE commit would settle it, and no such sample was taken.

title: The ratchet's gated list has no rule for test files, so a hex literal or off-scale px asserted in a browser spec or a test fixture is unchecked
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (its Step 1 coverage census), and sharpened by that task's review, which re-ran the checker over every file the plan touched rather than only the directory the report listed. MEASURED: 9 plan-touched files under src/web/ carry violations and are ungated, 6 of them under tests/e2e/ — editor.spec.ts, shell-appearance.spec.ts, rebuild-composition.ts, design-language.spec.ts, editor-rail.spec.ts, panel-labels.spec.ts. The other three are packages/editor/src/accessible-names.dom.test.ts (6 hexes), ui-copy.test.ts (7 hexes, theme fixtures at lines 114/133/141/142/146/367/368) and editor-shell.css (68), the last being vg-274. The gated list is not production-only by design: it names four test files (control.dom.test.tsx, control-choice-row.dom.test.tsx, display-switch.dom.test.tsx, settings-keyboard.dom.test.tsx, pane.dom.test.tsx and others), so the actual blind spot is that NO RULE decides which test files belong — membership was chosen file by file as each task converted something. CONSEQUENCE: a browser spec that pins a rendered colour or an off-scale spacing is a second owner of that value and no gate reads it; the violations measured today are mostly fixture data and selector strings rather than surfaces drifting, so this is a coverage hole, not nine defects. NOT FIXED HERE: widening the audit is plan 6's (2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy) and the plan's own Tasks 2 and 5 both say not to widen a coverage contract mid-sequence. SAME FAMILY as vg-274 (no .css file is gated) and vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts): each is the acceptance instrument claiming more coverage than it has. What would settle it: decide whether *.dom.test.tsx and tests/e2e are ratchet material and express that as a rule in the checker rather than as a list.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. THE RULING IS UNIMPLEMENTED AND NO PHASE OWNS IT, MEASURED 2026-10-13: D5 ruled on 2026-10-12 that TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST, with the operative clause 'the four files carrying violations become checked'. **No phase of the active plan carries that work.** Searched the plan's own text: this row's id appears only in Phase 1's ruling-recording steps (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:275`, `:319`, `:325`, each saying 'record them; do not re-ask'), and nowhere in Phases 2-10, whose row lists are closed out. Phase 4 is the phase that owns `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and it names `vg-327`, `vg-332` and `vg-340` -- not this row -- so the checker's own membership rule fell between the ruling and the phases. **THE RULING CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS WORDED WITHOUT PINNING ITS CRITERION, AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOWS IT.** 'A test file that renders the shell' is the membership test, and the checker cannot evaluate it: a test's rendering is not visible in its text. Tested at HEAD by taking the *derivable* reading instead - every test or spec file carrying a design literal joins the list - which is the reading the ruling's own operative clause invites: `git ls-files` finds **289 test/spec files, 14 gated and 275 ungated, and the 275 carry 732 violations between them**. That set is mostly files the design language has nothing to say about - `renderer-core/src/charts/fill.test.ts` (50), `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts` (49), `renderer-core/src/charts/gauge.test.ts` (38), `line.test.ts` (35), `scene-fabric/src/text-runs.test.ts` (25) - where a hex literal is chart or fixture data rather than a surface drifting. Gating them would redden the gate over values the ratchet was never meant to read, which is the failure mode ADR-0040 names ('a gate that starts red and stays red is turned off'). **AND THE IMPORT-BASED READING MISSES MOST OF THIS ROW'S OWN VIOLATORS.** The nine files this row measured are six under `tests/e2e/` (editor.spec.ts, shell-appearance.spec.ts, rebuild-composition.ts, design-language.spec.ts, editor-rail.spec.ts, panel-labels.spec.ts) plus `accessible-names.dom.test.ts`, `ui-copy.test.ts` and `editor-shell.css` (that last being `vg-274`). **A browser spec imports no shell module** - it drives a built preview - so a rule keyed on imports finds the two dom tests and none of the six e2e specs, while a rule keyed on literals finds 275 files. The ruling sits between the two readings and does not say which. **WHAT UNBLOCKS IT, WHICH IS ONE SENTENCE FROM THE RULING'S OWNER.** The criterion: whether a browser spec that pins a rendered colour is 'a test file that renders the shell' - this row's own text says a browser spec pinning a rendered colour 'is a second owner of that value and no gate reads it', which reads as yes - and if yes, whether membership is expressed as a path rule (`tests/e2e/**` plus the dom tests that mount a shell component) or as an explicit list the checker requires to be complete. With that pinned, the work is bounded: the ruling's 'four files' is a subset of the nine measured here, and each violation is a fixture value to move onto a role or a step. **Not implemented by this session, and deliberately**: the criterion is a decision about the gate's coverage, not a correction, and a session that guessed it would either gate 275 files or gate the wrong six. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: `vg-228` carries the full measurement. In short: none of D5's five rows appears in any work phase's list, and the plan's closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) lets a ruled row close only on the phase that lands its change, so this row is ruled and unclosable until a task adopts it. The blocker is its criterion rather than its scope -- see `vg-228` for the two readings and their measured costs.

title: Nothing detects a committed capture that a later plan invalidates, so the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images sat two plans stale
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 6 (commit b602dd13), by reading the images it was about to re-capture rather than by any test. The seven files committed until then under docs/evidence/screenshots/ (shell-palette-* x6 and keyboard-reference) were pictures of the PRE-PLAN-2 shell: no rail, a `Layers | Insert | Assets | Document` pane bar, a palette chip in the header, `Save package`. Plan 2 rebuilt all of that, and nothing noticed, because a capture is only ever refreshed by the action that owns it running again — and every registry in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md and docs/design/mockups/README.md names an action and a file, never a surface version or a plan that produced it. Re-captured here against rebuilt bundles. CONSEQUENCE: visual evidence in the repo can contradict the product for an arbitrary number of plans while every gate stays green, which is the opposite of what spec §13 asks a capture to be. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a detection mechanism (a marker recording the commit or shell generation each image was taken against, checked by a gate, or an ownership link from a surface to its captures), which is design work no active plan owns. What would settle it: decide who owns a capture's freshness and express it as a check rather than as a habit.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE REGISTRY OWNS A CAPTURES FRESHNESS, AND THE CHECK IS A RECORDED SHA AGAINST THE SURFACE IT DEPICTS. Each registered capture records the commit it was taken at and the surface paths it shows; a script reports a capture whose surface paths have commits after that sha, so a stale image is a finding rather than a habit. Today both READMEs name an action and a file and nothing about the product generation, which is why the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images could contradict the product for two plans with every gate green. COST IF WRONG: a new scanner and a manifest to maintain, and a capture whose surface paths are wrong is reported stale for the wrong reason -- which is visible and fixable, unlike the present silence.

title: RESERVED_LETTERS refuses a bare-modifier chord but not its Shift variant, so Ctrl+Shift+T, N and W are accepted as bindings and can never fire
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11, and confirmed at source. shortcut-manager/bindings.ts:75 lists the reserved letters (l, n, p, q, r, t, w) and :299-305 refuses one only when `binding.modifier && binding.shift !== true`, so every Shift variant of those letters passes validation and is stored as a binding the browser owns: Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab), Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window) are taken in every Chromium build, so the author binds a chord and nothing ever happens. The rule's own doc comment states the Shift exclusion as fact without stating why, which is the claim-without-a-reason shape this plan hit repeatedly. CONSEQUENCE: the refusal exists precisely so the author is told where the limit is rather than binding a chord that will never fire, and it does not cover the case that is most likely to be tried. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because the correct membership is a data decision - which chords the editor's actual browser matrix reserves - and over-refusing is its own defect (it would reject chords that do work). What would settle it: state which browsers the editor runs in, measure the Shift variants against them, and make the reserved rule and its comment reflect that evidence.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DEFECT, and the Shift exclusion is backwards: three of the four chords most likely to be tried are exactly the Shift variants the browser keeps, so the rule misses the case its own comment says it exists to catch. The rule becomes TWO sets rather than one guarded by `shift !== true` — the letters reserved with a modifier and no Shift, unchanged, and the letters whose SHIFT variant is reserved too — because the blanket exclusion was never a measurement, it was an assumption that Shift makes a chord safe. Membership is measured, not guessed: the starting evidence is Chromium's documented page-unreachable accelerators, Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window), Ctrl+Shift+R (reload ignoring cache), Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window), and Firefox is checked against them, because the host opens the editor in the author's own browser rather than one this repo chooses. The comment carries the browser and the date it was measured against — a reserved set with no provenance is the claim-without-a-reason shape this row already names. The `ponytail:` note stays: a longer list, or a key-capture API, is still the upgrade path.

title: The mockup was never replaced where a surface was deliberately rebuilt differently, so the checked reference still draws a design the product does not ship
detail:
FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the captures Task 6 had just re-taken: the gap between them and docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html is still large. WHICH GAP IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the new set includes -editorial (flat cream) and shell-palette-light captures, while the mockup is drawn on graphite (#0b0e12 per Task 6's D9), so comparing a light capture to it shows the palette rather than drift, and that has to be ruled out first by naming the files compared. THE USER THEN NAMED THE GAP, on 2026-10-10: "The panels on both sides, rail, top menu bar are all on their separate islands with rounded corners. That's completely different from the mockup. The graphite color scheme is different from the mockup's, too." Both are shell-level - plan 2's chrome and 0035's palette - not plan 6's glyphs or copy. The bible's own §3 makes panels `--radius-lg` (8px) and reserves `--radius-xl` (10px) plus backdrop blur for floating clusters OVER THE CANVAS (dock, view controls, identity chip), while the shipped stylesheet carries four literal `border-radius: 12px`, a value the closed scale (4/6/8/10) does not contain. A read-only measurement of both halves - per region, per palette role - is running as .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/mockup-vs-shell-measurement.md, and this row's detail gets the measured values when it lands. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is the structural cause. docs/design/mockups/README.md's "Keeping them current" section ends: "If a surface is rebuilt differently on purpose, capture the new state and replace the mockup file - the reference is always the current target, never a historical one", and its opening line is "These are the target." Neither parity gate did that. Plan 2's Task 10 adjudicated 22 shell differences and plan 5's Task 6 eleven settings differences, ten of them deliberate (horizontal tab strip where the mockup draws a vertical sidebar; 2-column radio choice rows with one ground+accent chip where the mockup draws a 3x2 grid of two-bar cards; no printed description under the heading; a Close the mockup omits; a Keyboard tab header and Reset placement the mockup predates; the modal painting the palette's glass), and every one was recorded in a commit while the drawing stayed as it was - so the rule the README states was applied as "say why" rather than "replace the file". CONSEQUENCE: the repo's own reference is now a historical target for two surfaces, which the README calls worse than no mockup because it is believed; the shell half carries the same shape in vg-217, vg-219 and vg-230. NOT FIXED HERE: replacing the mockup is design work over the adjudicated lists, it needs a home (plan 6's closing parity capture, or design-md-replaces-the-bible which decides the mockups' standing beside DESIGN.md), and the alternative - pulling the product back to the drawing - would reopen plans 2 and 5 and needs the user's call. What would settle it: name the files compared, then replace the settings section and the shell features the two lists adjudicated, or rule the drawing the target again and schedule the product work. UPDATE 2026-10-10, THE USER'S RULING: the mockup is NOT replaced ("Do not replace the mockup."), so the product-vs-drawing fork this row left open is closed in favour of the product, and what survives here is this row's process half alone — nothing signals that a mockup and the product have drifted, and docs/design/mockups/README.md's "replace the mockup file" rule was applied as "say why" for two surfaces across two plans (plan 2's 22 shell differences, plan 5's eleven settings differences, ten called deliberate). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-292 is the missing comparison itself — no gate anywhere compares a built surface to the mockup, so §13's parity capture could not fail; this row is the stale file, that one is the absent instrument, and the instrument is the cause.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D4's ruling on this row: it DISSOLVES INTO vg-292's instrument row -- one row, one plan, owned by Phase 10 (W9). The stale-file record stops being an item of its own.

title: The parity gate accepts any reason for a divergence, so a plan can grade its own surface 'deliberate' against a drawing it does not resemble — the rule that the mockup governs where the written rules are silent was absent
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER on 2026-10-10, answering the user's "why is it so hard to stay on target when we already have a clear visual mockup?" — the question was the finding: the process had no instrument that could report drift. MEASURED, by reading what each parity gate actually did rather than what it promised: plans 1-5 built to docs/design/design-language.md (the bible — §3 space/radius/elevation, §4 colour roles, §5 the closed control vocabulary, §7 per-surface rules) plus the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md), and BOTH ARE PROSE ABOUT A LANGUAGE. A surface can carry every correct token, every control in the vocabulary, no hex literal and the right rhythm, and still look nothing like docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html — which is exactly what shipped: the shell insets its four regions 8px apart at an off-scale 12px radius where the drawing is flush (editor-shell.css:726,729,749,814,1130,1784, filed as vg-231), and the settings modal the just-closed plan built departs from the drawing's settings section in its frame, tab strip and palette cards (evidence: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md). Spec §13 makes "a capture beside the mockups" a gate item, so every plan did produce one — six images for the settings modal alone — and every plan also produced a WRITTEN LIST of differences, ten of eleven called deliberate at plan 5 Task 6 and 22 at plan 2 Task 10. A written list is an argument; it has no failing state, so the gate could not redden and each plan closed green on accumulating drift. The controller compounded it by ruling those differences legitimate instead of treating the drawing as the acceptance test. CONSEQUENCE: the acceptance instrument claims coverage it does not have, the same family as vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts), vg-274 (no .css file is gated at all) and vg-286 (no rule decides which test files the ratchet covers). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-291 is the mockup file left stale; this row is the absent comparison, and this one is the cause. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a check or a rule — either measure a built surface's treatment and compare it to the drawing's, or make the drawing's own values the source a surface resolves from so the two cannot diverge — and that is the mockup-parity plan the user's 2026-10-10 ruling requires. What would settle it: state which surface-to-mockup comparison is enforced, name the owner, and prove it reddens on the state shipped today. CORRECTED 2026-10-10, BY THE USER, who said the verify step was requested at the outset: "I specifically requested to add a verify step to each of the plan to compare the current state against the mockup." That is true and this row's first version was wrong to say no comparison existed. VERIFIED: the requirement is in the spec — §12's table is followed by "Every plan above ends with a mockup-parity gate (§13) ... a completion condition of each plan", §13 steps 1-4 specify capture, placement beside the drawing, a difference list and an empty-diff finding, and the Acceptance section carries it as an item — and all six plans carry the gate (parity-step hits: gates 4, shell 3, inspector 4, panes 2, settings 4, copy 5). So the step existed, ran in every plan, and produced exactly this. THE REAL DEFECT IS THE ADJUDICATION RULE, at §13 step 3 as it stood: "Every difference is either fixed, or recorded in the commit as deliberate, with the reason." Any reason satisfied it. Plan 5 Task 6 listed eleven differences and recorded ten as deliberate, each citing a section's SILENCE as the warrant — D1 kept a horizontal tab strip because "§7 fixes the three tabs and what each holds, not their axis"; D2 kept two-column radio rows where the drawing has a 3x2 grid of cards; D3 kept the drawing's explanatory line absent; D9 kept the palette's glass where the drawing is opaque — and the aggregate of those locally-reasonable reasons is a modal the user described as looking nothing like the mockup. Plan 2's Task 10 has the same shape at 22 differences. A verdict that cannot be wrong is not a gate, and the missing premise was that silence in the bible is the drawing's jurisdiction rather than a licence. FIXED IN THE SPEC, 2026-10-10: §13 step 3 now requires a deliberate difference to name the bible §N, ADR or spec section that POSITIVELY requires the product's treatment; a new paragraph states that the mockup governs wherever the written rules are silent and quotes this failure as why it exists; the mockup-current paragraph now records the user's ruling that replacing the drawing is not an available disposition, allowing edits only to repair a stale or self-contradictory drawing; and the Acceptance item now reads for what a citation proves. STILL OPEN: the product surfaces are not yet brought to the drawing — that is the mockup-parity plan, scoped from the measurements in .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/. What would settle it: a parity report whose deliberate differences each cite a rule that requires them, or none. SECOND MECHANISM, SAME ROW, FOUND BY THE MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10: a plan can license its own divergence. Exactly one of the settings modal's 19 measured regions is backed by a bible section, and that section - §5's "Choice row" - was ADDED TO THE BIBLE BY THE SAME PLAN that then cited it to justify drawing palette choices as radio rows instead of the mockup's cards. Amending the written language is legitimate (the control set is closed and the plan had to name the control it added), but a section written in the same commit is evidence of what was decided, not a rule that required it, and it cannot discharge the gate. The spec's §13 amendment of 2026-10-10 carries this as well as the silence rule: only a licence that predates the divergence counts.

title: The settings modal fails the drawing on 13 of its 19 measured regions, and no ruling authorises the deviation
detail: FOUND BY A READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10 (opus), dispatched after the user reported that "even the setting panel you just built looks nothing like it" and ruled that the mockup is not replaced. EVIDENCE: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md — 19 regions compared, verdicts 13 drift / 1 mockup stale / 2 match / 2 undefined. THE LARGEST IS COMPOUND, not one property: the mockup draws the palette choice as a 3x2 grid of bordered cards each carrying TWO 16px bars (ground and accent) plus a capitalised name, under the explanation "Colors the editor, not your theme"; the product draws a 2-column grid of radio choice rows carrying ONE 14x14 chip (shell-surface with an accent inset ring), the palette's lower-case id, and no explanation at all — four drifts (columns, card-vs-row, swatch, missing copy) that the plan's difference list recorded as four separate deliberate items. Others named by the measurement include the modal's frame and inset, its 13px lead, its tab strip axis and the glass panel where the drawing is opaque. OF THE 13, EXACTLY ONE IS BACKED BY A BIBLE SECTION and that section was written by the same plan (see vg-292's second mechanism); two are outright bible VIOLATIONS rather than questions and are filed separately as vg-294 (the scrim) and vg-295 (the lead); the rest are implementation choices no section names. NO AUTHORISATION FOUND: the measurement grepped docs/decisions/, docs/architecture/, the spec's §7 and the plan, and found nothing ruling on the treatment. COLOUR, the user's other report: the drawing's palette is hand-written CSS inside the mockup with zero hits anywhere under src/web/packages, only --accent #72e0c0 agrees with the product's, every other role differs (the drawing is flat and opaque where the product is alpha glass over a gradient), and bible §4 names ROLES not values - so the bible names nothing that can break the tie and a value decision is owed. BLAST RADIUS: about 5 files (editor-shell.css, settings.tsx, settings-keyboard.tsx, ui-copy.ts, possibly control-choice-row.tsx), and three of them leak to shared surfaces - the dialog frame, its lead and the kbd chip are shared with the ? sheet (shortcut-reference.tsx) and ControlChoiceRow is shared with the control-set fixture - so this is not a modal-local edit. NOT FIXED HERE: it is the mockup-parity plan's work, and the modal's 12px radius is the SAME rule as the shell's four, so the frame is one defect with one fix (vg-231), not two. What would settle it: a capture of the settings surface placed beside the drawing's Appearance and Keyboard specimens whose remaining differences each cite a rule that requires them.

title: The drawings invent the treatment of two controls no original draws - the segmented control and the in-button chord - so a surface the product has is given a gold target that no normative source states
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 9'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), reviewing commit 5773f652 against the user's ruling that the original mockup style is the gold target while the content is corrected to the product. THE GAP: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and `shell.html` draw two surfaces that no original draws and that the bible's closed control vocabulary does not name - the segmented control (Left/Centre/Right, Top/Middle/Bottom; the product's `control-segmented.tsx`) and the chord drawn INSIDE the publish trigger (the product renders `<kbd class="editor-shell-primary-key">` as a child of the trigger at `publish-control.tsx:145`, where the original drew a standalone chip). The drawings are right that the surfaces exist - that is content, and the user's ruling puts content on the product's side - but their **treatment** is invented by extending the well idiom, and treatment is the half the user ruled is gold. CONSEQUENCE: the in-button chip's border is `#06131a59` in the drawing, about 35%, where the product composes `color-mix(currentColor 45%, transparent)` (`editor-shell.css:1304`) - a numeric drift between the drawing and the product that no `PARITY` row asserts, because no row reads either drawing today. Under spec section 13 as amended a deliberate difference must name a normative source that requires it, and there is none for a treatment nobody has ruled on. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawn treatment is what the original's author would have drawn, or the implementer's reasonable extension - the review found no original that draws either control, so the question cannot be answered from the drawings. FLAGGED AS MINOR BY THE REVIEW, and filed rather than fixed because the fix is a ruling on the treatment, not an edit. OWNED BY NO PLAN: plan 7 Task 8 makes the two control drawings read by a test (its Step 1 adds the PARITY rows), which is what would catch the drift once the treatment is settled. What would settle it: a ruling naming the treatment for a control the originals do not draw - most cheaply, the product's own composed value adopted as the drawing's, since the drawing is otherwise a copy of the product's treatment for every surface that has an original.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE PRODUCT'S COMPOSED VALUES STAND AS THE DRAWINGS' VALUES. The segmented control and the in-button chord keep the composed paint -- the chip border as color-mix(currentColor 45%) -- and the drawings are corrected where they differ, rather than a drawn value being ruled for them.

title: The drawing's view cluster draws its three zoom/fit buttons at 22px where section 5's icon button starts at 26px, so the checked drawing shows a glyph control the bible has no vocabulary for
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), reviewing `42283107` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-3-review.md` finding 3. MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:158,161,164` draw the zoom-out, zoom-in and fit buttons as `width:22px;height:22px`, while `DESIGN.md:411` defines the icon button as "A 26-30px square at `--radius-md`, glyph only" and the product's own `.editor-shell-view-step` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:2430`) is a 26px square. So the bible's only vocabulary for a glyph square starts 4px above what the drawing draws, and the drawing is the artifact the plan pulls the product to. CONSEQUENCE: this is a size divergence, not a radius one, which is why it is not Task 3's: Task 3 corrected the same three buttons' `5px` radius to `--radius-md` (`42283107`), and folding a 4px geometry change into a radius task would move the drawn cluster's width and every gap around it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawing's 22px is a deliberate compact gesture for the cluster (the drawn readout beside them is `min-width:34px`, and section 7 makes the top-right cluster wrappable) or drift from the document the cluster's own chips are drawn from. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 5's 26-30px bound is the floor for every glyph square in the drawing, and if it is, `current/shell.html:158,161,164` drawn at 26px, with whatever the cluster's own layout then needs. No parity row reads this geometry today, so nothing reddens in the meantime.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the stage's top-right cluster): MEASURED ON THE BUILT BUNDLE - the `.editor-shell-view-step` class matched three elements, each 26x26 CSS px at `border-radius: 6px` ("Zoom out", "Zoom in", "Zoom to fit"). MEASURED IN THE DRAWING, re-derived rather than taken from the row: the same top-right cluster's three glyph squares at `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:160`, `:163` and `:166` are each `width:22px;height:22px` at `border-radius: 6px`, so the row's cited `:158,161,164` are two lines early. §5's icon-button bound the row asks about ("A 26-30px square at `--radius-md`, glyph only") is `DESIGN.md:411`, inside the section whose `<!-- §5 -->` marker is `DESIGN.md:398` - both re-measured. The path the row cites, `docs/design/design-language.md`, is untracked and no longer on disk: `db000c40` (2026-10-11, "the bible is DESIGN.md, and the old file is gone") deleted it. Those are the two numbers; which side the bound binds is the row's own open question and is not answered here.

title: The derived-palette ladder is asserted as order only, so a palette whose three surface rungs collapse to steps of 0.0001 keeps its ordering and passes every assertion
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 4 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11) IN ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, reviewing `a3d2c407` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-4-review.md` finding 4. MEASURED BY READING THE ASSERTION: `design-language.spec.ts`'s derivation case compares `--bg`/`--panel`/`--panel-2` by luminance ordering (`bg < panel <= panel2`), which is what the plan's Step 5 asked for - "the luminance ordering ... matches graphite's" - and the plan's Step 3 asks for more: "takes from graphite the relationships between roles: the luminance separation". A palette whose three surfaces sit 0.0001 apart satisfies the ordering and shares nothing of the separation, so the assertion that exists to keep six transcribed value sets from drifting apart cannot see a collapse. TASK 4's FIX ROUND TIGHTENS WHAT CAN BE STATED WITHOUT INVENTING A NUMBER: strict `bg < panel < panel2` for the five derived palettes, editorial's equal `panel`/`panel-2` named as the one licensed exception. What is left is the magnitude, and that is why this is a row rather than a constant: a floor of "at least X luminance" has no rule behind it in the bible, and picking one is the move this plan has already had to undo once (the `designLanguagePx` allowlist entry added to make a gate pass, R25). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a magnitude floor is worth having at all, since a derivation is re-derived rather than edited, or whether the bible should state a minimum surface separation - section 4 gives the roles and no spacing between them. What would settle it: a bible rule naming the minimum separation between a ground and the panel above it, and then an assertion reading it. PLAN 7 TASK 6 SEARCHED FOR THE RULE AND FOUND NONE (2026-10-11). Read, and this is the search rather than the conclusion: section 3 (`design-language.md:64-109`, the spacing, radius and elevation tables) states no surface separation; section 4 (`:111-140`, the role table) gives the roles and no relationship between `--bg`, `--panel` and `--panel-2`; section 5 (`:141-206`) gives contrast ratios only (3:1, 4.5:1), which bind a boundary against its ground rather than the distance between two grounds; the drawing (`current/shell.html:17-18`) declares three literals with no stated relationship. No constant was added and this row stays open, because a magnitude floor with no rule behind it is the `designLanguagePx` move (R25) this plan has already had to undo once.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `design-language.spec.ts`, and the magnitudes are read off the live `:root` custom properties resolved through an element): the ordering case passes (`graphite's roles are the drawing's, and the other five keep its ladder`, 3404ms), and the magnitude the row asks about, measured as WCAG relative luminance, spans 40x across the five palettes that can be measured. panel minus bg / panel2 minus panel, with the three luminances: graphite 0.0036 / 0.0035 (L 0.0043, 0.0079, 0.0113); ember 0.1454 / 0.0581 (0.6428, 0.7882, 0.8463); moss 0.1307 / 0.0680 (0.7016, 0.8324, 0.9003); plum 0.1438 / 0.0652 (0.6511, 0.7949, 0.8601); editorial 0.1008 / 0.0000 (0.8815, 0.9823, 0.9823 - the licensed equal pair). light's `--bg` is `linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)` and has no single luminance, so its bg rung is unmeasured here rather than estimated; its declared surfaces are `#eff9f2bf` and `#f8fffbdf`, both carrying alpha. A magnitude floor would bind graphite first: a threshold above 0.0036 reds it.

title: light is the one palette whose chrome is still translucent, so "chrome is opaque" holds in five of six palettes and light composites against a gradient ground
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while making the chrome opaque, and reported to the controller as the brief asked rather than settled here: "where a palette's chrome has no derivation to read that is a finding for me, not a literal invented here". MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER after the change, reading `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` on `.editor-shell-rail`: editorial `rgb(255,253,247)`, graphite `rgb(18,22,28)`, ember `rgb(247,226,210)`, moss `rgb(228,239,217)`, plum `rgb(236,227,247)` - all opaque - and light `rgba(239,249,242,0.75)`. CAUSE ESTABLISHED: `.editor-glass` now paints the palette's own `var(--panel)`, and light is the only palette whose surface roles carry alpha at all - `--shell-surface: #eff9f2bf` and `--shell-surface-strong: #f8fffbdf` - while its `--shell-backdrop` is the set's only gradient, so no role light declares is an opaque surface and plan 7 Task 4's derivation (graphite's relationships: the luminance ladder, the edge's weight against its surface) produces none. It is not expressible in CSS either: deriving the composite needs `color-mix` over `--shell-backdrop`, which is a gradient and is invalid inside `color-mix`. CONSEQUENCE: the rail, both panes, the inspector and the header each composite 25% of the mint gradient behind them, so light's chrome contrast is not one composited value and its boundary ratio (measured 1.40:1, `vg-200`'s pin) moves with the ground. The treatment assertion in `shell-appearance.spec.ts` names light as its one exemption and reads the translucency it carries, so a value that lands reds the gate and the exemption has to be deleted rather than left to excuse a regression. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: choosing an opaque light surface is a palette value decision, and the task that owns the derivation is the one that should make it.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174; the venue is `shell-appearance.spec.ts`, and the surfaces are `.editor-shell-rail`'s computed background per palette): five rails are opaque - editorial rgb(255, 253, 247), graphite rgb(18, 22, 28), ember rgb(247, 226, 210), moss rgb(228, 239, 217), plum rgb(236, 227, 247) - and light is rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75), the field the browser reports for the declared `#eff9f2bf` surface, over the set's only gradient ground (light `--bg` = linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)). No value moved. The treatment case is green in the same run (`chrome is flat and opaque, and the canvas clusters keep the glass`, 11894ms).

title: `--shell-flat` is declared in two palette blocks and consumed by nothing, so the file carries a token whose only reader is a name list in a test
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11), which reported it as an observation rather than filing it. MEASURED: `--shell-flat` is declared at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:45` (editorial, `1`) and `:136` (graphite, `0`), and a sweep of `packages/editor/src` finds no consumer - no `var(--shell-flat)`, no `@media`, no rule keyed on it - while `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:238` names it only inside `NOT_A_COLOUR`, a list of tokens that are not colours. After Task 5 the token is more plainly metadata: it was never what chose the flat treatment, which the palette selectors decide. CONSEQUENCE: a declared-but-unread token reads as a live knob and is not one, so anyone changing it sees no effect and no test fails. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether it was declared ahead of a consumer on purpose - ADR 0040 records `--stage`, `--hdr` and `--edge-2` as the three roles declared ahead of their first consumers on the user's instruction, and `--shell-flat` is not among them, but the same pattern would look identical. What would settle it: a ruling on whether a per-palette flat flag is wanted at all (the treatment is selector-driven today), and if not, the two declarations and the `NOT_A_COLOUR` entry deleted in one commit.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller as a code/architecture correctness question: THE TOKEN GOES. --shell-flat's two declarations (editor-shell.css:149, :259) and its NOT_A_COLOUR entry (editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:398, with the prose at :78) are deleted in one commit. It is not one of ADR-0040's three roles declared ahead of a consumer on the user's instruction -- those are named and this is not among them -- and the flat treatment is selector-driven after Task 5, so a per-palette flag no var() reads is a knob that lies: changing it moves nothing and fails nothing. COST IF WRONG: a future per-palette flat flag is a one-line declaration plus its consumer, which is what the pattern would need anyway.

title: `current/shell.html` draws no Add-pane asset preview, so the surface the product renders at `file-section.tsx:189` is one no gate can check
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `7efea17f`) and adjudicated by its task review rather than left as the implementer's observation. MEASURED: `current/shell.html:128-140` draws the Add pane's Asset group as a select, then `Import a file`, then Replace/Remove, and a case-insensitive search for `preview` in that file returns nothing, while the product renders an `img.vigilia-asset-preview` carrying `data-vigilia-asset-preview` at `panes/add/file-section.tsx:189-194`, styled at `editor-shell.css:1107`, and both `editor-shell-add-desktop-chromium.png` and `pane-add-desktop-chromium.png` show it. DISPOSITION: `drawing-stale`, not `fix` - pulling the product to the drawing would delete a real capability (the thumbnail and its hidden-when-unpreviewable rule), spec section 13.1 does not let a visual difference waive a required capability, and Task 9's own rule sends a capability the product has and the drawing lacks into the drawing, because a gate cannot check a surface the drawing never draws. The frozen original `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` stays as it is; the repair belongs to `current/shell.html` and was in flight as Task 7's fix round 1 when this row was filed. CONSEQUENCE UNTIL IT LANDS: the plan's own completion condition (section 13: every difference fixed or backed by a cited rule) is not met, and the Asset group is the least-comparable region besides, because the 1280x720 capture clips `Import a file`, `Replace asset` and `Remove asset` below the fold where the 1180x1040 drawing shows them. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the repair should be paired with a reader row, since that needs machinery the parity table does not have today. THE DRAWING HALF IS DISCHARGED (2026-10-11, artefact 221bf1a1, Task 7 fix round 1): `current/shell.html` now draws the preview well between the Asset select and the `Import a file` row, in the drawing's own idiom, with the class it stands for named in a comment beside it - `height:120px;aspect-ratio:1672/941` taken from a live measurement of `[data-vigilia-asset-preview]` on the built bundle (213.3x120 at the pane content's left edge, flush under the select), and a gradient standing in for the chosen picture. The frozen original is untouched and nothing was renumbered. The parity table re-ran green with the drawing changed and no row's answer moved (9 passed at `--workers=1`, re-run by the controller against `design-language.spec.ts` rather than taken from the report). WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN: the title's second clause is untouched - a surface the drawing omits is still one no gate can check. No reader row was built, and the reason is measured rather than laziness: the product's contract is `max-height:120px` with `object-fit:contain`, a bound and not a size, and the Add pane is `display:none` while Document is open, so a row would read no element. This class - a drawing that omits a surface the product renders - needs a surface-inventory check and belongs to `vg-304`'s family; the row stays open as that family's member rather than closing on the half that was repaired. REOPENED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN, on review: a close in this task was reverted rather than defended. THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS AND IS GREEN, AND IT STILL CANNOT CARRY A `verified`. What it proves: the surface this row names is named on all three sides — the component that renders it (`img.vigilia-asset-preview` carrying `data-vigilia-asset-preview`), the `editor-shell.css` rule that treats it, and `current/shell.html`, which draws the box beside the name. What it cannot prove, and this IS the class the row exists for: the list of surfaces it reads is HAND-WRITTEN AND ONE ENTRY LONG, so a product surface that is not on the list reddens nothing — the instrument re-asserts the one surface already found and cannot discover the next. AND THE DRAWING SIDE READS A NAME, NOT A DRAWN ELEMENT: the drawn box at `current/shell.html:134` is an anonymous inline-styled div with no class and no hook, so that side is satisfied by the `<!-- asset preview (.vigilia-asset-preview) ... -->` comment at `:133` — delete the drawn box and leave the comment and the instrument stays green. DERIVING THE SET FROM THE PRODUCT WAS MEASURED AND DOES NOT CONSTRUCT: the panes render 73 distinct `data-vigilia-*` hooks, 5 of them named anywhere in `editor-shell.css`, and NO checked drawing names any of them — the drawings are hand-authored HTML that names a product surface by its class, in prose beside the box, never by a hook on a drawn element. Measured 2026-10-12 by walking `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/**/*.tsx` and testing each hook against the stylesheet and the six checked drawings; a derivation that required the drawing to name every hook would red the suite at 73 entries — or at 5, scoped to the hooks the stylesheet names — with no way to satisfy any of them. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an enumeration of the product's surfaces that the drawings can be held to — either the drawings gain a mechanical way to name a product surface, or a product-side registry of surfaces exists for the drawings to be checked against. The §8.11 path correction and the §8.2 line correction recorded above still stand and are unaffected: the surface is `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/add/file-section.tsx:192-193`, and the `.vigilia-asset-preview` rule is `editor-shell.css:1229`.

title: Shipped source cites a plan's git-ignored execution state, so the citation points at a file no clone has
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `0c6a17c0`). MEASURED: `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:494` introduces the `PARITY` table with "The shell's regions, as the census adjudicates them (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md`)" - a path inside `.superpowers/sdd/`, which the repo's own plan README (`docs/superpowers/plans/README.md:7`) calls "ignored execution state", and which the subagent-driven-development skill deletes when a plan's final review comes back clean. So the citation names a file no clone has, and the census it points at (the region-by-region adjudication every `PARITY` row's licence and disposition comes from) has no durable home. THE CONVENTION IS ALREADY IN USE IN TRACKED DOCS, which is why this is a question rather than a one-line fix: `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md:123`, `docs/decisions/0003-authored-text-box-outlives-the-text.md:186` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:605` each cite a different `.superpowers/sdd/` workspace the same way, and `docs/decisions/0003` is an accepted ADR, so the pattern predates this file. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the right answer is to keep the workspace (the plan's evidence then outlives the plan, at the cost of a git-ignored directory nothing prunes), to move a census worth keeping under `docs/evidence/` when the plan closes, or to treat the citation as provenance that a reader is expected to reconstruct from the archived plan plus the register. The third is the cheapest and is what the other three sites already rely on; the second is the only one that makes the claim checkable. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a user ruling on where a closed plan's evidence lives, since this decides whether the census a parity gate argues from is reviewable by anyone but the session that wrote it. Owned by whoever closes the next plan, not by plan 7, which is closed.

title: The settings modal's Close button is `--shell-text` on `--vigilia-control-bg` where the drawing draws `--muted` on `--panel2`, and no plan-8 task owns it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 1 (2026-10-11, census row #19, filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `9a6667ac`). MEASURED: the re-adjudication of the closed plan's region #19 - the drawing at `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` draws the modal's Close control in `--muted` on `--panel2`, and the product renders it in `--shell-text` on `--vigilia-control-bg`. The census classifies it `fix` - no predating rule requires the product's treatment - but no task in plan 8's ten touches the control, so it is filed here rather than folded into a task it does not belong to. WHY IT IS NOT IN PLAN 8: the plan's tasks were written from the measurement's own region list, and region #19 moved when the drawing did - the measurement's row read `undefined`, because the superseded `editor-shell.html` drew no Close control at all, and the current set does. So the row is new evidence the plan could not have scheduled, and adding a task for it now would put an unscheduled edit in a plan whose phases are already dispatched. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §4 colour-role correction on the Close control's rule in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, with plan 8 Task 1's settings row (or a fifth row) reading `--muted` against `--panel2`, and the §13 capture in Task 10 showing it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the product's treatment is deliberate - the control is a `ControlButton` and `--vigilia-control-bg` may be the control set's own resting fill rather than a second declaration of the same value. If it is the control set's, the fix is the control's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is why this is a row and not a one-line change. SECOND INSTANCE - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's return-to-default actions render the same fill against the same drawn treatment. The drawing draws `border:1px solid var(--edge);border-radius:6px;background:var(--panel2);color:var(--muted)` on every one of them (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:50`, `:61`, `:70`, `:79`, `:92`, `:101`, `:110`, `:119`, `:128`) while `.editor-shell-keyboard-action` renders `background: var(--vigilia-control-bg)` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1586-1594`), so the class is the Close button plus these - and the text colour is NOT part of this instance, because the product's `--shell-muted` is the drawing's `var(--muted)` renamed. Task 7 reported it rather than fixing it, because the fill belongs to the control set's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is what this row already says. The correction belongs to that one owner, not to three edits.
