PLAN 8 TASK 10 RE-CONFIRMED THIS ROW'S FIRST INSTANCE AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (2026-10-11, commit b78ee264): the Close renders --shell-text on --vigilia-control-bg, left-aligned, padding 6px 12px, margin-top 18px (`editor-shell.css:1397-1416`) where `current/settings.html` draws --muted on --panel2, right-aligned, padding 4px 12px, margin-top 16px - and no section names this control's fill or text colour, so it is a fix with no predating licence. Its 18px is also one of the four vg-325 values Task 9's ceiling counts by name, and the left alignment is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the reading is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, in force palette light. The settings modal's Close renders color rgb(16, 33, 25) (--shell-text) on background rgb(245, 241, 232) (--vigilia-control-bg), margin-top 16px, padding 6px 12px; the Keyboard tab's return-to-default actions, 21 of them, render rgb(79, 102, 89) (--shell-muted) on the same fill. The drawing's roles resolve to --shell-muted #4f6659 on --panel-2 #f8fffbdf, so the fill is the divergence and the text colour is not, exactly as this row says. Two citations on this line corrected, and one number: .editor-shell-dialog > button is at editor-shell.css:1502, not :1397-1416; .editor-shell-keyboard-action is at :1694, not :1586-1594; and its margin-top is 16px today, not the 18px this line records — the drawing's own value, so that half of the divergence is already gone. STAYS OPEN, and the one-token fix is deliberately NOT taken: --vigilia-control-bg is declared on five rules across six palettes, and design-language.spec.ts:2045-2050 names it as the separation editorial carries in place of its panel rung, so repainting it is a design decision about the control set rather than a fixer's edit. RECORD CORRECTED AND THE OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED, 2026-10-13, measured on the tree at ec1e39e7; no product file changed. (1) THE LAST LINE OF TASK 2.4b IS FALSE OF THIS ROW'S FIRST INSTANCE. 'the fill is the divergence and the text colour is not' holds for the Keyboard instance and not for the Close: the same sentence measures the Close's label at rgb(16, 33, 25) (`--shell-text`) where the drawing draws `--muted`, which resolves to the product's `--shell-muted` #4f6659, and this row's own title says the same. So the Close carries three divergent properties, not one - the fill, the colour, and a padding the rule states as `6px 12px` (`editor-shell.css:1589`) against the drawing's 4px 12px - and a fixer reading that line alone would repaint the fill and leave two. (2) 'NOT ESTABLISHED' IS NOW ESTABLISHED, AND ON THE SIDE THE ROW WARNED ABOUT. `--vigilia-control-bg` IS the control set's own resting fill rather than a second declaration of `--panel-2`: seven palette declarations (`editor-shell.css:106`, `:153`, `:204`, `:275`, `:325`, `:355`, `:385`) and five consuming rule-blocks, every one of them in that single file - the panel's asset buttons (`:1317`), the layer rename (`:1332`), the inspector's action block (`:1353`), the dialog's button (`:1587`) and the keyboard action (`:1782`). It is not one of section 4's roles, and its value differs from the named role's in the palette the drawing actually compares: light declares control-bg #f5f1e8 where its `--panel-2` is #f8fffbdf. So the divergence is systemic across the control set rather than a Close-button slip. (3) THE CLOSE PATH THIS ROW STATES ('a section 4 colour-role correction') IS NOT AVAILABLE AS WRITTEN, because DESIGN.md gives a labelled button no fill to correct to. Section 4's role table names `--panel-2` as 'A panel, and a control inside it'; every filled control in section 5's vocabulary is `--panel-2` (Well, Segmented, Choice row); and section 5's list, whose own first line is 'The vocabulary is closed', holds no labelled button - so a button is not a control in the language's own words. The only text about buttons anywhere in DESIGN.md is about the primary one: `button` occurs at `:110` ('the primary button', in the accent rationing), `:150` ('650-700 only for the brand mark and a primary button') and `:203` ('`Publish` is the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor'), and none of the three defines a secondary button's shape. `:203`'s strict reading - no other button is filled - would make both the drawing's fill and the product's wrong, so the two sides of this difference are not a colour-role disagreement at all. The gap is filed as `vg-441`. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, REVISED: a decision in DESIGN.md on the secondary button's shape before any edit to the five rule-blocks - section 5 gaining the control, or `:203`'s 'only filled' standing with every labelled button becoming unfilled - with the Close's colour and padding following that decision. NEAR ROWS: `vg-441` (the vocabulary gap that makes this row undecidable), `vg-322` (item 16's other difference, blocked on the parked `vg-330`), `vg-436` (the same width-vs-rule trap in the drawings' own pair).

title: The dialog's shared `h3` and read-only `dl` rules resolve no bible role: a group heading is `--text-xs` where §2 gives the eyebrow `--text-2xs`, the row pads 3px where §3's steps have no 3, and §5 rule 2's 74px label column is drawn by neither side
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 4'S REVIEW (2026-10-11, findings F1 and F4, `task-4-review.md`) and NOT carried by its commit - `6ca510ce` has no `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer, so it is materialised from the review instead, which is why the provenance names a finding number rather than a message. THE THREE FACTS, each measured at the line it rests on. ONE, the group heading: `.editor-shell-dialog h3` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1353-1357`) is `font-size: 11px` with `letter-spacing: 0.12em`, while §2 (`docs/design/design-language.md:47`) gives the eyebrow role `--text-2xs` 10px and `:55-57` fixes an eyebrow at `--text-2xs`, `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`, muted, 'always labels a region, never a control' - 11px is `--text-xs`, whose role at `:48` is 'Panel rows, hints, status bar'. Task 4's drawing is right and the product is wrong: `current/settings-keyboard.html:54` draws `font:600 10px/1.2 ...;letter-spacing:.11em`. TWO, the read-only row's inset: `.editor-shell-dialog dl > div` (`editor-shell.css:1368`) is `padding: 3px 0`, and §3's steps (`design-language.md:69`) are `4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32` - there is no 3. The drawing takes 4px (`current/settings-about.html:50`). THREE, §5 rule 2's grid: the rule (`:163-165`) says read-only rows 'share the grid with controls so a section does not jump between shapes' and that 'the grid is a 74px label column and one value cell', while the product's rule is `justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px` with a content-sized label and the drawing copied that shape - so the column is implemented by neither side. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: all three live on two shared element rules, and those rules are rendered by three surfaces across two dialogs - `settings-keyboard.tsx:153-154`, `settings.tsx:146` and `:214`, `shortcut-reference.tsx:39-40` - so a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings wrong, which is the defect Task 3 already fixed once at its owner. WHY NO ROW READS ANY OF IT TODAY: the parity table's About and Keyboard rows read the panels' own declared properties and pass, and plan 8 Task 8's widened gate reads the DRAWINGS' literals, not the product's - so the three facts are invisible to every gate in the repo. THE 74px HALF IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION rather than a value: whether §5 rule 2 binds a dialog's read-only `dl`, or whether the shared grid is the control rows' alone, decides whether the About panel's rows must take a column the Appearance panel also uses. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 role on the `h3` rule, a §3 step on the `dl` row's inset, a ruling on the grid question, and a parity row that reads each - with the §13 capture in Task 10 showing the result. RELATED, NOT THE SAME: `vg-317` is the dialog body's UNDECLARED 13px base, `vg-295` (verified) was the class one level up - the dialog's lead - and `vg-302` (verified) is the same 74px column on CONTROL rows, which plan 7 Task 8 landed as `ControlRow`'s `column`/`boxed`/`headed` shapes; this row is the READ-ONLY row's half, which that one did not cover. SECOND MEASUREMENT - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's group heading is this same shared rule, and the divergence is two properties with one cause. The drawing declares `font:600 10px/1.2 system-ui;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:54`) and `.editor-shell-dialog h3` renders `font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1367-1372`), which is section 2's eyebrow rule (`design-language.md:55-57` - `--text-2xs` at 10px, weight `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`) read one step and one thousandth off. CORRECTED BY TASK 7'S REVIEW (2026-10-11): the first version of this sentence gave the wrong reason - that sharing puts it out of reach, 'the same reasoning that scoped the chord chip'. Those are opposite moves. Scoping the chip fixed the panel WITHOUT touching the sheet, and a `.editor-shell-keyboard h3` scope would fix this panel's eyebrows without touching the sheet either, so sharing is not what puts the value out of reach. The reason is OWNERSHIP: a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings off section 2, splitting one concept across two owners, so the fix belongs at the shared rule's owner, which is where this row already puts it. The divergence is live and correctly deferred either way; what was wrong was the reason, because a later reader could have reused it to defer something genuinely in scope. The Keyboard panel alone is off section 2 on twenty eyebrows until the shared rule moves. This is evidence for the row, not a second row. A THIRD INSTANCE, MEASURED BY PLAN 8 TASK 10 AND FILED AS ITS TRAILER IN b78ee264 (2026-10-11): the Appearance drawing's own heading is `font:600 12px/1` sentence case (`current/settings.html:42`) where the Keyboard drawing draws its group headings at `font:600 10px/1.2;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`current/settings-keyboard.html:54` and four siblings), and the product renders both through the shared `.editor-shell-dialog h3` at 11px / .12em uppercase - so the DRAWING side does not hold the treatment section 2 reserves for a section eyebrow either, and the two sides are wrong in opposite directions. The eyebrow rule is `design-language.md:54` (a first pass cited `:56`, which is the middle of the sentence). Task 4 and Task 7 reported the product side identically. READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the portalled `.editor-shell-dialog`): all three facts measure on the built bundle, and the sheet the row predicted they reach is the third surface. ONE - the shared `h3`: the Appearance group heading ("Shell palette") computes to font-size 11px, letter-spacing 1.32px (0.12em), uppercase, weight 400, against §2's eyebrow (--text-2xs, 10px, .11em, weight 600). TWO - the read-only row: the About tab's `dl > div` computes to `padding: 3px 0px`, a value with no §3 step. THREE - the grid: that row's `justify-content: space-between` and `gap: 16px` show no 74px label column. `closest(".editor-shell")` on the dialog is null - it is portalled. The `?` sheet takes the same two shared rules in the places that were read: all five of its group headings ("File", "Edit", "Canvas", "Publish", "Help") compute to 11px / 1.32px, and of the 20 `dl > div` rows it holds, the one read takes `padding: 3px 0px`. So a per-surface patch leaves the sheet wrong, which is the row's ownership argument measured at those two rules. CITATIONS REFRESHED WITHOUT REWRITING THEM, 2026-10-13. Every `docs/design/design-language.md` line above was measured against the bible, which has since been replaced -- the file no longer exists and its `§N` markers now live in `DESIGN.md` (`AGENTS.md` holds `§N` stable). The current equivalents, verified 2026-10-13: `§2`'s eyebrow role at `DESIGN.md:145`, `§3`'s steps at `:177`, and `§5` rule 2's read-only rows and its 74px grid at `:423` and `:425`. **The historical numbers are left as written rather than repointed**, because a citation records where a rule stood when it was read, and editing it onto a path that did not exist then would assert a reading nobody took -- the same ruling this drain applied to the dated snapshots under `docs/architecture/`. **FACT TWO IS FIXED, 2026-10-13.** `.editor-shell-dialog dl > div`'s `padding: 3px 0` became `4px 0` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, and its now-dead entry was removed from `CEILINGS` in `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` in the same change -- the instrument reddens on an exemption that matches nothing, so the value and its licence move together. The drawing already took 4 (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-about.html:50`) and `§3` has no 3, so this is a substitution rather than a design pass; the parity row that reads this element (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:1376`) asserts its `gap`, not its padding, so nothing pinned the old value. Measured after: `npm run design:check` exits **0**, `counted: 0`, `dead: 0`. **FACTS ONE AND THREE REMAIN OPEN, each on a design decision rather than a value.** The group heading's shared `h3` is off `§2` in one direction while the Appearance drawing is off it in the other -- 10px uppercase against 12px sentence case -- so no single shared rule can satisfy both; and `§5` rule 2's 74px column is implemented by neither side. Both were measured on the built bundle in this row's 2026-10-12 reading, and neither is a fixer's edit. FACT ONE'S OTHER SIDE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: the row rests on `settings-keyboard.html` drawing the group heading at `font:600 10px/1.2` with `letter-spacing:.11em` (five of them) and calls the product wrong. **The other settings sheet draws a different heading, so the conflict is between the drawings and not between one drawing and the product.** `settings.html:42` draws the panel's own group heading as `
Shell palette
` -- 12px, sentence case, no tracking, no uppercase -- over the same palette grid this row's sheet would head at 10px. The seven `font-size:11px` declarations in the same file are the palette cards' captions and the system-follow row (`:50`, `:57`, `:64`, `:71`, `:78`, `:85`, `:90`), not headings, so 12px is the sheet's only heading size. **So the choice is a drawing's, not a fixer's**, which is what keeps this fact open: whichever sheet wins decides whether the product's `11px` moves to `--text-2xs` 10px (the keyboard sheet and section 2's eyebrow) or to `--text-sm` 12px sentence case (the settings sheet, which would also drop the uppercase and the tracking the product currently has at `letter-spacing: 0.12em`). Both are single-rule edits and they are different edits. **Also recorded because it narrows the fact-3 question beside it**: no drawing implements section 5 rule 2's 74px label column, which that fact already says, and this measurement adds that the two sheets agree on the read-only row's shape (`padding:4px 0`, `justify-content:space-between;gap:16px`) while disagreeing on the heading above it -- so the grid question and the heading question are independent and neither is settled by the other. WHAT THE NORM SAYS ABOUT FACT ONE, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHY THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN TWO DRAWINGS. DESIGN.md section 2 reserves uppercase rather than describing it - 'Uppercase is reserved for **section eyebrows** - Content, Position, Layer, Paint, Spends, and the group headings in the Add pane' - and adds 'Nothing else is uppercase: a chord is printed as the platform prints it, and a menu row is sentence case'. Section 7.3 is the only other place the role is granted: a pane's body, where 'Sections use the section 2 eyebrow'. Every surface named is a shell surface, and no normative source gives a dialog's group heading the eyebrow role. The product renders `.editor-shell-dialog h3` uppercase at 11px with `letter-spacing: 0.12em` and weight 400, which is neither the eyebrow section 2 defines (10px, 600, .11em) nor sentence case - so it resolves no section 2 role whichever way this fact is read. THE CHAIN, STATED SO IT CAN BE ATTACKED AT ONE LINK: if section 2's list is the reservation it says it is, a dialog heading may not be uppercase, `current/settings.html:42`'s 12px / 600 sentence case is the drawn treatment that survives, and `current/settings-keyboard.html:54`'s uppercase heading is the stale side - the same shape as `vg-440`, a drawing losing to the written rule. The fix is then one rule at `.editor-shell-dialog h3`'s owner: `font-size: var(--text-sm)`, weight `600`, tracking and `text-transform` dropped, reaching the settings modal and the `?` sheet together. WHAT SETTLES IT: one sentence confirming that reservation, or a section 2 or section 7 clause granting a dialog's group heading the eyebrow role - in which case the product's 11px / .12em / 400 becomes 10px / 600 / .11em and the keyboard sheet is the right one. Both are one rule; they are different rules, which is why this is a ruling and not a fixer's edit. FACT THREE'S SENTENCE, FOUND 2026-10-13, AND THE READING IT SUPPORTS. Section 5 rule 2 does not stop at the 74px column; it ends with an escape: 'A row a surface's own drawing shapes differently - a switch row whose label fills the row inside a panel box, a control spanning the row under its own heading - is not a field row and keeps the shape it is drawn with.' Both settings sheets draw the read-only row as `justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px`, which this row's own 2026-10-13 measurement confirms, so if that clause reaches this row then it is not a field row, the 74px column does not bind it, the product's copy of the drawing is right, and fact three is not a defect at all - it is a rule whose own escape clause covers the case. THE COUNTER-READING, STATED SO IT IS NOT HIDDEN: the clause's two examples are shapes a drawing invents, a switch row inside a panel box and a control spanning the row under its own heading, where this is a label-and-value row that a drawing aligns differently, and rule 2's grid is plausibly exactly what a read-only row is for. Which one is meant is a sentence from the same owner fact one waits on, and the two facts are independent: confirming the escape clause does not decide the heading, and confirming section 2's reservation does not decide the grid.

title: The settings drawing's frame is a fixed 560px while the modal is content-sized, so it measures 405px on Appearance and every drawn region inside it renders half-size — and no row reads a drawing's frame width
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 5 (2026-10-11, as the third `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `411dbe91`). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:20` draws the modal's frame at `width:560px` fixed, while the product's `.editor-shell-dialog` is `min-width:340px; max-width:560px` and content-sized (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1311-1312`), so Task 5's report measures it at 405px on the Appearance tab, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: the palette cards render about 58px wide against the drawing's about 120px, so the grid is the drawing's three columns while each card is half the drawn width and the drawn proportions are not reproduced anywhere in the modal. WHY NO GATE SEES IT: the one row on the frame reads its `border-radius`, and no row reads a drawing's width - the same gap `vg-292` names for another geometry and `vg-320` names for a drawing's value. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: it is the frame's geometry rather than the palette group's, and Task 5's outcome is the group; the plan's ten tasks name no frame width, and the three panels' content differs (Keyboard is already 507px), so taking the drawing's fixed width is a ruling about the modal rather than an edit inside it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the modal should take the drawing's 560px, or a width per panel, or whether a content-sized modal is right and the drawing is the stale one - the drawing's `width:560px` may simply be how a static drawing is authored rather than a property the product must match. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: that ruling, plus a row that reads the frame's width so the next divergence is visible. IT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE GLASS OR THE RADIUS: the modal's frame radius is a green row and stays green. PLAN 8 TASK 10 MEASURED THE PRODUCT SIDE, WHICH THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE (2026-10-11, b78ee264): the modal is content-sized today at 405px on Appearance, 507px on Keyboard and 393px on About, against the drawing's fixed `width:560px`; the Appearance pane's palette cards therefore render about 58px wide where the drawing draws about 120px, and the difference is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing. NO PREDATING RULE NAMES A DIALOG'S WIDTH: section 3's table is spacing, and the bible's two dialog rules are the title's type (section 2) and the scrim (section 3), so this is not licensed and stays open. REJECTED RATHER THAN ANSWERED, BY THE USER (2026-10-11), and this is the larger finding: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' The question was whether the modal takes the drawing's fixed 560px; the answer is that there should be no modal to measure, so this row's width question and the 405/507/393px measurements are about a container that is going away. Filed forward as `vg-330`, which owns the change and the drawing redraw. This row stays open only so the measurement is not lost; it closes when `vg-330` does.

title: No drawing in the checked set draws the `?` shortcut sheet, so one modal surface is outside the acceptance instrument and two plan-8 rulings leaned on that absence
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11, while scoping the chord chip). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six drawings - `controls.html`, `controls-light.html`, `settings.html`, `settings-keyboard.html`, `settings-about.html`, `shell.html` - and **not one of them draws or mentions the shortcut reference sheet**. `settings-keyboard.html` contains the word 'shortcut' because it is the Keyboard panel's own drawing; a search for the reference itself ('shortcut reference') matches nothing in the directory. The sheet is not a fringe surface: `shortcut-reference.tsx:36-45` renders `h2.editor-shell-dialog-lead`, one `section` per group and a `kbd` per row directly into the dialog, so it is the second consumer of the modal's shared rules and it is on the keyboard-only walkthrough (spec `:516-521`, 'open and close a popup', 'cancel shortcut capture'). TWO RULINGS LEANED ON THIS ABSENCE, both soundly: Task 7 scoped the chord chip to `.editor-shell-keyboard kbd` rather than moving the shared `.editor-shell-dialog kbd`, because moving it would move a surface no drawing governs; and `vg-319` defers the shared `h3` eyebrow for the same reason. Neither ruling is wrong - the point is that the instrument's hole became load-bearing twice without being named. WHY IT MATTERS: the sheet has behaviour proof (`vg-284` names what that proof misses) and no treatment comparator at all, so every pixel of it is unmeasured against the gold target - the same shape as `vg-314`, which names the Add pane's asset preview as a surface no gate can check. Spec `:506-507` is explicit that a visual difference cannot waive keyboard access or contrast, and those are exactly the properties a drawing is the instrument for. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a drawing of the sheet in `current/`, in Task 4's pattern for the Keyboard and About panels - or a ruling that the sheet's treatment is wholly inherited from the modal's drawing and needs a comparator of its own nowhere. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of those two is right, and whether the sheet is in scope for the drawing set at all - the plan's Out of scope assigns the shell and its clusters to plan 7 and says nothing about the sheet.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the `?` sheet opened by the shell's own dispatcher): the hole is still there and the sheet is live. Pressing `?` opens a portalled `.editor-shell-dialog` labelled "Keyboard shortcuts" carrying `h2.editor-shell-dialog-lead`, 5 group `h3`s, 20 `dl > div` rows and 20 `kbd`s - the modal's shared rules' second consumer, as the row says. It is compared against nothing: `docs/design/mockups/current/` holds six HTML drawings (controls, controls-light, settings, settings-keyboard, settings-about, shell), a grep for "shortcut reference" matches none of them, and "Keyboard shortcuts" matches only `settings-keyboard.html:244`, which draws the binding that OPENS the sheet rather than the sheet.

title: Section 3's row-density rhythm is read by no gate: the drawings gate holds spacing to the step list and never to the 26/30/32 rule, which is where 75 corrected well insets would have shown
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8'S REVIEW (2026-10-11). MEASURED: section 3's density rule (`docs/design/design-language.md:82-84`) gives the row rhythm 26, 30 and 32 - values that are deliberately NOT on the spacing step list at `:69` - and Task 8's widened drawings gate holds a spacing declaration to the step list alone, so a row drawn at the wrong density passes as long as its padding is a step. The scale where it would show: the 75 `5px -> 4px` well insets, because `control-well.tsx:52-56` pins `h-[26px]` in the product while the drawing expresses the same row through padding, so the drawn well height is font-metric-dependent - the `font` shorthand the drawings use sets no line-height - and the two sides can disagree with neither gate nor report examining it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawings and the product actually disagree on any row's height - the review that found this did NOT claim a break, only that nothing examines it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: either a rule that the density values are outside the spacing arm's reach with a reason, or an arm that reads them (which needs a rendered height rather than a declaration, so it is a different kind of check from everything else in this gate). IT IS NOT vg-320, which is a drawing measured against the frozen original; this is a drawing measured against a written rule no arm reads. STILL OPEN AFTER TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (2026-10-12). The arm the row wants was attempted and not landed, and the reason is a measurement rather than a shortage of effort: §3's row rhythm is 26/30/32 and the product expresses it through `ControlWell`'s `WELL_HEIGHT`/`ROW_MIN_HEIGHT` density tables, but **no caller in the workspace passes `density="dialog"` or `density="settings"`** — every call site takes the default — so nothing renders at 30px for an arm to read, and a rendered arm built on the densities that do render would assert one number three times, which is the shape `vg-233`'s first pass closed on and the review refused. What the run established: the drawings gate is green over all six checked drawings with the field row at 26px in a panel reading its rhythm, and the deliberate decision §3 makes (26/30/32 are densities, not gutters, and are `design-tokens.mjs`'s `SPACING_PROPERTY` comment's reason for excluding them from the step list) still holds. What would close it: a rendered arm with a comparator for a surface's density, which needs at least one surface to render at the dialog density first. ONE CLAUSE CORRECTED 2026-10-13. This row reads the drawings' `font` shorthand as setting no line-height, which is true of the element rules and not of the files: the page furniture does state one - `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, inherited by every drawn element - so a drawn row is not metric-dependent at the inherited ratio, only where an element overrides the size and keeps it. The ratio itself is off section 2's scale and is filed as `vg-440`; this row's subject, section 3's density rule (26/30/32) and the well-height disagreement it hides, is unchanged.

title: Settings is a modal today and the user has ruled it should be a pane like Add and Composition, opened from the rail's gear, with the settings drawing redrawn as a panel
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), reading the current mockup capture, in answer to the modal width question this round put to them: 'Setting should not be a modal but a panel like add, composition.' Three further sub-rulings came with it, each asked with a recommendation and each answered as recommended. (1) HOW IT OPENS: the rail keeps its FOUR slots -- Composition, Add, Tokens, Document -- and the gear opens Settings as a pane in the same area, exactly like Add and Composition; the pane's own header then names the surface, which is also this round's answer to `vg-328` (one name). A fifth rail slot was offered and declined: it would change the drawing's 46px rail and leave the gear redundant with the slot, which is two controls opening one surface. (2) THE DRAWING: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` is REDRAWN without the scrim and the modal frame, as a pane at the shell's pane width. The user was told this edits the gold artefact and chose it anyway, because they had ruled the drawing is the acceptance instrument and a panel that is not drawn as a panel cannot be compared against anything -- Task 9's parity item could not be met for Settings at all. (3) SEQUENCING: after plan 6, not now. WHY IT IS A SPEC AND NOT A TASK: it touches the rail, the shell layout, `ownership.md` and the drawing, and AGENTS.md requires brainstorm then spec then plan for something of that shape; it also cannot run beside plan 6, because exactly one implementation plan is active at a time. WHAT IT INVALIDATES, recorded here so the future spec re-reads them rather than rediscovering them: plan 6 Task 8 Step 3's acceptance item -- 'the rail's gear opens the settings modal rather than a fifth pane' -- which is TRUE while Settings is still a modal and is superseded the moment this lands (that item is deliberately NOT corrected in plan 6, since plan 6 finishes first and the item is accurate for its duration); `vg-318`'s scrim measurement, which measures a container that will not exist; and `vg-322`, whose whole subject is the modal's width. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the spec and its plan landing, with the redrawn drawing committed beside the shipped pane and a PARITY row on the pane's frame so the next divergence is visible. PARKED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): 'Let's park the settings becomes a pane spec.' The row stays OPEN and nothing is queued against it; the sequencing sub-ruling above is unchanged, and what it invalidates stays invalidated until a spec is written.

title: The palettes carry one accent and the user has asked for a second highlight, orange for graphite, whose role is an attention or in-flight state and must be defined before any colour is chosen
detail: FOUND BY THE USER (2026-10-11), looking at the current mockup capture: 'graphite needs another highlight/accent color, like orange, on top of the current pallete (other themes to follow once we define the role of this color).' THE ROLE WAS ASKED AND ANSWERED FIRST, because a colour chosen before its job is a colour that will be used for the wrong thing: it is an ATTENTION or IN-FLIGHT STATE -- something that is neither the primary action nor destructive, such as unsaved or unpublished changes, a reading that is stale or awaiting the author, or a pending operation. Two alternatives were offered and declined: a second colour for emphasis with no state meaning, and re-hueing graphite's existing --shell-accent to orange instead of adding a role. WHAT THE ROLE REQUIRES BEFORE ANY HEX IS PICKED, and each is a decision rather than a lookup: a name that says the JOB and not the hue (--attention, not --orange); a bible section 4 clause saying when it may appear, since section 4 already rations --accent to at most one accent-filled element visible and a second colour with no stated job is exactly the competition that rationing exists to prevent; and a rule keeping it off the same element as --accent, so the two can never both claim a surface. IT IS NOT GRAPHITE'S ALONE: the user's own framing is that the role is defined once and the other five themes follow, so the output is a section 4 role plus a per-palette value in each of the six, not a graphite-only token. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the section 4 clause and the six values, which is spec work rather than a task, together with whatever gate reads a state colour -- the contrast instrument measures text and boundaries and has no state-colour row today. RELATED: `vg-330` is the other change the user asked for in the same sitting, and both are sequenced after plan 6.

title: The colour picker's four track sliders announce their test id, so a screen reader reads out a CSS-selector-shaped token instead of a word
detail:
SURFACED BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11) while adjudicating the copy walk's skip rule, and it is THE ROW `vg-194` HANDED OFF AND NOBODY FILED: that verified row's own closing paragraph ends 'each track's `aria-label` is its `testId`, so what a screen reader announces is `picker-saturation, slider, 0`, and the words an author would want are a copy decision rather than a mechanism one. That is a separate row, not a reopening of this one.' This is that row; the mechanism half `vg-194` owned is done and is not re-opened by it. THE MEASUREMENT: `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx`'s `Track` renders `aria-label={testId}`, so each of the four tracks (the saturation/brightness area, hue, and the two strips) has an accessible name of `picker-saturation`, `picker-hue` and so on -- a token shaped like a selector rather than a word. `vg-194` closed the keyboard path and the declared `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` in the same component, so the value announcement is sound; what a person hears first is the name, and the name is the defect. WHY THE COPY WALK DOES NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth recording: the walk's rule skips any element whose `aria-label` equals its `data-testid`, and the reviewer ruled that rule CORRECT -- a driver's hook is not a word a translator would change, and forcing these into `uiCopy` would be wrong. So the net is right to skip them and the label is still wrong: the two facts are independent, and the skip rule must not be weakened to catch this. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each track's `aria-label` reads a word from `uiCopy` (`Saturation`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `Value`) while the `data-testid` hooks keep their current values, so the skip rule stays and the announced name becomes a word. The wording is a copy decision, which is why it is not an agent's to take silently. RELATED: `vg-194` (verified, archived) is the row that identified this and deferred it; `vg-179` is an unrelated picker row.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FOUR PICKER TRACKS ANNOUNCE Saturation, Hue, Alpha AND Value FROM uiCopy, and they keep their current data-testid hooks so the specs that address them do not move. The reasoning is vg-264s: user-visible strings come from the copy owner, and an accessible name is user-visible text. COST IF WRONG: four strings move into the copy catalogue and the census grows by four keys, which is what that census is for.

title: The one control that renders a chart setting descriptor has no production caller, and its module doc names a consumer that does not exist
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of plan 6, which recorded it as out of that plan's range; it is not a plan-6 finding. `settingsField()` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts` has ZERO production callers: read in node across `src/web` (dist excluded), all twelve of its call sites are tests - one in `copy-defects.test.ts:138` and eleven in `controls.dom.test.ts`. Its module doc at `settings-field.ts:13-14` reads "The inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering, so the loop is this control rather than a second copy of it". The call sites were removed deliberately, not lost: `f254259b` (2026-10-06) added the file, then `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09) - "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM", plan 3 Task 3a - turned `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s descriptor loop into a view-model projection, and `settingsField` has had no production caller since. `SettingsFieldDescriptor` is referenced in production only by `settings-field.ts` itself and its owner `renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts`. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for the doc half: whether the inspector's per-kind column was meant to be migrated to this control and never was, or renders descriptors by another route, the record does not settle, and this row does not guess which. Two fixes are possible and they are a design decision rather than a task: delete the now-unused control, or migrate the column to it. Checked for duplicates first: the archive's three `settings-field` mentions are `vg-145` (a gauge end angle), `vg-121` and `vg-122` (unreachable descriptor keys), and none owns this.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: MIGRATE THE INSPECTOR'S PER-KIND COLUMN TO IT. The module doc names a consumer that does not exist and the doc was right about the intent -- the column is re-pointed at settingsField rather than the control being deleted, so the descriptor route becomes the control's real caller. BLOCKED ON A CONFLICT WITH THE REDESIGN'S SETTLED ARCHITECTURE, FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER, WHILE LOOKING FOR THE NEXT UNBLOCKED PIECE OF THE REDESIGN'S SIXTEENTH ACCEPTANCE ITEM -- WHICH NAMES THIS ROW AS ONE OF THE `fix` DIFFERENCES THAT DISCHARGES IT, SO THE CONFLICT IS ON THE CRITICAL PATH RATHER THAN BESIDE IT. The ruling above directs that the inspector's per-kind column be re-pointed at `settingsField`. **Measured: `settingsField()` returns an `HTMLElement`**, built from `addEventListener`, `setAttribute` and DOM nodes (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/controls/settings-field.ts`), so re-pointing a React column at it puts an imperative DOM island inside that column -- which is exactly what the redesign's Acceptance forbids ("Every editor surface is React, including chart fields ... no imperative UI island survives under a React wrapper") and where ADR-0039 draws the boundary. `4dc220c6` (2026-10-09, "a chart's fields are React views, not DOM") is the commit that deliberately removed the call sites, so **the ruling as written reverses a decision the redesign was built on rather than restoring one**. The half of the ruling that has moved is its premise: it rests on the module doc's claim that "the inspector's per-kind column mounts that same rendering", and `4dc220c6` superseded that intent. **NOT TAKEN IN EITHER DIRECTION, DELIBERATELY.** Deleting the control for a React view is not what was ruled; re-pointing the column is what was ruled but contradicts the redesign's own acceptance clause. A controller's licence covers code and architecture correctness, not the reversal of a user's design ruling, so the two readings need the user's word. Task 6.5b declined this same close on 2026-10-13 for the adjacent reason (a rendered-surface rewrite that would reverse `4dc220c6`), and Phase 6's close recorded the row open rather than resolving it. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT:** either the ruling is re-read as "the descriptor route should have a **React** owner", which makes the work a control in `selection-inspector/` and lets `settings-field.ts` retire unused; or the imperative island is accepted on purpose, in which case the Acceptance section's React clause gains a named exemption beside ADR-0033's. Either answer is small; guessing it wrong is a rendered-surface rewrite in the wrong direction.

title: A chart's scalar settings are validated on neither path, so a v2 envelope carrying min above max, windowSeconds 0, or innerRadiusPercent above outerRadiusPercent is accepted
detail:
FOUND BY the review of ad94e5ed (finding 5), which asked the retirement report to stop justifying the deleted chart-content cases as coverage the Fabric half performs. It does not: fabric-envelope-validate.ts chartPaintReferences (line 513, called at line 96) reads a chart's settings for PAINT fields only - gauge track/progress, line stroke/area/palette, bar fill/track, pie remainderFill/palette - and its isRecord guard means a chart whose settings is not an object skips even those. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, so the negative can be judged rather than trusted: grep -rn for windowSeconds, maxPoints, innerRadiusPercent, outerRadiusPercent, min, max and total across src/web/packages/*/src and src/web/tests (excluding *.test.ts), plus schema/theme-document.schema.json. The only hits that touch these scalars are charts/settings-fields.ts (authoring bounds for the inspector, which ADR-0028 explicitly says must not become document validation), charts/line.ts and charts/pie.ts (render, where pie clamps via clampPercent and never refuses), data/store.ts and fake-source (Math.max(0, windowSeconds) floors the window rather than refusing it), and editor/src/preview-source.ts. schema/theme-document.schema.json carries no settings property at all, because a v2 scene is opaque Fabric JSON, so no JSON-Schema bound exists either. MEASURED, not inferred: calling validateFabricThemeEnvelope on a conforming envelope whose chart object carries gauge {min: 10, max: 1}, line {windowSeconds: 0}, line {maxPoints: -5}, pie {innerRadiusPercent: 80, outerRadiusPercent: 20}, pie {total: {kind: fixed, value: null}}, or settings: ["windowSeconds"] returns ok: true for all six. PRE-EXISTING, NOT CREATED BY THE RETIREMENT: the deleted v1 validator did own these (validate.ts validateSettingsRange required gauge/bar max > min, line windowSeconds and maxPoints above 0, pie outer above inner and a finite fixed total), but the v2 path never reached it - fabric-envelope-validate.ts called validateThemeDocument with a synthetic {schemaVersion: 1, nodes: []} document, so no node-level case ever ran against an envelope. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether a scalar chart bound is meant to be enforced at the envelope boundary (refuse) or recovered at render (clamp, as pie already does); if recovery is the intent, this closes as intended behaviour with the clamping owners named.

RULED 2026-10-12: REFUSE AT THE ENVELOPE BOUNDARY, and the range comes from the descriptor table rather than a second table written into the validator. `charts/settings-fields.ts` already owns each scalar setting and already carries its own `min` (windowSeconds 1, maxPoints 2, lineWidth and markerSize 0), so the validator READS that owner instead of re-deciding it — which is what the deleted v1 validator did, and deleting it removed the refusal without moving the ownership anywhere. The relational cases are the same rule one step out: Y `min` above `max`, and `innerRadiusPercent` at or above `outerRadiusPercent`, are a PAIR the family's own descriptor owns, so they are refused where the pair is complete rather than by a range on either half. `settings: ["windowSeconds"]` is the third shape of the same rule — the allowed key set is the descriptor table's own reading, not a list the validator keeps. The pie's render-time clamp STAYS, as defence for the in-memory path that never passes through the envelope, but it stops being the only thing between an impossible document and a drawing. A document whose saved numbers disagree with what is drawn is the authored-versus-derived split this repo forbids, and a clamp at render is exactly that disagreement made invisible.
check: NOT YET RUN - the case to add: validateFabricThemeEnvelope over a chart whose scalar settings are out of bounds (gauge min above max, line windowSeconds 0, pie innerRadiusPercent above outerRadiusPercent) must be refused. Measured today all three are accepted, so that case fails until a validator owns chart scalar settings.

title: The settings drawing light preview bar is the one bar no gate reads, because its ground is a gradient rather than a solid colour, so a wrong light ground passes every row
detail:
FOUND BY the task-1 review round of 2026-10-11 (finding 2, reviewed commit 6da1716a). THE RULING OPERATIVE SENTENCE IS NOW MET FOR FIVE OF SIX BARS: mockup-values.ts carries one colour row per solid-ground palette - editorial, graphite, ember, moss, plum - each reading a bar background-color in current/settings.html against the product .editor-shell-palette-swatch[data-shell-palette=...]. THE RESIDUAL IS light: its bar (current/settings.html:82) paints background:linear-gradient(145deg,#d8ebe4,#afd4d1), and no row reads it, so repainting it to any other gradient reddens nothing. WHY THAT IS NOT A GATE - the reason this is a row rather than a test: the five rows key on background-color, the light bar declares the background shorthand, lookup (mockup-values.ts:364) matches property names exactly and returns the drawing silence for a property it does not declare, colourValue (:514) answers null for a gradient, and a length comparator cannot read a colour - so a sixth row of the same shape would fail on a drawing that is currently correct. OWNER: whoever owns the drawing preview bar; the instrument is the mockup-values.ts comparator set. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either the light bar declares a solid background-color like the other five, in which case a sixth row is the same shape and the drawing becomes a worse depiction of a product whose light ground really is a gradient; or the reader grows a comparator that resolves a gradient first stop and compares it with the product --shell-backdrop, which needs a ruling on which stop of a multi-stop gradient is the ground. The second is the honest solve and is a decision, not a silent choice. NOT A DUPLICATE: vg-310 is light translucent chrome, and vg-321 (now withdrawn, archive) is the ruling this residual belongs to - its own detail already named light a backdrop gradient.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE LIGHT PALETTE'S BAR BECOMES A SOLID background-color LIKE THE OTHER FIVE. One ground per palette and one rule in the reader, so the drawing is corrected to the shape the other five already have rather than the parity reader growing a gradient comparator plus a ruling on which stop is the ground. This does not absorb vg-322, which still owns which role a palette preview ground bar depicts.

title: The §1–§10 marker range is a shared namespace, so rule 3 accepts a bare §N from another document's numbering as a claim on a DESIGN.md marker
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2 review (2026-10-11, reviewed commit 127ff808), finding 1, filed rather than fixed. WHAT: scripts/design-md.mjs's citation rule 3 asserts that every `<!-- §N -->` marker in DESIGN.md is claimed by at least one citation, but its claim test is a bare text match over `docs/`, `src/` and `scripts/` with no notion of which document is speaking, and §1–§10 is a shared namespace. docs/product/requirements.md marks its own requirements `## §N — title` and carries a bare §7 (requirements.md:20, the Product and scope heading); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md numbers itself §1–§13. So an in-range §N from another document satisfies rule 3 for a DESIGN.md marker that nothing has actually cited. FAILURE SHAPE: if DESIGN.md's §7 marker's genuine citations were later removed, requirements.md's own §7 heading would keep rule 3 silent — the check would pass while the marker went unclaimed. DORMANT TODAY: §7 carries 178 genuine DESIGN.md claims and it is the only overlap (requirements' other markers are §31 and above); the review's independent census found each of the 18 markers carries 6–198 real claims, so no marker is currently satisfied only by a foreign §N. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: a correct fix needs a decision the plan does not make — whether a citation must come from a document that is *about* the design language, and if so which documents those are; inventing that policy inside a fix round would either over-exclude real claims or set a rule the plan owns, and the fix round was scoped to findings 2 and 3. THE SPEC'S D3 IS THE SOURCE: it claims every other §N in the range belongs to the redesign spec, which is false because requirements.md also uses §7. OWNER: whoever next touches the citation rule — the design-md-replaces-the-bible prose and code sweep (Tasks 4–5), or a follow-up to scripts/design-md.mjs. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on which documents' §N may claim a DESIGN.md marker, then encode that set as a source filter in the check. ALSO A SWEEP GUARD: Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a requirements.md §N as if it were a bible citation.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DECISION THE CHECK ENCODES: the citation namespace is DECLARED BY SOURCE, not inferred from the number. `scripts/design-md.mjs --cite` accepts any `§N` in the canonical range from any document, so `requirements.md`'s own §7 — which numbers that document's requirements — reads as a claim on `DESIGN.md`'s §7. The fix is a SOURCE SET: the check takes the list of documents whose `§N` are design-language citations (the redesign spec and the specs that build on it), declared where the canonical range is declared; `requirements.md` is NOT in it, because a document about the product's requirements is not a document about the design language and its numbers belong to itself. Two consequences stated so they are not rediscovered: `DESIGN.md` is the target and never a source, and the sweep's guard stands — Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a `requirements.md` §N as though it were a bible citation. Over-exclusion is the risk the row names, and the set bounds it: a document joins by being ABOUT the design language, which is a property a reviewer can check, unlike a number.

title: DESIGN.md's front-matter `fontFamily` is owned by nothing: no CSS token declares it, `--sync` ignores it, and the design.md linter does not require it
detail:
FOUND BY the design-md final review (2026-10-11). Every one of the six typography entries in DESIGN.md's front matter carries `fontFamily: "system-ui, sans-serif"`, and nothing owns that value. `editor-shell.css`'s `@theme static` block declares no `--font-*` token -- the stack is written inline at the use sites -- so `--sync`, which reads only the `spacing`, `rounded` and `typography` groups, never compares it. And the format does not require it: a copy of DESIGN.md with every `fontFamily` line deleted lints 0 errors / 0 warnings under `@google/design.md@0.4.0`, so the spec's step-1 claim that `fontFamily` is required by the format's Typography is not borne out. The value is therefore a transcription that no gate keeps honest and no rule forbids changing -- neither a second owner of a CSS value (the front matter's other groups are locked to the CSS) nor an enforced transcription. IT IS CORRECT TODAY; it will silently lie if the UI stack changes. THE CONTROLLER'S RULING: unresolved, and closing it needs a decision rather than a patch -- either the shell gains a `--font-*` token the front matter can be synced against (making it a real transcription like spacing/rounded/typography, the same shape the rest of the front matter has), or `fontFamily` is declared `omitted` with a reason (the format's own mechanism, already used for `colors` and `components`) so its absence is documented rather than silent. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two landed, with the front matter and the CSS agreeing afterwards.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FRONT MATTER AND THE CSS AGREE, RATHER THAN fontFamily BEING DECLARED OMITTED. The shell already declares its display stack per palette (--shell-display), so the front matters fontFamily syncs against the shells default display stack: --sync compares them and the design.md linter requires the key, which makes one fact declared once instead of a field no consumer reads. COST IF WRONG: a DESIGN.md front-matter field that must be kept in step with a CSS declaration, which is exactly what --sync exists to check.

title: `design:check` and `gates:self-test` are wired and green but run by no CI job and no hook, so the design gates' verdict depends on someone running them
detail:
FOUND BY the design-md final review (2026-10-11). WHAT WAS SEARCHED, and the negative result: `git ls-files '.github/**'` lists seven paths -- three issue templates, two markdown files, and two workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/visual-evidence.yml`); `grep -rn -E 'design:check|gates:self-test|design:md|design-tokens' .github/workflows/ .claude/settings.json` matches nothing; the only tracked hook config is `.claude/settings.json`, whose PreToolUse, PreCompact and SessionStart hooks run only `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` and `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs`; `git config core.hooksPath` is unset; no husky or githooks files are tracked; and `.git/hooks/` holds only the shipped `.sample` files. So both commands are reachable only by hand. NOT A REGRESSION: this matches the pre-existing `design-tokens` ratchet, which CI has never run either -- it is convention for this repo rather than a break introduced by the design-md plan. CI's `npx vitest run` does collect `tests/scripts/design-md.test.ts`, so the checks' logic is exercised in CI; only the live-tree verdict (`--lint`, `--sync` and `--cite` over DESIGN.md and editor-shell.css) is not. An unrun gate and a green gate look identical from outside, which is why this is filed rather than assumed harmless. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a CI step or a hook that runs `design:check` (and `gates:self-test`), or a recorded decision that they stay manual like the ratchet.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded. This row is the CI half of that answer: design:check and gates:self-test are run by CI, not by hand, so no manual-by-design record is owed.

title: A bare editor mount resumes whichever theme won a millisecond mtime tie, so the document a run starts from is not reproducible
detail:
FOUND BY Task 1 of the keyboard-only walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), as the reason its first census was not reproducible. OBSERVED: two runs of the same spec against the host app directory reseeded identically by tests/e2e/global-setup.ts opened two different documents -- the first resumed E2E missing (one object in the Layers tree, census 18 presses) and the second E2E deliberate bleed (three objects, census 26 presses). Nothing in either run touched the library. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM SOURCE rather than inferred from the two runs: theme-library-client.ts reports updatedAt, the host store sets it from stat.mtime.toISOString() (themes/store.ts, entryFor), the listing sorts by id (themes/store.ts, list), and boot-theme.ts latestOwnTheme keeps the first strict maximum -- so equal updatedAt strings are broken by id order, and toISOString truncates to milliseconds. A filesystem listing of the fixture themes shows why ties are ordinary here: e2e-bleed, e2e-bleed-all, e2e-media and e2e-missing-sensor all carry the identical mtime 2026-10-12 01:16:55.827373400, because seedHostTheme writes all ten in one pass. The part NOT observed: whether the first run seeds straddled two milliseconds -- that is what the two different winners require, and the winning id under a tie (e2e-bleed) is exactly what the second run opened, but the first run state is gone and that half stands as the explanation that fits rather than as a measurement. IMPACT: a browser test that does not name a theme starts from a document it did not choose and cannot predict, which is how a press count and a scene assertion move for a reason that is not the change under test. Two saves inside one millisecond is not something an author does by hand, so the visible product impact is small and the measured one is in tests. CLOSE THIS when the tie-break is decided and written down -- by id, by name, or by a stored save counter rather than an mtime -- or when a store with two equally-recent themes is ruled to have no right answer and the bare mount stops being used as a starting state. The walkthrough plan worked around it by pinning ?theme= and did not repair it, which is the shape this row records. OWNER: whoever owns boot-theme.ts and the theme store listing, and the decision is theirs because more than one answer is defensible.

RULED 2026-10-12: RANK BY ID — most recent save first, then `id` ascending as the tie-break, written in the store that lists themes. No new persisted field: a save counter would add a column to every theme document to cover two saves inside one millisecond, and it would need a migration and would have to stay honest forever, while `id` is already stable, already unique and already persisted — which is the whole point of a stable id. Name is rejected as the tie-break because a name is editable and two themes may share one, so it converts a rare tie into a common one. This closes the row: the bare mount may keep starting from the store's own answer, because that answer is now reproducible.

title: The manager ownership review asked for on 2026-10-09 was deferred to plan 3's close, that condition has long passed, and its seventeen rows are still open
detail: FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-09, NOT on 2026-10-12 -- this row was first filed an hour ago saying the latter, and it was wrong. The correction matters because the earlier text would read as a fresh finding and duplicate the seventeen rows this work already produced. THE ORIGINAL REQUEST, 2026-10-09, in two parts. First: "Does any domain managers need some clean up? I.e. same domain ownership spread across a few managers. A domain under another manager needs to become a manager of its own. Etc". Then, an hour later: "One question I forgot to ask earlier. Maybe you've already considered it. It's the reverse direction, does any manager turned out to be too small/narrow of a concept to stand on it own and should be folded into another?" WHAT PROMPTED BOTH, in the user's words: "the fact that we now have several files crossed the 500 lines threshold". WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing here is re-found. A read-only survey was run against docs/architecture/ownership.md and filed SEVENTEEN rows, vg-232 through vg-248, all 2026-10-09, all still open and none archived three days later. The user then said "File the manager issues in the backlog for now then", and the cleanup was DEFERRED to plan 3's close with the ordering recorded in STATUS.md (commit 47d47d32). vg-240 was named at the time as the row with real drift risk and the likeliest to be pulled forward. THE DEFERRAL CONDITION HAS PASSED. Plan 3 closed, and so did the whole redesign programme; the registers were never revisited, which is why the user had to re-raise this on 2026-10-12 and again to ask whether it was tracked. So this row is the DEADLINE for that deferral rather than a new finding. THE REVERSE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED -- measured on 2026-10-09, and the answer was NO. layer-manager (68 lines), deletion-manager (62) and object-lock-manager (129) were each read in full, and each owns a decision nobody else owns: Fabric's membership trap in ownerOf; "a removal that found nothing is not a deletion"; and the transform-flag derivation including that undo revives a locked object at Fabric's defaults. error-manager is 59 lines with 13 importers, a service by nature. That read instead surfaced the INVERSE defect, filed as vg-247: the locked predicate has no owner, so object.get("locked") is read in eleven non-test places across eight modules in two polarities. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT THE LINE COUNT, and the survey said so at the time. ownership.md carries its own test: for each row, find the code that would reject a wrong value for that concept -- the guard, the validator, the refuse -- and ask whether it lives in the module the map names. A guard in an unnamed module is a missing row or a wrong owner. That is what found vg-232 through vg-246; a line count never would have. THE SIZE MEASUREMENT, for reference and NOT as the criterion. On 2026-10-09 it was 35 source files over the 500 signal and 15 over the 800 stop out of 264; at HEAD on 2026-10-12 it is 32 and 12, so it has improved slightly. snap-manager remains the largest single domain at eight files and roughly 7,000 lines, of which five files are past 500 and four past the stop. font-trios.generated.ts at 28,284 lines is GENERATED and exempt, and editor-shell.css at 2559 already belongs to vg-274. CARRIED BY the dead-code sweep plan as Phase 4, Tasks 8 and 9, which now name the guard instrument, the passed deferral and the answered reverse question rather than treating any of them as open. SIZE CORRECTED BY THE CENSUS (2026-10-12): this row said snap-manager was "eight files and roughly 7,000 lines, of which five files are past 500 and four past the stop". docs/architecture/manager-census.md measured 30 non-test files, four of them past the 800 stop. The size is not the finding and not the fix, and this row cites the census's FILE counts rather than its line totals: a top-level and a recursive count differ by more than a factor of two in that directory, and a line total depends on whether a file's trailing newline is counted as a line, so two figures can both look authoritative while measuring different things. The census also demotes snap-manager to LAST of ten candidates: one external production module reaches it (editor-session.ts, established from the code by the census review), so its fix is a protocol re-shape needing a spec, not an extraction.

title: scene-fabric/src/persist.ts lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES with no row owning that decision
detail:
FOUND BY the manager census (2026-10-12), carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on commit a2fe5a89 and materialised here as its own row. scene-fabric/src/persist.ts:81 lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES, so whether an object's lock state persists is decided in the persist list. That is a decision about the persisted scene with no row and no map entry, and the rule that only authored state persists makes it a question rather than an oversight: a lock is authored state if the user set it deliberately and derived state if it merely mirrors a transform flag. Whether the two can disagree after a restore is not established here.

RULED 2026-10-12: `locked` IS AUTHORED STATE and persists — and the decision is already made and stated in code, which is why the missing thing is the RECORD and not the behaviour. `object-lock-manager/index.ts:92-94` says it in as many words: undo rebuilds the scene, so a revived locked object is a new instance back at Fabric's defaults, `locked` is the persisted state, and the transform flags are re-derived from it rather than persisted alongside it; `onHistoryLoaded` is the re-derivation. A lock is the author's deliberate refusal of a transform, and dropping it on save would silently re-enable editing on whichever machine reloads the file. The ownership-map entry and this row's closure belong to the ownership map's filing pass, which is the pass that exists for exactly this shape. `selectable` and `evented` beside it in the same list are NOT covered by this ruling and are not the same case: the lock writes `hasControls` and the `lock*` flags and never those two, so nothing in the lock path makes them authored — whether some other writer does is a separate question this row does not answer, and it is named in the map entry rather than answered by it.

title: A gitignored scratch directory inside src/web skews every scan that walks the filesystem, because .gitignore hides files from git and from nothing else
detail:
FOUND BY the manager census's fix round (2026-10-12), while establishing why its own file-count denominator would not reproduce. src/web/.agent-scratch/ is hidden from git by .gitignore:75 and holds residue from earlier tasks: eight files including browser probes, PNG screenshots and a vitest JSON report. It is invisible to git status and to every git-based check, and to nothing else -- a scan that walks src/web/** sees those files, which is what made the census report 317 non-test source files where a walk over packages/ yields 302. The dead-code scanner is NOT affected, and that was checked rather than assumed: its walk skips any dot-prefixed entry and .agent-scratch sits outside all four of its roots, so no row of the 311-row candidate report is phantom. WHAT IS NOT DECIDED, which is why this is a row and not a fix: whether the directory should be deleted, relocated outside the tree, or excluded by each tool that measures. Deleting it is not obviously safe -- it holds screenshots and a vitest report that may be the only copy of evidence from earlier tasks. SEVERITY: low as a product risk, moderate as an evidence risk, because it silently changed a measurement that had already propagated into a plan and two register rows before the contradiction was noticed.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled — RELOCATE src/web/.agent-scratch/ OUTSIDE THE TREE. The filesystem skew ends for every scanner at once, and the eight files -- browser probes, screenshots and a vitest report that may be the only copy -- are kept rather than deleted.

title: The authored box's minimum dimension is decided in two places, and consolidating the writers applied one of them to the resize path
detail: FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 4's review (2026-10-12). Commit dd7c3365 moved the three writers of vigiliaText.box onto writeAuthoredBoxDimension, and the owner's `value < 1` / non-finite refusal (authored-box.ts:203, pre-existing, deliberate and documented there) now applies on the text-manager resize path, which previously wrote unconditionally. THE DELTA: a resize whose `target.width * scaleX` falls below 1 now returns without writing, so the authored box keeps its previous width while Fabric's width moves -- a silent no-op rather than a visible refusal. Reachability is NOT ESTABLISHED: it needs a text object carrying a non-1 scaleX, because Fabric floors its own width at 1 and only the scale can push the product under; the review derived that from vendored Fabric 7.4.0 and the editor's resize controllers but did not execute it, and no test fires the sub-unit input -- text-manager's resize specs run at scaleX 1 and widths 170-120. THE SECOND SITE: selection-inspector's funnel floors the same dimension with MIN_DIMENSION = 1 (index.ts:272, per-kind-column.ts:281), which serves all geometry and so cannot simply move to the text owner. The two floors agree today and neither is wrong; the open question is which site owns the box's minimum, and whether `< 1` is the right floor for a path a user drags. One browser check settles it together with vg-233 -- scale a text object, drag a side handle, compare vigiliaText.box.width against width * scaleX. SEVERITY: low, because the affected input class is a text object under about two scene units wide. MEASURED 2026-10-12 (Task 2.1, the one browser check this row asked for), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote': the starter wordmark is scaled to scaleX 0.7432 by a real corner drag and its mr handle is then dragged to a scene x of left + 0.4 -- a requested rendered width under one unit. THE REFUSAL DID NOT FIRE AND THE BOX WAS NOT SKIPPED: the box was written 460 -> 26.485, and the edge landed at a rendered width of 20.427 (Fabric width 26.485), so no sub-unit width was ever produced for the value < 1 guard to refuse. The drag's landing is 20.0 scene units away from where the pointer asked to put it (62.4 units on the widened drag that follows it, in the same case). RE-RUN 2026-10-12 after commit 6cec8acf fixed the resize path's stored units (it now writes the box unscaled): the same sub-unit drag writes 460 -> 35.637 and lands at a rendered width of 27.228 -- the pre-fix numbers times 1/scaleX -- so a sub-unit width is STILL never produced and the refusal is still not reached, now 26.8 units from the ask, and the widened drag that follows lands within 1.31 units. REACHABILITY IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and the 'silent no-op' this row describes is not reproduced. The landing-versus-request disagreement is filed as vg-393; this row's own question -- which site owns the box minimum -- is untouched by the run and stays open on it.

title: `npx biome check .` fails on a test file while the CI gate runs only lint and format:check, so the repo's own toolchain is red and nothing reports it
detail:
FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 5's review (2026-10-12), which ran the whole-toolchain command rather than the two the gate names. `npx biome check .` fails on `card-insert-surfaces.dom.test.tsx` over an organizeImports assist, while `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` both pass at 616 files -- so the failure is invisible to CI and to every agent that runs the documented gate. NARROWED by the controller after filing: the assist is an `organizeImports` reorder, not a change of what the file imports -- `artboardSize` and `uiCopy` are both present and both used, so the finding is ordering only. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the repository intends `check` to be the gate, or whether the two named commands are the whole gate on purpose. What is decided: the gate and the toolchain disagree, and only one of them is run.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded.

title: The library save protocol's error is reported under the `controls` subsystem, a label that now names a module it no longer lives in
detail:
FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 5's review (2026-10-12) and flagged by the candidate's own report as a decision someone owes rather than something to smuggle into a refactor. Commit 248ff08f moved the save protocol out of `editor-session.ts` into `theme-library-manager/index.ts` and carried `errors.warn("controls", ...)` verbatim, so the warning's subsystem label names a module the code has left. SEVERITY: low as runtime behaviour -- the label is diagnostics, and the message still reaches the log -- but it is exactly the kind of stale name the move exists to remove, and a rename here is a user-visible string change that wants a decision rather than a refactor's side effect.

RULED 2026-10-12: RENAME the subsystem label to the module that owns the call now, in the next commit that touches that line — not as a refactor's side effect and not as a commit of its own. The label names a module the code has left, which is the kind of stale name the move existed to delete, and it is a diagnostic slug rather than designed copy: `errors.warn` labels a log line, and nothing in the design language governs a log line. Keep the message text untouched; only the slug moves. If that label is ever rendered in the diagnostics surface, the rename lands with the copy table's own review instead — as a log label it is not product copy, and that is the condition this ruling rests on rather than an assumption about the surface.

title: The sweep's scanner carries 22 self-test checks that no command runs, so the fix-loop work on it is unguarded
detail:
FOUND BY the controller (2026-10-12) while preparing Task 3's dispatch, checking the scanner's CLI surface before asserting it in a brief. `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs` supports `--self-test` (usage at `:48`) and Task 1 grew it from 15 to 22 checks across five fix rounds, the last rounds landing precisely because a vacuous check was caught each time. Nothing runs it: `src/web/package.json:34`'s `gates:self-test` chains seven scripts and omits this one. VERIFIED by reading the chain and by grepping the repo for the script name -- no package.json entry, no workflow, no other script invokes it. NOT ESTABLISHED, and why this is a row rather than a one-line fix: whether that chain is meant to be exhaustive. `scripts/ownership-enforcement.mjs` is in the same position and worse -- its self-test is invoked by nothing anywhere -- so the repo's rule cannot be read off the chain as 'every script with a self-test belongs in it', and adding one entry may be the wrong repair for both. SEVERITY: moderate, and it is a guard gap rather than a defect in the scanner, which passes 22/22 when run by hand. What it costs: the five rounds of work that made those checks non-vacuous is now protected by nothing, so the next edit to the scanner can break a check silently, and Task 3 runs the scanner rather than its self-test. What settles it: a decision on whether `gates:self-test` is the owner for every `scripts/*.mjs` self-test -- then either the two entries are added, or the exclusion is written down as deliberate.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D1's lead ruling covering vg-213, vg-262, vg-372, vg-355 and vg-379 together: ADOPT biome check AS THE GATE. A CI step runs biome check and gates:self-test, the organizeImports findings are fixed in that commit, and every scripts/*.mjs self-test is chained into gates:self-test rather than excluded. This row is the chaining half of that answer: dead-code-sweep and ownership-enforcement join gates:self-test, and no documented exception is taken instead.

title: The sweep has no instrument for the reverse direction: a class production source writes that no stylesheet defines
detail:
FOUND BY Task 2's independent review (2026-10-12), which recorded it as the opposite direction from that task's own question and deliberately did not chase it; VERIFIED by the controller before filing, with one repo-wide search. `settings-field.ts:248` writes `note.className = "vigilia-field-hint"`, and the string `vigilia-field-hint` occurs exactly ONCE in the entire checkout -- that write. No rule in `editor-shell.css` or `host/public/vigilia-page.css` defines it. NOT ESTABLISHED that this instance is a defect, and it probably is not: six lines below, the same statement sets an inline `cssText` that hides the element (`position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;clip-path:inset(50%)`), so it is a screen-reader-only description node and a missing rule costs nothing visible. **The row is the GAP, not the instance**: Task 2's report reads CSS-to-source (which selectors the product still reaches) and Task 1's scanner reads modules and exports nothing imports, so a class that production writes and no stylesheet defines falls outside every instrument this sweep built -- and this example is harmless only by accident of the inline style beside it. SEVERITY: low for behaviour, moderate as a completeness finding about the sweep's own coverage. What settles it: a decision on whether the reverse direction is in scope at all. If it is, the cheap form is extending the selector instrument to read `className`/`classList` writes alongside `class=` literals, which is also the shape that would make the `PRODUCT` column independent of whether a name happens to appear in prose.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE REVERSE DIRECTION IS IN SCOPE, AND THE SELECTOR INSTRUMENT WIDENS. It reads className and classList writes alongside class= literals, so a class production writes that no stylesheet defines becomes visible and the PRODUCT column stops depending on whether a name happens to appear in prose. The one measured instance is harmless by accident, which is why the gap is closed before an instance arrives that is not.

title: The sweep's `redundant-export` tier counts a declaration-shaped occurrence as a use, so a symbol kept alive by its own object key or its own re-export reads as live
detail:
FOUND BY Task 4's independent review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), verifying a claim the sweep's implementer raised and deliberately did not file. MECHANISM: the tier's liveness test is an occurrence of the symbol's name outside quoted strings in its own declaring file, and `panel:` inside an object literal satisfies it while being a KEY rather than a read. OBSERVED at the sweep's base commit `5854bed5`: the row for `panel` in `packages/editor/src/new-fabric-theme-globals.ts` read "the symbol is LIVE: its own declaring file uses it (2 occurrence(s) of the name outside quoted strings, the declaration that names it excluded)", and both occurrences are property keys -- `starterPalette.panel` (now `:84`, `panel: { name: "Panel", value: { kind: "solid", color: "#081523d9" } }`) and the second map's `panel: "#081523d9"` (now `:163`). Neither is a reference and the const had no reader, so the sweep deleted it in `93bb2c5f`; what flagged it was `noUnusedVariables` once the `export` keyword came off, so TYPECHECK IS THE BACKSTOP for this class rather than the tier. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the safe direction: every symbol whose name happens to appear as an object key in its own declaring file is withheld from the removal list, so this tier can only over-retain; the cost is survivors, never breakage, and the plan's bias prefers a survivor to a bad delete. It is nonetheless a precision defect in the instrument that produced the removal list, and it hid one deletion behind a verdict that read as evidence. FIX DIRECTION NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the tier should stop counting property keys, or whether the tier is meant as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests -- deciding that is the work. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`. VERIFIED by the review report at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-4-review.md`. SECOND INSTANCE, found 2026-10-12 by Task 5's independent review of the same sweep (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-5-review.md`, attack 6) and carried by that task as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in commit `c9ed9dcc`. The same self-use test is satisfied by a RE-EXPORT STATEMENT: `packages/player/src/artboard-crop.ts` re-exported `countable` and `EDGE_TOLERANCE`, and the tier read those re-export lines as in-file uses, which withheld both rows from the removal list. Verified in `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`: the tier asks `usesIn(selfUse.get(file), name)`, and `declaredExports` reads `export { x };` as declared exports, so a re-export is counted as a use of the name it re-exports. Task 5 removed the dead re-export anyway, on the grounds that the re-export line is the thing that needed removing rather than evidence that the symbol was live. CORRECTION TO THE TRAILER, for whoever picks this up: the trailer quotes the scanner as printing "(2 occurrence(s))" where it prints 1, because `usesDeclaration` subtracts the import specifier. AND THE TWO INSTANCES SHARE ONE FIX, which is why this is an amendment rather than a second row: the self-use test counts an occurrence that DECLARES the name (an object key, a re-export) as though it READ it, so the fix direction is stated once -- either the test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, or the tier is treated as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A DECLARATION IS NOT A USE.
