The self-use test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, so an object key or a re-export stops counting as a read of the name it declares and the redundant-export tier reports a symbol kept alive only by its own declaration.

title: The sweep's `barrel-only-export` tier is unreachable, so 133 candidate exports were never reported and the report's zero reads as a measurement
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), a read-only seat, as one of its two load-bearing findings; REPRODUCED by the controller against the real classification loop before this row was written, because the seat's own evidence sat in an ignored directory a clone does not carry.  THE MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than a property of this tree. `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs:705` is `if (prodConsumers.length > 0) continue;`, and it runs before the `barrel-only-export` branch at `:708`. A file's own package barrel reaches it by a re-export edge the scanner does follow, and the barrel is not a test file, so `prodConsumers` is non-empty for exactly the shape `:708` exists to report. Its condition can therefore only be evaluated when it is already false: the tier cannot fire for any input.  THE PLAN REQUIRES THAT SHAPE, in those words. Step 2 of Task 1: "`barrel-only-export` - a name whose only importer is its own package's `index.ts`." So the requirement is unimplemented, not merely unexercised, and the difference matters to whoever acts on this row: an unexercised kind may fire tomorrow, this one cannot fire at all. The ledger parked it at line 838 as "remains unexercised", which understates it by exactly that gap.  MEASURED, by a copy of the scanner with one filter corrected to exclude the file's own barrel from `prodConsumers`, run over the same tree at `93fa9a5a`: 240 candidates, of which `barrel-only-export` is 133, and the other kinds come out at exactly their HEAD counts (dead-export 8, redundant-export 83, test-only-consumer 7, unreachable-branch 9, and `no-importer-file` at 0, so it has no rows). The 133 are therefore pure additions and the existing 107 do not reclassify. By package: editor 1, fake-source 2, host 21, renderer-core 91, scene-fabric 18.  TWO DEFENSIBLE DEFINITIONS, and the disagreement is part of the defect rather than noise around it. The plan's literal wording - the only importer is the barrel, tests included - yields 76: those of the 133 whose evidence names no test importer. The code's own intent at `:708` - no production consumer other than the barrel, with test consumers disclosed in the row - yields all 133. Both measured: 76 rows have an empty test-importer list and 57 name test importers. Which one the tier means is a decision, and that is why this is filed rather than fixed on the spot, even though the filter itself is one condition.  NOT PROVEN DEAD, and nothing may be deleted on this row alone. A candidate is not a verdict. renderer-core's 91 (49 strict, 42 test-consumed) is consistent with a private library barrel wider than its consumers, but no row was adjudicated and the string-resolved vocabulary this repo resolves at runtime is invisible to the graph.  WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE THE SWEEP'S REMOVALS BEING SOUND. Nothing the sweep removed had been reported by the missing tier, so the removals stand. What does not stand is the picture: `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md` reports this kind as 0 in its by-kind table and again in its delta table, which reads as a measurement that there are none, and its own disclosure said the kind "has never fired in this tree" - inviting the same conclusion instead of naming the incapability. The sweep's after-picture, 312 candidates to 107, is a floor rather than a measurement of what remains, and the report now says so.  REMEDY, and it is deliberately not taken inside the sweep: correct the filter, decide the tier's definition, re-run, and adjudicate the newly visible rows as a sweep of its own. Reopening a phase three reviews had closed, to make the candidate count larger rather than more correct, was the wrong trade at that plan's close.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: the barrel-only-export tier means NO PRODUCTION CONSUMER OTHER THAN THE BARREL, WITH TEST CONSUMERS DISCLOSED -- 133 candidates, not the plan's literal sole-importer shape's 76. A test importing a barrel export is disclosed in the report and does not hide the export from the tier, because a survivor costs a ticket and a deleted live symbol costs the product, so the bias stays on detection. The filter is corrected, the sweep is re-run, and the newly visible rows are adjudicated as a sweep of its own.

title: An in-app store where authors submit themes and anyone can browse and download them
detail: RAISED BY THE USER on 2026-10-12 as a brainstorming exercise: not accepted work, and the user does not intend to start it soon. DESIGN RECORD: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-theme-store-design.md, Status draft. SHAPE AGREED IN CONVERSATION: GitHub is the whole backend, so nothing is run and nothing is paid for. The catalogue is item.json files in one public repo; identity is the author's GitHub account reused for everything; a submission is a pull request; the review instrument is the diff, which a theme being JSON makes readable; merging lists the item; a login added to a verified-authors list makes that author's own PRs auto-merge, and that auto-merge must be scoped to the author's own catalogue path or one compromised account rewrites the store's CI; media rides on release assets, which carries a native download_count. THE EXCHANGE UNIT ALREADY EXISTS, which is why this is small: §139, ADR-0004 and 0017 fix the validated package ZIP as the portable artifact, §141 fixes validation, and host/src/themes/store.ts already enforces 32 MiB per asset and 128 MiB total, on save and on load, so the store defines no format, no validator and no size policy. IDENTITY IS SKIPPABLE: browsing is a static index.json and downloads are plain URLs, so neither needs a token nor an API call, favorite COUNTS still render anonymously because the Action bakes them into index.json, and sign-in is a just-in-time prompt on the heart only. VIEWS ARE DROPPED: GitHub exposes no free per-item view count, so 'most viewed' is not a sort and sorting is created, updated, downloads and favorites. MEDIA: video is expected to be common and rides inside the package, so an unbounded video is what would break a zero-cost host; the existing size cap needs a companion duration cap (proposed 30s) and resolution ceiling (proposed 1920 long edge) or an author cannot predict the outcome, and a publish-time normalizer holds the envelope. OPEN, each needing a decision rather than a patch: hosting the bytes (release assets versus an object store with zero egress), the ffmpeg source for the normalizer (a probed system binary versus a bundled static build carrying GPL parts such as x264), index.json freshness, who inspects imagery for moderation, and removal semantics. UNVERIFIED: every free-tier limit the design leans on, listed in the spec, because a false one changes the architecture. NAMING: the owner ruled on 2026-10-12 that the existing editor-to-phone publish route is renamed so the store owns the word; 'activate' was the suggestion but collides with keyboard-activation in editor/src/viewport-manager/navigation.ts, cast and go-live are the clear candidates, and the rename is a family spanning the route, the published store in host/src/server.ts (a watched path) and publish-loop.spec.ts, so it can land alone before any store work. WIDGETS ARE OUT OF SCOPE: widget packages do not exist yet because §139 defers them until they have an authoring workflow, so the widget store needs its own spec.

title: Escape out of a layer rename drops focus to the document body, so a keyboard author loses their place
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4'S REVIEW of the keyboard walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), MEASURED rather than read: the reviewer's probe on the committed bytes printed `PROBE-AFTER-ESCAPE BODY|`, where the walk expected to still be on the row it was renaming. WHAT: with a composition row's rename field focused, Escape cancels the draft and the field unmounts, and focus is left on `document.body` -- nothing returns it to the row. The next Tab therefore restarts from the top of the document instead of continuing from the author's place. WHY IT MATTERS: section 13.1's keyboard-only walkthrough requires focus to be where an interaction left it, and this is the one sub-step in the assembled walk where it is not; the helper that drives it re-tabs from the document root under a bounded press count, which works and is not the behaviour a keyboard user gets to rely on. It is NOT in the assembled §13.1 walk: that walk's field interaction is the inspector's ControlText, whose Escape leaves focus in the field, and the rename cancel lives in the plan's separate Task 4 test. WHAT IT COSTS the plan that found it: the walk is less continuous there than it reads, and Task 5 must not assume it resumes in place -- recorded in that plan's ledger. NOT FIXED THERE ON PURPOSE: the walkthrough plan's Out of scope reads "No new focus management. If a region is unreachable, this plan records it; changing the shell's focus order is its own change with its own spec." A register row is that record. OWNER: whoever owns the composition row's own focus -- the rename field is opened by Enter or F2 on a treeitem and is unmounted by the cancel without a focus return. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether the same cancel-by-Escape inside a settings row or a dialog does the same; only the composition row was driven.

title: Two plans' parity comparisons no longer exist, and the acceptance item that requires them has no wording for that
detail: FOUND BY the counted acceptance pass of 2026-10-12, which walked every item of the design-language spec's Acceptance section and found this the only one not discharged. WHAT: that section's last item requires every plan's parity capture to exist beside its mockup in docs/design/mockups/ with every difference either fixed or backed by a cited rule. Plans 6, 7 and 8 have captures (shell-capture-add.png, shell-capture-graphite.png, shell-capture-glyphs.png beside shell.html; settings-capture-graphite.png and settings-capture-editorial.png beside settings.html, registered in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md). Plans 1 and 3 do not: current/controls.html and current/controls-light.html have no capture beside them, no .superpowers/sdd/ workspace survives for either plan, and the archived acceptance ledger in docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy.md records in its own words that Plan 1's ten differences no longer exist anywhere. WHY IT MATTERS: the item cannot be met or refused as written, because for those two plans the thing it asks to be checked is gone; the verdict the archived ledger records for the item (met) was taken on the capture half only and never addressed this half. WHAT IT NEEDS: a decision rather than code -- either reproduce the comparison from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive. OWNER: whoever owns the spec's Acceptance text; the item is the spec's, so the decision is the user's. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW: whether any of plan 1's or 3's differences were in fact fixed later under another plan's name; only that no record of the comparison survives to establish it. THE CAPTURE HALF IS NOW PLACED FOR EVERY DRAWING, MEASURED 2026-10-13, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THIS ROW OWNS BUT NOT WHAT IT ASKS. The paragraph above said `current/controls.html` and `current/controls-light.html` have no capture beside them; they do now. `controls-capture-graphite.png` and `controls-capture-editorial.png` sit beside those two drawings (`988d1788`), placed from the registered action `the control set renders in the design language` (`captureVisualReview(page, testInfo, "control-set")`, `design-language.spec.ts:1410`) and registered in `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md`. **And the same pass closed the modal's third sheet**: `settings-keyboard.html` and `settings-about.html` had no capture either, though the one action already photographs all three tabs, so `settings-keyboard-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` and `settings-about-capture-{graphite,editorial}.png` were added beside their drawings and the existing two were re-shot, because the committed six were taken 2026-10-11 (`f7078e93`) and the dialog moved under them on 2026-10-13 (`69e6e7f1`'s `dl > div` padding, `7a92d0fe`'s dialog section-2 body role) — the Appearance and About renders are now 2px shorter and the Keyboard render 6px narrower than the committed bytes (`e412c98d`). **So as of `e412c98d` every drawing in `docs/design/mockups/current/` has a capture pair beside it** — six drawings, twelve PNGs — and the first half of the acceptance item is met for every plan whose matching mockup is one of them. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND IT IS THE ROW'S ACTUAL SUBJECT.** The item says *each plan's* completion report carries *its* capture, and the prose attributes captures to plans 1, 3 (`988d1788`), 6 (`shell-capture-glyphs.png`), 7 (the shell pair) and 8 (the three settings pairs). **No durable record names a capture for plans 2, 4 or 5** — their completion reports died with their `.superpowers/sdd/` workspaces, and the register holds no row for it. Whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps. **WHAT IT NEEDS IS UNCHANGED**: a decision rather than code — either reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons from each capture and the commit body that carried it, or narrow the item's wording to the plans whose reports survive, and settle whether plans 2, 4 and 5 are inside that wording at all. NEAR ROWS: `vg-436` (the `controls-light.html` naming question, which this row's own paragraph names by that filename); `vg-434` (references that resolve to nothing); `vg-316`, `vg-319` (the open `fix` differences that keep the item's second clause unmet regardless of the capture half). THE OPEN QUESTION THIS ROW NAMED IS NOW ANSWERED, 2026-10-13: the row said "whether their captures were the shell and settings images already beside those drawings, or were never distinct, is not recorded anywhere this repository keeps". **They were, and the mapping is now recorded.** **THE PLANS, FROM THE SPEC'S OWN TABLE** (`2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md:396-405`): 1 the control set, 2 the shell and rail, 3 the inspector, 4 the panes, 5 settings and appearance, 6 iconography and copy, 7 shell parity, 8 settings parity. **WHAT EACH DRAWING ANSWERS FOR.** `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` draw plan 1's set, which plan 3's column is built on. `shell.html` draws plans 2, 3 and 7 at once: its Position, Paint and Spends sections are the inspector's (`grep` finds those words in it and finds Composition, Tokens and Document in no drawing at all), and it is the drawing both parity plans were pulled to. Plans 2, 4 and 5 are named in none of them, so a reader pairing captures to plans finds those three absent and concludes the evidence is gone. **That paragraph is now written**: the README records which surfaces each of the six drawings and their eleven captures show, explicitly not as a claim that a plan's own report names its capture. **WHAT THE RULING THEREFORE TURNS ON, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN THE ROW FIRST PUT IT.** It is not "reproduce plan 1's and plan 3's comparisons or narrow the item", although plans 1 and 3's own comparisons are still gone with their workspaces. THE WORDING QUESTION HAS A NORMATIVE RULE ON ONE SIDE, FOUND 2026-10-13: `docs/design/mockups/README.md` is not only a description of the set -- it carries a rule for keeping it current, under **Keeping them current**: "**The current files are refreshed when the set of surfaces changes.** A pane, a tab, a section or a rail slot that appears or disappears is drawn -- in the original's treatment, never in a treatment of the product's devising." **So the undrawn panes are not merely unreachable; the drawings' own rule requires them to have been drawn.** Composition, Tokens and Document are shipped panes and they are named in no drawing (`shell.html` draws the shell and the Add pane, and the three panes' captures sit beside nothing). THE SECOND CLAUSE'S RESIDUE IS EVERY PLAN'S, MEASURED ACROSS ALL EIGHT ON 2026-10-13, AND IT IS NOT THREE ROWS. The spec's discharge paragraph counts plan 8's three, which is right for plan 8 and understates the clause, because the clause reads "every plan's parity capture ... every difference it lists". DISPOSITION CORRECTED 2026-10-13, because the sentence above is one step stale. title: No spec asserts the player's update loop reaches the canvas now the case that did was deleted with display-fabric.spec.ts
detail: FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-196 rather than reading the coverage out of a row whose subject was deleted. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A HOLE: vg-196's subject was `display-fabric.spec.ts`'s case `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, held by that row's own words to be a STANDING RED -- a 30 s timeout landing before its assertion, reproduced at `af499716` -- so the coverage the file believed it had for the update loop was absent rather than passing. Commit `ad94e5ed` deleted the spec and with it the red; it did not repair the loop, and whether the loop is still covered was never answered. WHAT IS VERIFIED AT HEAD (2026-10-12): `openCanvasPlayer`, the shared helper that case awaited, has zero occurrences repo-wide; `page.clock` survives only as the shared `tests/e2e/clock.ts` helper `installFixedClock`, whose call sites are `tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts`'s two determinism captures (`:4435`, `:4518`) and `clock.ts`'s own `openPaused`, an exported helper with no callers anywhere (measured 2026-10-12), so no player spec installs a clock; and no surviving spec reads the artboard canvas twice with a sample between the reads -- `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` proves samples arrive (its `batchCount` reading and the disappearance of `#vigilia-connection`) and that the artboard canvas is visible, neither of which is a repaint. The case in `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/scene/mount.dom.test.ts` that does drive `handle.update` asserts DOM span identity, which is the DOM renderer, not the Fabric canvas the player mounts. WHY IT MATTERS: the deleted case's own comment recorded its failure verified by sabotage -- the update call cut, and it goes red -- and it was the only thing in the suite that would notice the update loop ceasing to reach the canvas. OWNER: the refresh path that reaches the canvas is `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts` (`refresh()`, which drives `hydrateCharts` and `refreshBoundText` and then calls `handle.canvas.requestRenderAll()`, scheduled by `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30, ...)`), whose binding helpers come from the scene-fabric package — `refreshBoundText` in `fabric-text.ts` and `startChartRefresh` in `chart-refresh.ts`, with `hydrateCharts` local to the player — while `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts` is the mount path (`createSceneAdapter`), not the refresh; a replacement case belongs in `src/web/tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` beside its live-sample test. WHAT SETTLES IT: one browser case that reads the artboard canvas, drives at least one sample, and requires the pixels to differ between the two reads. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the coverage is wanted at all -- the close is legitimate without it, and this row exists so the hole is tracked rather than reconstructed from a row whose subject is gone.

title: The inspector's write funnel is unreconciled: its writers left selection-inspector/index.ts, but the dispatch and the closure state it reads stayed behind
detail: FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-255. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A QUESTION: vg-255's subject was a line count -- `selection-inspector/index.ts` past AGENTS.md's 800-line stop -- and its own AMENDED note already recorded that commit `3e8c9523` had taken the file back under the stop (822 -> 736) while the archived plan's own 540-line constraint still stood. The file is 707 lines today, so the close holds. THE QUESTION THE CLOSE DROPS, in that row's own words: splitting the write funnel out 'means deciding where the write path lives and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`, which are closure state the funnel reads at call time'. THE SPLIT HAPPENED; THE FUNNEL DID NOT MOVE WITH IT: the writes now live outside `index.ts` -- `writePanelField` and `writeShapeGeometryField` in `selection-inspector/panel.ts`, `writeGlassField` in `selection-inspector/glass.ts`, `writeMark` in `selection-inspector/bleed.ts`, and the run and binding writes in `selection-inspector/run-edits.ts` -- while the state they are asked from stayed in the closure. WHAT REMAINS UNRECORDED: the revision-and-lock refusal is `view.ts`'s `editRefusal`, read against the live target inside `createSelectionInspector`'s `edits.commit`; the dispatch that picks a writer by `fieldId` (the `panel-` and `glass-` prefixes and the shape-geometry fall-through) is that same function; and the state that makes the read correct is the closure's `let described` and `let targetRevision`, which each writer receives second-hand as an argument rather than reads. So the per-kind writers are named owners and the funnel that asks them is not, and nothing decides whether the next converted field adds another branch to `edits.commit` or moves the funnel out. `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the writers (`panel.ts`, `glass.ts`) and the directory, and says nothing about the dispatch or the closure state. WHY IT MATTERS: it is vg-255's question one refactor later -- the file is under the stop because leaves were extracted, not because the shape was decided -- and `panel.ts` is now 751 lines, close to the same stop. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/selection-inspector/` (`createSelectionInspector` and its closure state); the decision is a design one, and `docs/architecture/ownership.md` is where a ruling would land. WHAT SETTLES IT: a recorded decision on where the write funnel lives -- in the closure, in a module of its own, or in the per-kind writers -- and how it reaches `described` and `targetRevision`. NOT A RUNTIME DEFECT: vg-255's reviewer found no behavioural problem, and none is claimed here.

title: A side-handle resize of a scaled text lands its edge tens of scene units away from the edge the pointer asked for
detail: FOUND while writing the browser check vg-233 and vg-370 asked for (Task 2.1 of the backlog-drain plan), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote'. THE MEASUREMENT, AS IT STANDS AFTER COMMIT 6cec8acf: the starter wordmark carries scaleX 0.7432 and its mr handle is dragged to a scene x the test names. Dragged to left + 240 the edge now lands within 1.31 scene units of the request -- that drag has LEFT this row, it was the resize path storing width * scaleX, and it is fixed and measured with vg-233 (the 240-unit request landed at 177.58431831416544 before the fix, so it was 62.4156816858345 short (exactly `asked - landed`). CORRECTED 2026-10-12: this row called that landing 'the request times scaleX', and it is not -- 240 x 0.7431987269831705 is 178.36769447596086, 0.78 above it. The equality that IS exact is on the box: the pre-fix `boxAfter` 237.94593984979582 is the post-fix 320.1646224767875 times `scaleX`, so the scaled write shrank the object by exactly `scaleX`). The subject that remains is the OTHER drag in the same case: to left + 0.4 the edge lands at a rendered width of 27.228 where 0.4 was asked, 26.8 scene units away, with the box written 460 -> 35.637 for the ask. WHAT THE FIX DOES NOT EXPLAIN: the sub-unit gap moved from 20.427 to 27.228 -- the pre-fix number times 1/scaleX -- and is still 26.8 units wide, so a wrong stored unit explains neither its size nor its direction. The relation this row flagged for a tracer (the landed rendered width being 0.740 of the request) is therefore explained and closed; the sub-unit landing is not. One number to trace by: the landed Fabric width is 35.637, neither the sub-unit value asked for nor the floor at 1, so the value < 1 refusal is not what decides it. THE HARNESS IS NOT THE SUSPECT: the same helper (resizeRightHandleTo with editor-canvas.ts objectHandleScenePoint) lands group-ram-card's mr handle within 3 units of where the pointer was put in 'snaps a resize onto a neighbour's line', and the test's own askedLanding is the pointer's scene x read back through the canvas' getScenePoint, so the pointer was where the test says it was. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for this drag: whether Fabric's changeWidth measures a pointer in another frame once a scaled Textbox is near a unit wide, or an editor path re-derives the width after guardBoxWidth restores it, is not traced. OWNER: scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts's guardBoxWidth and the editor's text-manager resize path, whichever the trace lands on. SEVERITY: low for the product -- an author sees the edge stop short and drags again -- but it is why vg-370's sub-unit input could not be reached, so it blocks that row's settlement. EVIDENCE: the pre-fix numbers were identical in every run of that case (three runs, one report retained per run at C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize.json), and the post-fix numbers are from C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json -- both outside the tree, each read from that run's own JSON report.
