title: The reuse gate cannot refuse a new file in most of its watchlisted directories, because a note claiming the directory covers everything beneath it
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE CHECKING WHETHER TWO LIVE SEATS WERE BLOCKED BY THE GATE -- they were not, and finding out why surfaced this. `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s `covers()` treats a `Paths:` claim ending in `/` as covering every path beneath it, so a note that claims a DIRECTORY permits a first write to ANY file in it, including files that did not exist when the note was written and that the note never discusses. THE MEASUREMENT, taken by piping a synthetic path for every watchlist entry through the gate itself (`{tool_input:{file_path}}` on stdin; the probe lives at `C:\tmp\vigilia-drain\gate-audit.mjs`): **16 of the 20 watchlist entries allow a brand-new file.** The four that can still refuse are anchored file entries or the bare `scripts/` -- `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts`, `scene-fabric/src/object-asset.ts`, `renderer-core/src/data/protocol.ts`, `scripts/`. Every directory entry is open, and the notes claiming them are about other decisions: `renderer-core/src/theme/` is claimed by 0022, 0023, 0028 and 0041; `editor/src/components/ui/` by 0033, 0036, 0037 and 0038; `renderer-core/src/charts/` by 0028; and `host/src/providers/` -- a directory whose whole purpose is that each provider's acquisition is its own mechanism -- is opened by a note naming one provider. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: the gate's `--self-test` still passes and its refusal path still works, because it asserts against a SYNTHETIC `claimed` array (`reuse-gate.mjs:161-171`), so no self-test case can see the real registry. And whether a directory claim is MEANT to cover a new file is a decision, not an obvious correction -- the honest case for today's behaviour is that four notes collectively own the theme package. `docs/decisions/0025` decided a different question (how deep a bare entry matches) and does not settle this. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a rule stating whether a directory claim reaches files the note never discusses, then either a per-file claim convention or a gate that asks for a note naming the file. OWNER: `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`, with `docs/decisions/README.md`. SEVERITY: low at the surface and high in kind -- nothing breaks, and the boundary the watchlist names is unguarded for a new file in most of it, which is the gate's own stated failure ("a gate that cannot see a boundary is worse than no gate").

title: Nothing measures how much of the editor the design-token ratchet has not converted, so "only grows" has no target and no finish
detail: FOUND BY TASK 8.3B'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-13), WHILE CHECKING WHY `vg-334`'s RAW LITERAL WAS NOT CAUGHT BY THE SCANNER THE ROW SAID WAS WATCHING IT. THE SCANNER IS A CONVERSION RATCHET BY DESIGN, AND THAT DESIGN IS THE FINDING: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` holds 71 entries, and `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:9-11` states the list is the files ALREADY CONVERTED and that it ONLY GROWS. A listed file must be clean, so a file still holding a raw literal cannot be on it -- which is exactly correct behaviour and exactly why the ratchet can never say what is left. THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx` sits outside it (0 grep hits; `git log -S` over the list finds no commit ever naming it) and so does its sibling `colour-picker.tsx`, which holds 17 raw hexes. IT IS NOT AN EXCLUSION BY KIND -- 14 `.dom.test.tsx` files ARE listed -- so the gap is per-file conversion progress with no denominator. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the honest repair is not "add both files" (that is two entries against an unknown remainder) but a decision about whether the ratchet owes a measure -- a count of editor files still holding literals, or a rule that new UI files join the list when they are written. The second is the one that stops the remainder growing, and it is a policy call about where a new component's tokens come from, not a scanner edit. NEAR ROWS: `vg-334` (closed 2026-10-13 -- its `check` never claimed the gated count, so it stands; its `detail` carried the false scanner attribution and is corrected). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a rule stating whether the gated list is a migration in progress or the permanent coverage boundary, and then either a measure of the remainder or a requirement that a new `components/ui/` file arrives with its tokens. OWNER: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`, with `docs/decisions/0040` (the ratchet is ours, not a biome rule) as the decision it extends. SEVERITY: low today, and it compounds -- each new component written with a literal is a file the ratchet will never see.

title: The host's library listing keeps an empty theme name where the editor falls back to the id, so one theme is named two things
detail: FOUND BY TASK 8.2A'S FIX-ROUND RE-REVIEW (2026-10-13), WHILE CHECKING `vg-218`'S CLOSE. `vg-218` CLOSED THE EDITOR'S SPELLING AND ITS `check` CALLED THE HOST'S A FIFTH SPELLING OF THE SAME FALLBACK. IT IS NOT THE SAME FALLBACK, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS OBSERVABLE. THE TWO SPELLINGS, BOTH READ AT HEAD: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/bridge.ts:128` is `return identity.name || identity.id;` and `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts:555` is `name: envelope.metadata?.name ?? id,`. `||` FALLS BACK ON EVERY FALSY NAME AND `??` ONLY ON NULL/UNDEFINED, SO ON `metadata.name === ""` THE EDITOR NAMES THE THEME BY ITS ID AND THE HOST NAMES IT BY THE EMPTY STRING -- the same theme appearing as its id in the editor and as a blank row in the host's library listing. THE EMPTY STRING IS REACHABLE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: `schema/theme-document.schema.json:30` gives `name` `"maxLength": 200` AND NO `minLength`, so a theme with `name: ""` validates -- and the same schema sets `"minLength": 1` on the palette and typePreset names at `:72` and `:79`, so a floor was deliberately applied where one was wanted and deliberately omitted here. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the repair is not a substitution but a decision. Either the host adopts `||` (`vg-218`'s reading), or the schema gains a `minLength` and the empty name becomes unsaveable -- and the second is the stronger claim, because it fixes the reachability rather than the symptom, while touching saved-theme validation and every fixture that writes a theme. NEAR ROWS: `vg-218` (editor spelling, ruled 2026-10-13; its `check` is corrected by this pass and no longer calls the host's `??` the same fallback). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether an empty theme name is a name at all, and then either the host's spelling or the schema's floor. OWNER: `src/web/packages/host/src/themes/store.ts` with `schema/theme-document.schema.json`. SEVERITY: low -- a blank entry in a listing, on input no UI produces today.

title: Destructive is painted `--hot` a second time by a primitive prop and two pane buttons, so a control can say destructive on its own authority
detail: FOUND BY TASK 8.3B'S FIX-ROUND RE-REVIEW (2026-10-13), WHILE CHECKING WHETHER THE FIX LEFT ANY SURFACE WITH ITS OWN WAY TO PAINT §4'S MARK. `vg-226` SETTLED THAT DELETE'S MARK AND ITS COLOUR COME FROM THE REGISTRY'S OWN `destructive` FLAG, THROUGH ONE `destructiveMarker` AND ONE `[data-vigilia-destructive]` RULE. THREE PLACES STILL EXPRESS "DESTRUCTIVE PAINTS --hot" WITHOUT THE REGISTRY, AND NONE RENDERS A REGISTRY ACTION, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE A ROW AND NOT PART OF THAT FIX. ONE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-icon-button.tsx:55` DECLARES `readonly destructive?: boolean`, WHOSE ONLY EFFECT IS `tone = "text-hot"` AT `:77-81`. COMMIT `bda5ce30` MADE IT PRODUCTION-DEAD -- THE SOLE REMAINING PASSER IS `src/web/packages/editor/src/control-fixture.tsx:236`, A DEV GALLERY, AND NO TEST PASSES IT -- SO THE PROP NOW EXISTS ONLY TO BE FORGOTTEN. TWO AND THREE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx:460` AND `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx:391` EACH CARRY A BUTTON PAINTED `text-hot disabled:text-faint` FROM THEIR OWN CLASS LIST. THE FAILING SCENARIO THE REVIEW MEASURED: A CALLER PASSING `destructive` ALONGSIDE THE MARKER AND `disabled` GETS `text-faint`, WHICH THE UNLAYERED MARKER RULE OUTRANKS -- SO A DISABLED DESTRUCTIVE CONTROL PAINTS `--hot`, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT `DESIGN.md` §4 FORBIDS AT `:112` ("a disabled destructive control stays `--faint` rather than dimming red"). IT IS INERT TODAY BECAUSE NO CALLER PASSES THE PROP, WHICH IS ALSO WHY NOTHING WOULD NOTICE. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX IN THAT ROUND: THE THREE SITES ARE OUTSIDE `vg-226`'S SURFACES (NONE RENDERS A REGISTRY ACTION), THE FIRST NEEDS A DECISION ABOUT WHETHER THE PRIMITIVE KEEPS THE AFFORDANCE AT ALL, AND THE OTHER TWO PAINT A DELIBERATE EDITOR-STATE COLOUR THAT IS NOT THE MARK. THE REPAIR IS EITHER DELETION (REMOVING THE PROP AND POINTING THE GALLERY AT THE MARKER -- VERIFIED AS TWO FILES WITH NO TEST OR E2E IMPACT) OR A RULING THAT THESE THREE ARE OUTSIDE THE ONE-OWNER RULE. NEAR ROWS: `vg-226` (closed 2026-10-13). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: A RULING ON WHETHER THE MARK IS THE ONLY ROUTE TO `--hot` IN THE EDITOR, AND THEN DELETION OR AN EXPLICIT EXCEPTION. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-icon-button.tsx` WITH `control-fixture.tsx`, `panes/tokens/preset-list.tsx` AND `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx`. SEVERITY: low -- the same second-expression shape `vg-226` was filed for, one level down and inert, but a control that can declare itself destructive is the thing that produced `vg-226` in the first place.

title: `reuseExistingServer` lets a browser pass run against a preview server left over from a previous session, so the bundle under test can predate the change
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE CLEARING THE MACHINE FOR TASK 8.3D, AND IT WOULD HAVE SILENTLY INVALIDATED THE PHASE 8 CLOSE. `src/web/playwright.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: true` on all three `webServer` entries (the player preview, the editor preview and the real host). THE MEASUREMENT: a listener on port 4174, PID 83448, `vite preview packages/editor --port 4174 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1`, started 2026-10-12 09:17:30 and STILL LISTENING TWENTY-ONE HOURS LATER. It was spawned by an earlier Playwright run and never reaped. `AGENTS.md` requires that affected bundles be rebuilt before a browser pass, and this is why that rule is not sufficient on its own: THE REBUILD IS INVISIBLE IF A STALE PROCESS KEEPS SERVING THE PREVIOUS BUNDLE. Playwright would have reused that server and tested a bundle built before every editor change made on 2026-10-13 -- including the destructive-mark CSS that took three review rounds -- and reported GREEN. That is the exact false-verified shape this drain has already been caught by twice, and here nothing in the output would have hinted at it. IT IS NOT ONLY A TEST-CORRECTNESS PROBLEM: the same live process held native `.node` bindings open, which is what made `npm ci` fail with `EPERM` on unlink -- once on a rolldown binding (task 8.3d's seat) and once on `@tailwindcss/oxide` (the controller). `ci` deletes before it installs, so that failure LEFT THE TREE WITHOUT ITS DEPENDENCIES; `npm install` recovered it. All three symptoms are one cause, and the cause is a process nobody reaps. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the repair is a decision with more than one defensible answer -- stop reusing servers (`reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI`, paying a startup per run), have the harness reap survivors before it starts, or make staleness detectable (a build stamp the config compares against the bundles on disk). Each trades differently between run time and the risk of a green run that proved nothing. NEAR ROWS: none -- the three `EPERM` reports this wave treated as environmental are this row. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether a browser run may reuse a server it did not start, and then the config change and a way to notice a stale one. OWNER: `src/web/playwright.config.ts`, with whoever owns the test-run hygiene in `AGENTS.md`'s verification rules. SEVERITY: high in kind and invisible in effect -- nothing fails, and the thing that is wrong is the evidence itself.

title: The editor's vite config names no CSS target, so lightningcss may drop an unprefixed declaration and ship only a vendor-prefixed one the browser cannot use
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE RETIRING `vg-311`, WHICH NAMED THIS CAUSE AND WAS NOT ITS SUBJECT. `vg-311` RECORDED A SYMPTOM: the built stylesheet carried only `-webkit-backdrop-filter` while `editor-shell.css` declared both forms, so a cluster's blur computed to `none` in a Chromium where `CSS.supports("backdrop-filter", "blur(1px)")` is true and `CSS.supports("-webkit-backdrop-filter", "blur(1px)")` is false. That symptom is GONE because the blur declarations were deleted outright, not because the emit was fixed. THE CAUSE STANDS: `src/web/packages/editor/vite.config.ts` sets no `css.lightningcss.targets` and the workspace has no browserslist, so lightningcss chooses the prefix set itself and is free to emit only the aliased form of any property it considers prefixable. `vg-311`'s own text draws the line: "a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one". WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A LINE IN THAT CHANGE: setting a target rewrites the whole built stylesheet for every package, and which browsers the editor supports is a support-matrix decision, not a styling one -- `vg-311` refused it for the same reason and so does this. WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: the failure mode is invisible. Nothing errors, a declaration silently does not apply, and the only instrument that caught it was a test reading the authored file BECAUSE the built one could not answer. NEAR ROWS: `vg-311` (its symptom, retired 2026-10-13). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on the editor's browser floor and then `css.lightningcss.targets` (or a browserslist) in each package's vite config, with a built-bundle assertion that a declared property survives the minifier in a form the target browsers accept. OWNER: `src/web/packages/*/vite.config.ts` with whoever owns the editor's support matrix. SEVERITY: low today and high in kind -- the class of defect it permits is a stylesheet that looks correct in source, builds green, and paints wrong only in the browsers nobody in the loop is using.

title: A glass-delta case measures itself against a repaint floor the editor no longer produces, so it fails on its own match-set guard rather than on glass
detail: FOUND BY PHASE 8'S CLOSE (2026-10-13), AND IT IS THE ONE FAILURE OF THAT CLOSE'S BROWSER PASS THAT IS BOTH REPRODUCIBLE AND THIS WAVE'S. `src/web/tests/e2e/glass-lifecycle.spec.ts:25` (§ the glass panel adds no repaint of its own) fails with `expect(measurement.withPanelMin).toBeGreaterThan(10)` reading **4**, and the full run read **3**. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: in the full suite the case is red; run alone at the same commit, serial (`--workers=1`), it is still red at 7.2s -- so it is not load. Run against the phase's base `614265de` with the wave's 18 production files reverted it **passes**, so this wave is its cause. THE CAUSE IS NAMED IN THE FILE'S OWN HEADER: "the editor runs a 30 Hz chart-refresh loop of its own, so an idle editor repaints about 22 times a second whatever glass is doing ... Measured, not assumed: every one of those 22 requests stacks to `LiveRuntime.refresh` and `ChartManager.refresh`." Commit `97264e6c perf(charts): a chart is drawn when its reading moves, not every frame` (row `vg-107`) deleted exactly that: `ChartManager.refresh()` no longer ends in an unconditional `canvas.requestRenderAll()`, so an idle editor with static readings now requests almost nothing. WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A PATCH IN THAT CLOSE: the product is behaving as `vg-107` intended -- an identical reading should not repaint -- so what broke is the **instrument**, and repairing it is a measurement decision with more than one defensible answer. The `> 10` guard is not decoration: it is the match set that stops the case passing vacuously, because with both windows at ~0 renders the delta `withPanelMin - withoutPanelMin` is trivially 0 and `compositesInOneFrame === 1` still holds. Options, none obviously right: drive a repaint the test owns each round (a rAF loop or a scene mutation), assert composites-per-editor-repaint with the floor taken over a window the test forces, or give the fixture readings that actually move so the family->pull path has something to draw. Each changes what the case proves. NEAR ROWS: `vg-107` (its cause, verified 2026-10-13); `vg-196` (`display-fabric`'s repaint check times out, a different file and mechanism). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on how a repaint-marginal property is measured over a demand-driven renderer, and then the case rewritten to that shape -- with the `> 10` guard replaced by something that cannot be satisfied by a still scene. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/glass-lifecycle.spec.ts`, with whoever owns what a canvas repaint is attributed to. SEVERITY: medium -- nothing in the product is wrong, but a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, and this one is the only browser instrument for glass's frames.

title: A settings DOM test cites `readStorage` by a line number that now lands on a JSX comment about the header strip
detail: FOUND BY PHASE 9 TASK 9.1'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-13), AND RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER BEFORE FILING BECAUSE THE CONTROLLER'S FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG IN TWO WAYS. `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.dom.test.tsx:117` reads: "`readStorage` answers `undefined` when the browser refuses it (`shell-layout.tsx:310`)". MEASURED AT `645020d0` WITH `awk 'NR==310'`, NOT WITH A `sed` RANGE: `shell-layout.tsx:310` is `{/* A full-width strip, not a floating card: the header is the window's`, the opening of a JSX comment about the header and §7.1. THE FILE IN THE CITATION IS STILL CORRECT AND THE CONTROLLER FIRST CLAIMED OTHERWISE: `readStorage` is defined at `shell-layout.tsx:122` in the same file, and it never left it -- the split moved it from line 348 to line 122 because the stores and the menubar were extracted ahead of it. So the citation's owner resolves; only its line does not. AND IT WAS ALREADY STALE BEFORE THIS WAVE: at `8b1b9106`, the phase's base, `readStorage` was at line 348 while the test already said 310, so the drift predates the split by 38 lines and the split moved the number again without anyone touching the citation. NOT FIXED WHERE IT WAS FOUND: the comment sits in a file the split did not otherwise touch, so repairing it is a change beside the task rather than inside it, which is AGENTS.md's bug rule for filing rather than fixing. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: the comment's whole job is to justify why a mounting with no store is a real product state instead of a harness fiction, and a reader who follows the pointer lands on markup that says nothing about storage, so the claim loses the evidence it was written to carry. THE SPECIES ALREADY HAS ROWS, WHICH IS WHY THIS ONE IS NARROW: the live register covers shipped source citing a plan's git-ignored execution state, and eleven rows citing a design file that was deleted -- both about citations that cannot be resolved at all. This is the in-file variant, where the pointer resolves to the right owner and the wrong place, which no existing row names. The register was grepped for an existing row before this one was written. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the citation rewritten to name the symbol rather than a line (`readStorage` in `editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx`) -- the house rule already applied to commit bodies, extended to a source comment. A lint that resolves `file.ts:NNN` citations inside source comments would settle the whole species, which is the larger fix this row is not. NEAR ROWS: `vg-276` (the split that moved the number again, verified 2026-10-13). OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.dom.test.tsx`. SEVERITY: low -- nothing behaves wrongly; the cost is a reader sent to the wrong place while checking a claim.

title: `EditorSession` assigns `#panelHosts` in its constructor and reads it nowhere, so the session's private shape advertises a channel it does not have
detail: FOUND BY PHASE 9 TASK 9.2'S IMPLEMENTER (2026-10-13) WHILE EXTRACTING THE DOCUMENT, CARRIED AS THAT COMMIT'S `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER, AND RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER BEFORE FILING. MEASURED AT `89db96b3` WITH A GREP FOR THE NAME OVER THE WHOLE FILE: `EditorSession.#panelHosts` is declared at `editor-session.ts:154`, assigned at `:169` from `options.panelHosts`, and read nowhere. THE OTHER SEVEN OCCURRENCES ARE A DIFFERENT OBJECT AND THAT IS WHY THE FIELD IS EASY TO MISREAD AS LIVE: they are reads of the constructor *option*, `options.panelHosts.document` / `.tokens` / `.selection` / `.add`, which is not the private field. PRE-EXISTING RATHER THAN INTRODUCED BY THE SPLIT: the field was assigned and unread before Task 9.2 moved the document out, so the split neither created it nor widened it. NOT FIXED IN THAT TASK: deleting a private field is a change to the class's own shape while its ownership is being redistributed, which makes it a change beside the task rather than inside it -- AGENTS.md's test for filing rather than fixing. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: an unread field that shares its name with a live option is a name that lies about what the session holds. A future refactor that wires it up believing it is load-bearing would be reading a value no one has ever written a consumer for, and the compiler would not object because the type is real. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: delete the field, and `EditorPanelHosts` too if the interface turns out to have no other reader -- the instrument is `npm run typecheck` plus the suites that already cover this class, which pass today with the field dead and so would pass with it gone. NEAR ROWS: `vg-374` (the split this was found during, verified 2026-10-13). OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-session.ts`. SEVERITY: low -- nothing behaves wrongly today; the cost is a misleading private shape in the file a reader is most likely to be learning from.

title: No check resolves a reference into the plans directory, so 55 register rows and 32 of 82 path references resolve to nothing
detail: FOUND BY PHASE 9 TASK 9.3'S FIX ROUND (2026-10-13) AND EXPANDED BY THAT TASK'S REVIEW, WHICH RAN ITS OWN WIDER SWEEP. Task 9.3 moved six plans to `archive/`, which broke references to them outside the directory. The fix round swept markdown links from `docs/` into `docs/superpowers/plans/` -- 24 links, 23 resolving, 1 broken -- and repaired four hrefs. The review then found the sweep's grammar was the limit: it could see markdown links and not code spans, and its commit message says "every link". THE FOUR SITES, MEASURED BEFORE FILING. (1) `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md:5` links `../plans/archive/2026-09-20-packaged-fonts.md`, and no correct target exists: `9135eb47` added that plan at `.agents/plans/2026-09-20-packaged-fonts.md`, it was never migrated into `docs/superpowers/plans/`, `.agents/plans/` no longer exists, and `04dc86dd` deleted its SDD workspace as one of "the five orphan workspaces". (2) `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-settings-scope.md:3` reads `Status: in progress` while its plan sits in `plans/archive/` -- the href beside it resolves and the status contradicts it. (3) `docs/product/triage/triage-B3.md:14` cites `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-766` in a **code span**, which the sweep's grammar could not see. (4) `docs/product/triage/triage-B1.md:51` cites `plans/README.md:5-6`, stale since this task rewrote that file. WHY 3 AND 4 ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN REPOINTED: both triage batches declare their baseline -- B1 is "cut contiguously from `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` at `87cc2311`", B3 is "Written at `87cc2311`" -- so they are snapshots of where a plan stood when the batch ran, and moving a plan does not falsify a record of where it was. Repointing them would edit a measurement to say something it never measured, which is the same ruling the controller applied to the three dated snapshots under `docs/architecture/`. They are listed because they are what an unbuilt check would have to cover, not because they are wrong. TWO FURTHER INSTANCES, NEITHER FIXED. **55 of the 70 rows carrying a `plan` field name an archived plan at a path that no longer resolves** -- 41 by a full `docs/superpowers/plans/<name>.md` path and 14 by a bare filename alone, across 11 distinct plans -- and only 15 of the 70 resolve. MEASURED 2026-10-13 BY RESOLVING EVERY `plan` FIELD AGAINST `docs/superpowers/plans/` AND ITS `archive/`, AFTER THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW SAID "ABOUT FIFTEEN" AND WAS WRONG BY MORE THAN THREE TIMES. So the register is not a marginal instance of this class but its largest one: almost every plan reference in `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` points at a name that has moved, and a reader following one concludes the plan was deleted. Whether those fields are meant to resolve or are historical labels is a question about the register's own semantics, so it is a ruling rather than a repoint; the measurement is what this row supplies for it. And the plans directory does have one live reader that the sweep never named: `scripts/check-status.mjs:188` resolves the active-plan slug against `docs/superpowers/plans/`, with no `archive/` fallback. It does not fire for today's active plan, whose full path resolves one line earlier at `:187` -- but it would reject a `STATUS.md` naming a plan that had been archived. THIS ROW'S OWN REVIEW MEASURED THE WHOLE CLASS RATHER THAN THIS MOVE, AND THE SCALE IS LARGER THAN THE MOVE. It enumerated every `...plans/...md` path token in tracked files with `git grep -o -E` and resolved each by hand: **82 references, 32 broken**, of which only 3 belong to this move's class (F1, and the two register files). The other 29 were already broken before this task moved anything -- `docs/decisions/0033-*.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-clock-and-theme-locale.md` each point at `2026-10-07-keyboard.md`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-github-issues-backlog-design.md` carries a **second** broken reference at a line the fix round did not touch even though it edited that same file at line 3; `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs` holds one as a self-test fixture; and six sit inside `plans/archive/`. So roughly a third of this repository's references into the plans directory resolved to nothing before this task began, which is what makes this a missing check rather than a consequence of six moves. THE CLASS IS THE FINDING: nothing resolves references of this kind. `design:check` lints `DESIGN.md` and its citations, `backlog:check` lints the register, and `design-md --cite` fails on a `section` marker that does not exist -- but no gate resolves a link or a path reference into the plans directory, and none compares a spec's status to where its plan now sits. The fix round's sweep is exactly that instrument and it lives in a scratch file, not in `scripts/`. WHY IT MATTERS: `archive/` exists so a moved plan stays readable, and a reference that points at the right name in the wrong place makes a reader conclude the document is gone. Moving six plans in one task is what made a sweep necessary; leaving the sweep unbuilt means the next move re-breaks the same references silently, and the next reader has no way to tell a moved plan from a deleted one. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the sweep promoted into `scripts/`, widened past markdown links to path references in code spans and prose, and wired into the gate chain so every reference from `docs/` into `plans/` is resolved on every run -- plus two rulings this row does not take: what a spec's `Status:` means once its plan is archived, and whether a register `plan` field is a live pointer or a historical label. NEAR ROWS: `vg-432` (a source comment citing a `file.ts:NNN` that now lands on unrelated markup) -- the same "nothing resolves a reference" class one level down, in code rather than in docs; `vg-152` (the directory truthfulness this was found under, verified 2026-10-13). OWNER: the reference convention across `docs/` together with `scripts/`, since the fix is a check rather than an edit. SEVERITY: low -- nothing behaves wrongly and no reader is blocked; the cost is a reader concluding a document was deleted when it was only moved, and the next six-plan move re-breaking the same references silently.

title: `controls-light.html` is named for the `light` palette and draws `editorial`'s, and the drawings README states the false claim outright
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE PLACING THE CONTROL SET'S PARITY CAPTURE -- the acceptance item says the capture sits "beside the matching mockup", so which mockup a drawing is had to be established before the pair could be read as matched. MEASURED, from the files. `docs/design/mockups/current/controls-light.html` declares `--bg:#fffdf7`, `--panel:#fffdf7`, `--panel2:#f5f1e8`, `--well:#f5f1e8`, `--text:#14120e` (lines 10 and 17-18). Those are `editorial`'s values exactly: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:186-195` gives `editorial` `--shell-backdrop:#f5f1e8`, `--shell-surface:#fffdf7`, `--shell-text:#14120e`. `light` is a **different palette and a different colour entirely** -- `editor-shell.css:400-402` gives it `--shell-surface:#eff9f2bf`, `--shell-surface-strong:#f8fffbdf` and `--shell-backdrop: linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)`, a mint. `DESIGN.md:86-87` lists them as two of the six (`editorial`, `graphite`, `ember`, `moss`, `plum`, `light`), and `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/palette.ts:16-22` keeps them distinct in `shellPalettes`, with `systemShellPalette` opening a light-reporting OS on `light` -- so the id is live and load-bearing, not vestigial. **THE DRAWING IS NOT A TOKEN SWAP OF EITHER PALETTE.** Its accent is `#0d7a6a`, which is neither `editorial`'s `--shell-accent:#14120e` (ink) nor `light`'s `#1c6b4f`, and its `--knob-edge` is the same `#0d7a6a`. So it is a hand-drawn light-mode variant on editorial's paper, and the token table was not swapped to any settled palette. **THE FALSE CLAIM IS IN A DURABLE DOC.** `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25` describes the file as "The same column in the light palette -- the same file with the token table swapped, so a hard-coded colour cannot hide in it". The second clause is the drawing's whole stated purpose, and the file does not do it. The same words are in the archived plan that created it (`docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-10-shell-parity.md:451`), so the intent was `light` from the start and the drawing never matched it. **THE LOOSE NAME HAS PROPAGATED INTO THE INSTRUMENT AND THE EVIDENCE.** `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:86` calls it "the same column on the light ground"; `:925` labels the parity row `region: "field row -- label column (controls-light drawing)"`; `src/web/tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts:464` calls it "its light twin"; and `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:59` says "the light ground `controls-light.html` draws (its `#fffdf7` paper)" -- a sentence that names the palette wrongly in the same breath as the value that contradicts it. **AND THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT POINTS AT ITSELF.** `controls-light.html:14-16` reads "`controls-light.html` is this file with the token table swapped and nothing else" -- cloned from `controls.html:16`, where the sentence is true, and not adapted, so on this copy it describes the file it is written in. The `<title>` (line 5) says "Vigilia inspector column, light" for the same reason. (`:7`'s `color-scheme: light` is correct and unrelated -- that is the CSS light-mode hint, not the palette id, and it is part of why the name reads as obvious.) **WHY THE COST IS NOT ZERO, GIVEN THE PAIR RENDERS FINE TODAY.** The capture that now sits beside it is `controls-capture-editorial.png`, correct because its ground is editorial, and the parity row reads geometry rather than colour -- so nothing is red. The hazard is the next reader: the acceptance item's clause is "its capture beside the **matching** mockup", and matching by name pairs this drawing with the `light` palette, whose capture would be mint. A reader, or a later capture run, that trusts the filename gets a surface the drawing does not show. **WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX.** Two readings, and they are different repairs: (a) the file was always meant to be `light` and should be re-drawn against `editor-shell.css:400`'s mint, which changes what the parity instrument checks (the region labels and the geometry both follow); or (b) the file is legitimately an editorial-ground drawing and should be renamed to `controls-editorial.html`, which is a five-site edit across the mockup, `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25`, `mockup-values.ts:106`/`:131`/`:925`, `mockup-values.test.ts:73`/`:398`, `design-language.spec.ts:464` and `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:59`. Which one is a design call about what the control set's second drawing is *for*, and (a) is a redraw of a checked drawing rather than a rename. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT:** the user picks (a) or (b). Under (b) the rename also fixes the README claim and the self-referential comment in one pass; under (a) the drawing is redrawn and the name becomes true. Either way the six-name palette list is the naming authority the file should agree with. NEAR ROWS: `vg-434` (references that resolve to nothing -- the same class, a name that does not mean what it says); `vg-319` (the control-set drawing's own unresolved facts, which this row's outcome changes the venue of, since both readings alter the drawing that row measures against); `vg-296` (a seventh drawing is read the moment it lands, which is how a rename would be picked up). OWNER: `docs/design/mockups/` together with `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts`, which is the instrument that names the drawing in its own regions. SEVERITY: low -- nothing renders wrongly and no gate is red; the cost is a name that means a palette the file does not draw, sitting in the acceptance instrument's own vocabulary. A THIRD READING, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHY OPTION (b) IS NOT THE CLEAN ONE. Option (b) reads the file as 'legitimately an editorial-ground drawing' and renames it, which is true of its paper - `--bg:#fffdf7`, `--panel:#fffdf7`, `--panel2:#f5f1e8` are editorial's exactly - and not true of its accent. `--accent:#0d7a6a` and `--knob-edge:#0d7a6a` appear nowhere in the product, and the six accents are `#1c6b4f` (baseline and light, `editor-shell.css:41` and `:409`), `#72e0c0` (graphite, `:146` and `:265`), `#14120e` (editorial, `:194`), `#8f4208` (ember, `:314`), `#38601a` (moss, `:347`) and `#543484` (plum, `:377`) - so the file matches no palette in either token. Renaming it `controls-editorial.html` would therefore replace a name that is false about the palette with one that is false about the accent. That leaves three repairs rather than two, and the third is the smallest: stop naming a palette at all, in `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25`'s 'the light palette' and in the instrument's labels and the evidence README, and describe the file as what it is - the same column on a light ground with a hand-drawn token table. THE PAIR'S STATED PURPOSE IS MET, MEASURED: the clause says the second file exists so 'a hard-coded colour cannot hide in it', and `controls.html` is graphite (`--bg:#0b0e12`, accent `#72e0c0`, the shell drawing's own palette at `current/shell.html:17-18`) while its twin is a light ground, so two grounds are drawn and the mechanism the clause describes exists. What is wrong is the name and the words that repeat it, not the pair.

title: A whole-suite browser run against a `dist` built by `npm run build` alone has no `control-fixture.html`, so `design-language.spec.ts:437` fails as a missing page and reads as a product regression
detail: MEASURED 2026-10-13, on the acceptance section's 'Are the fifteen met verdicts still supported' review. **The trap, measured rather than argued**: `npm run build -w @vigilia/editor` (exit 0) leaves `packages/editor/dist` holding `assets/`, `favicon.svg` and `index.html`; `npm run build:fixture -w @vigilia/editor` (exit 0) then adds `control-fixture.html`. The cause is deliberate and documented in `packages/editor/vite.config.fixture.ts`, whose docblock says the fixture is a second invocation rather than a second `rollupOptions.input` so the production build 'emits exactly the bundle graph it emitted before the fixture existed' and does not ship test scaffolding. So the page's existence depends on which build was run last, and a plain `npm run build` **deletes** it (`emptyOutDir` is true there, false in the fixture config). **What it costs.** Playwright's webServer previews `packages/editor` on 4174 and `openFixture` navigates to `http://127.0.0.1:4174/control-fixture.html`, so with the page absent that case fails on a 404 and looks identical to a design-language violation. **It has already produced a false classification in a durable record.** The phase-8 close annotation in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:915` triages the 18 whole-suite reds at `3a368c6a` and lists `design-language.spec.ts:437` among the three that are 'pre-existing, failing identically at base', with its cause correctly stated as 'its fixture page is not a vite input and so is absent from every built dist'. **The cause is right and the classification is wrong**: it failed identically at base only because neither run ran the recipe the repository documents, and at HEAD `aa16a2c5`, with `npm run build` then `npm run build:fixture`, the case **passes** (desktop-chromium, 15.4 s) in a whole-suite run. It is not pre-existing and it is not a product defect. **The recipe is documented and unowned.** Five places state it by hand - `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:8`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:510`, `docs/product/triage/triage-B6.md:11` and `triage-B5.md:120`, and the archived `plans/archive/2026-10-12-the-backlog-reproduction-pass.md:24` ('Build before browser runs') - and the archived `2026-10-11-settings-parity.md:29` records the exact hazard ('`npm run build -w @vigilia/editor` empties `dist` and deletes `control-fixture.html`, so `npm run build:fixture` must follow it'). No script enforces it: `test:e2e` is bare `playwright test`, and nothing in `playwright.config.ts` builds or asserts the page. **The decision it needs, which is why it is filed rather than fixed on the fly**: whether `npm run test:e2e` builds the fixture itself, or a `globalSetup` asserts the page exists and refuses with this cause, or the precondition stays documented and a run that skips it is simply wrong. Three owners could take it - the e2e config, the build scripts, or the docs - and each has a different cost: auto-building puts the fixture in every browser run including CI's, while asserting keeps the two builds separate and turns a 404 into a named refusal. **Scope, measured so the row is not read as bigger than it is**: this is the only case in either whole-suite sample that fails on a missing built page. `control-fixture.html` is reached by this case alone; the other fixture-opening specs (`glass-authoring`, `snapping`) build their own pages into the root preview and are unaffected. **Sampled beside it, at the same commits**: two whole-suite runs, `3a368c6a` (273 passed / 18 failed / 214 skipped) and `aa16a2c5` (273 / 18 / 214), whose red **memberships differ by nine of eighteen** - so a whole-suite red count is a load artefact rather than a defect list, and the five acceptance-relevant reds sampled from the second run (`shell-appearance.spec.ts:478`, `editor.spec.ts:1025`, `editor.spec.ts:2103`, `snapping.spec.ts:598` and `:702`) all pass alone and serial at that same commit.

title: A second colour parser lives in `renderer-core` with a different contract, so the ownership map's single 'shared colour parsing' row names only the editor's half
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 while self-reviewing `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md`, which had written the unification the wrong way round. **The duplication, measured.** `export function parseHex(input: string): Rgba | undefined` sits at `editor/src/components/ui/colour-maths.ts` beside `parseColour`, `toHex`, `rgbaToHsva` and `hsvaToRgba`, and **`export function parseHex(color: string): [number, number, number] | undefined` sits again at `renderer-core/src/charts/fill.ts`** — same name, same job, different return type. The editor's module is imported by exactly three files (`colour-picker.tsx`, `gradient-editor.tsx`, `colour-picker.test.ts`), so neither is shared with the other. **Why the map's row does not cover it.** `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the editor's file as the owner of 'shared colour parsing — hex, rgba and hsva conversion, and the refusal that returns `undefined` for a value that is not a colour', which is the row `vg-246`'s close added. That row is scoped to the Editor section, so `renderer-core`'s copy appears in no row at all — the same failure mode `vg-246` reported, one layer down and still true after its close. **`vg-246` is not a duplicate of this and did not measure it.** Its own detail ends with **NOT ESTABLISHED: 'whether colour-maths.ts is the right owner (it is a components/ui helper, which may be why it was never promoted) or whether other colour parsing exists that the survey did not find'** — and it closed `verified` against `dd308143` on the narrower check, that the map promotes the de-facto owner and drops the Known-ownership-gaps bullet. The map row is real; the second implementation is the half its own text left open, now measured. **The direction that cannot be built, which is what the spec had to correct.** The obvious unification — the editor's module owns it and `fill.ts` consumes it — is an upward import: `renderer-core` imports nothing from `editor` (measured), and the editor bundles `renderer-core` from source through a Vite alias, so that direction is a cycle. Any single-owner resolution therefore moves the primitive **down** into `renderer-core` and leaves the editor's richer conversions consuming it, or scopes the claim to the editor and records `fill.ts`'s tuple parser as a deliberately separate contract for chart fill strings. **Owner and cost.** Whoever owns the map decides, and the spec's decision currently takes the first: primitive down, `colour-maths.ts` keeps `Hsva`/`rgbaToHsva`/`hsvaToRgba`/`toHex` and consumes it, `fill.ts` retires its copy, and the ownership row moves with the primitive. The cost if that is wrong is a package-boundary move of one small pure module plus a row rewrite; the cost of leaving it is a third parser the next colour surface will write.

title: The acceptance instrument renders its own text at a line-height DESIGN.md does not state, and no reader reads the property, so the drawings show a rhythm the design language does not
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13, as the residue of `vg-437` once that row's product half was fixed. **MEASURED, in a browser, every drawing in `current/`.** Each of the six was loaded in Chromium and every element holding its own text was tallied by resolved `font-size`/`line-height`: 12px text renders at 17.4px (1.450) in `settings-about.html` (7 elements), `settings-keyboard.html` (24), `settings.html` (4) and `shell.html` (7); 11px text renders at 15.95px (1.45) in `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` (12 each), `shell.html` (12) and `settings.html` (7). Not one element in any drawing renders at a ratio DESIGN.md states. Elements whose computed line-height was `normal` were excluded rather than counted, so these are explicit values only and the drawings hold more text than the tally shows. **WHERE THE RATIO COMES FROM.** `settings-about.html:10` declares `font: 12px/1.45` in the file's `<style>` block - the page body - and the modal inside it declares no line-height of its own, so every drawn element inherits 1.45. Section 2's companions are 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.3, 1.3 and 1.2 for 10, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 19px, so 1.45 is on none of them. **WHY THE DRAWING IS THE STALE SIDE AND NOT THE COMPETING RULE.** The drawings README states the precedence in its own words: 'Where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale.' `design-language.spec.ts:3058-3065` adds that the page furniture 'is read like everything else' and passes today only because its values happen to be on the scale - so a furniture value off the scale was always going to redden that row, and does not only because `design-language.spec.ts:3054-3057` reads no line-height at all and states that limit as dispositioned. `vg-437`'s product half was fixed on 2026-10-13 against section 2, which leaves the instrument as the only side still rendering 1.45. **WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT AN EDIT.** The correction is not one value: section 2 gives each size its own companion, and a single page-body ratio cannot express six of them, so each drawn text element would have to state the ratio for the token it already uses - six files, every text element in each, and it changes the rendered rhythm of the thing this project compares the product against. It also cannot be verified by the gate that reads these files, because that gate reads no line-height. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** The furniture stops carrying a ratio and each drawn element states its token's companion, in the same commit as any re-shoot of the frames beside it - which nothing currently does (`vg-402`). **OWNER.** The drawings are the acceptance instrument the user ruled on 2026-10-10 (`STATUS.md`), so correcting them is that owner's act; a gate change that could see the property is a separate one and is named here rather than assumed. NEAR ROWS: `vg-437` (the product half, landed), `vg-326` (the same files' line-height from section 3's side, whose 'sets no line-height' clause this measurement corrects), `vg-402` (the stale frames).

title: DESIGN.md closes section 5's control vocabulary with no labelled button in it, while sections 2, 4 and 7.1 name 'the primary button' and three product owners render labelled buttons, so a control the editor uses in three places has no shape in the language
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13, reading DESIGN.md against the tree while answering `vg-316`, and it is that row's cause rather than its content. **MEASURED.** Section 5 opens its vocabulary table with 'The vocabulary is closed. A control is one of these, or it is not a control.' (`DESIGN.md:403`) and lists nine: Well, Well with chevron, Well with unit, Slider + well, Swatch well, Toggle, Segmented, Icon button, Choice row. No entry is a labelled button. Every filled entry in that list is `--panel-2`-filled (Well, Segmented, Choice row), and the only action entry, Icon button, is 'glyph only' with no resting border (rule 6). **THE WORD `button` OCCURS IN DESIGN.md THREE TIMES AND ALWAYS AS THE PRIMARY ONE.** `:110` in section 4's rationing ('the selected rail slot, the focused control, the selected row, the primary button'); `:150` in section 2's weights ('650-700 only for the brand mark and a primary button'); `:203` in section 7.1 ('Right: the publish chord, then the primary button. `Publish` is the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor.'). No line in the file states a secondary or labelled button's fill, border, radius, padding or text colour. **THE PRODUCT RENDERS LABELLED BUTTONS IN THREE OWNERS.** `ACTION_BUTTON`, which three dialogs' `.vigilia-dialog-actions` wrap; `.editor-shell-dialog > button` (`editor-shell.css:1587`), which reaches the settings modal's Close and the `?` sheet's; and `.editor-shell-keyboard-action` (`:1782`), 21 of them on the keyboard tab. Every button those owners render therefore carries a shape the design language does not define, and `vg-316`'s difference is the visible consequence: the acceptance instrument and the product resolved the gap differently, and neither resolution can be called wrong by a cited rule. **WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-SENTENCE EDIT.** `:203`'s 'the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor' reads two ways - co-ordinately (no other button is both filled and accent-coloured, which permits the product's control-bg fill) or restrictively (no other button is filled, which forbids it and forbids the drawing's `--panel-2` fill too). The two readings disagree about every labelled button in the editor, and section 5's 'closed' claim is only true under the second. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** A ruling on which reading holds, then either a section 5 entry for the secondary button stating its fill, border, radius, padding and text colour, or the correction of every filled labelled button in the product and in the drawings to the unfilled treatment. **OWNER.** DESIGN.md is the redesign's target document, so this is the design language's owner. NEAR ROWS: `vg-316` (the difference this gap makes undecidable), `vg-440` (the drawings' own stale half), `vg-402` (the frames nothing re-shoots).

title: No check compares a drawing's drawn type to the product's, and none reads a pane surface's rendered type either, so the shell's plain-DOM control boxes are type-checked by neither route
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13, measuring why `vg-274`'s one surviving D9 value cannot be closed with a check. **THE TWO ROUTES AND WHAT EACH REFUSES.** (1) The declared-versus-drawn comparison (`src/web/tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts`, the `productRows` block) reads a declaration out of the product's stylesheet and a declaration out of a drawing and compares the two strings. It carries those boxes' `padding` today - `.editor-shell-panel [data-vigilia-asset-import]` and `.editor-shell-inspector [data-vigilia-run-add]`, both against the one box `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:112` draws. It cannot carry their TYPE: the drawing states that box's type as the shorthand `font:400 12px system-ui`, and `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:392-399` refuses to answer a `font-size` question with it, deliberately, with the reason in its message ('this row reads the longhand, so a shorthand is a value it cannot see and would read as the drawing's silence'). Reading the drawing's whole `font` instead and comparing strings does not work either, because the product's idiom is a scale token (`var(--text-sm)`) where the drawing writes literals. (2) The scale route (`design-language.spec.ts:2846-2862`) compares a RENDERED value against a declared scale token, which is the shape that fits this row ('control text is section 2's `--text-sm` 12px'), and it needs the element rendered. Those boxes render inside the Add pane's file section and the inspector's action rows, and the surfaces that test reads are a whitelist in the spec itself (`:2790-2795`: the shell, `settings`, `settings-keyboard`, `settings-about`, `sheet`, `fixture`), so a row on a pane is not merely unread - it is rejected by a guard that exists to stop a typo being skipped by both tests. **WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHAT IT WOULD HAVE PROTECTED.** The value is live: the two rules declare no `font-size` and so inherit the shell root's `var(--text-md)` 13px (`editor-shell.css:687-689`, `:1317-1328`, `:1353-1363`), where section 2 gives control text `--text-sm` 12px and the same drawing's own instances state 12px (`docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:137`, `:140`). A third rule of the same shape, `.editor-shell-panel .vigilia-layer-rename` (`:1332`), is in no drawing at all, so its correct size is a question no instrument can ask either. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** Either a shorthand-aware reading in the declared-versus-drawn block - which is a decision about `mockup-values.ts`'s stated refusal rather than a repair of it - or a pane surface registered in the scale route; either, plus the declarations themselves. **OWNER**: the parity instrument's owner, because each candidate changes how the acceptance instrument reads rather than what the product renders. NEAR ROWS: `vg-274` (the value this instrument would protect), `vg-437` (this file's line-height half, whose instrument is a source contract rather than a parity row), `vg-441` (the same rules' fill, whose gap is in DESIGN.md). NARROWED 2026-10-13: THE VALUE IS FIXED, THE DRAWING COMPARISON IS STILL ABSENT. The type this row described is now stated by the three rules and asserted in a browser by `tests/e2e/add-pane.spec.ts`'s 'the pane's file controls take control text, not the shell's 13px base', so what remains is not the value but the route. Neither candidate has moved: `mockup-values.ts:392-399` still refuses to answer a `font-size` question with the `font` shorthand the drawings write (`controls.html:112` writes `font:400 12px system-ui`), and the scale route still reads a whitelist of surfaces (`design-language.spec.ts:2790-2795`) that names no pane, so a scale row for a pane element is rejected by a guard rather than merely unread. **What that leaves uncaught is a change on the drawing's side**: a redrawn box whose type moved would redden nothing, because the product's declaration is pinned by the pane's own spec and not by the drawing it is measured against. The declaration half is no longer open; this row is the instrument half alone.

title: The inspector's and the panel's section headings render in a serif display face in six of eight declarations, where §2 gives headings UI sans and every drawing draws sans
detail: FOUND BY RE-MAKING PLAN 1'S PARITY COMPARISON (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`), and confirmed at the rule. WHAT: `.editor-shell-panel h2, .editor-shell-inspector h2` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1142-1151`) sets `font-family: var(--shell-display)` alongside `font-size: var(--text-md)`, `text-transform: uppercase` and `letter-spacing: 0.14em`. `--shell-display` is `ui-serif, Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif` at six declarations (`:70`, `:199`, `:323`, `:353`, `:383`, `:421`) and `system-ui, sans-serif` at two (`:151`, `:270`), so in six palettes the heading block is serif. WHY IT REACHES TEXT THAT LOOKS LIKE IT DECLARES ITS OWN TYPE: the section header's children — the eyebrow span, the count span and the `Read-only` marker — set their own size, weight and tracking but no family (`components/ui/inspector-section.tsx:69`, `:75`, `:81`), so the family is inherited from the h2. WHAT THE RULE SAYS: §2's family table gives UI sans 'Everything a person reads as language | Labels, menus, headings, panel copy' (`DESIGN.md:123`) and confines theme fonts to 'Inside the artboard only; never in chrome' (`:125`); no clause grants a chrome heading a display face, and `DESIGN.md` names no serif family anywhere. WHAT THE DRAWINGS SAY: every current drawing draws those headings in `system-ui` (`docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:29` and `:169`), and the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 makes the drawing the acceptance instrument. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: `--shell-display` is declared *per palette*, which reads as a deliberate palette-level identity rather than an oversight, and that puts this row beside `vg-441` — a chrome property no clause of `DESIGN.md` names in either direction, so neither the product's face nor the drawing's can be called wrong by a cited rule. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 clause granting a chrome display face, in which case the drawings are the stale side; or dropping `font-family` from that rule, which is the direction §2 and all six drawings already agree on. ALSO RECORDED, because it is a trap rather than a live difference: the rule's own `--text-md` 13px and `.14em` tracking are inert today only because every child span states its own size and tracking, so any bare text added to an `h2` would take 13px uppercase serif tracking. MEASURED IN A BROWSER 2026-10-13, WHICH IS WHAT MOVES THIS ROW FROM A READ TO AN OBSERVATION. The class changes that fixed the *count*'s family (`inspector-section.tsx`'s section-count span now states `font-mono` and `text-faint`) were red-proved in `inspector-sections.spec.ts` before the rebuild, and the failure prints exactly the inheritance this row describes: `expect(...).toMatch(/mono/i)` received `"ui-serif, Georgia, \"Times New Roman\", serif"` for `[data-vigilia-section-count]`'s computed `font-family`. So the count was rendering in the h2's display face, on a build made from this tree, in the default palette. THE FIX MOVES ONLY THE COUNT. The eyebrow span and the `Read-only` marker still declare no family (`inspector-section.tsx:69`, `:81`) and so still inherit `--shell-display`, and the subject's name in `inspector.tsx` now states its weight but no family, so it takes the shell's sans — which means this row's remaining subject is two elements in the same header, not the whole block: §2 assigns headings to UI sans, all six drawings draw sans, and six of eight `--shell-display` declarations are serif.

title: An attended layer row whose reserved strip is wider than its own columns can spare runs the role under the state slot, which paints over it
detail: FOUND BY FIXING `vg-265` ON 2026-10-13, MEASURED ON A BUILT BUNDLE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT FIX DOES NOT REACH. `vg-265` was the slot painting its surface whether or not it held a control, so every row at rest lost the role's last glyphs to a six-pixel block that drew nothing; that half is fixed — the surface and the 6px lead-in now belong to the slot's buttons (`.vigilia-layer-state:has(button)`), and `composition-panel.spec.ts`'s 'the state slot does not cover the role' reads every row at rest, role against slot, and passes. THE HALF THAT REMAINS: once the slot holds real controls the reservation is real too, and on a row where the reserved strip is wider than what the row's columns can spare, the in-flow line overflows to the right and the role ends up under the slot. MEASURED at 1280×720, desktop-chromium, the starter document: a hovered or selected chart row (`network-chart`, three controls, 96px reserved) leaves the role 45.3px under the slot, and a row drawing four (`group-time-card` hovered, or `group-large` selected in the two-hundred-row document, 126px reserved) leaves 53.8px of it covered — the whole role, since the role is 26px wide there. WHY THE FIX IS NOT A FIX: the row's three columns are each recorded as never giving way — the mark is `flex: 0 0 28px`, the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` with a `min-width: 6ch` floor, and the role is `flex: none` with the stylesheet's own sentence 'it is never the element that gives up width: a role that clipped or ellipsised would say nothing' — so at 246px a four-control row (122px of controls on a 218px row) has no column left that may yield, and which one does is a design decision rather than a bug fix. The candidates, none of them free: lower the name's 6ch floor when the slot needs the room (the name ellipsises instead of the role being covered, and the panel's own record already measures name clipping as its cost); let the role clip in this one case (contradicting the sentence above, though a clipped role says more than a painted-over one); or move the role out of the slot's path (a layout change, since the role reads between the name and the key). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on which column yields, the same `:has` arms re-derived from it, and this file's case extended from the at-rest sweep to the attended one — the assertion is already written in the case's comment and was removed from the test because it would have asserted a defect as a pass condition. NEAR ROWS: `vg-265` (the half this came out of, closed the same day), `vg-260` (the same row width, measured from the key column's side), `vg-301`.

title: The rail slot's radius is --radius-lg where section 4 gives a control --radius-md
detail: FOUND BY FIXING `vg-227` ON 2026-10-13, WHILE WRITING THE §5 ROW THAT RULING ASKS FOR, AND IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS THE ROW IT WAS FOUND IN: a value off DESIGN.md's own tables that no gate watches. `editor-shell.css` sets the rail's slot to `border-radius: 8px`, which is §4's `--radius-lg`; §4 assigns `--radius-lg` to "Panels, cards, tiles in a grid" and gives `--radius-md` (6px) to "Controls, menu rows, small tiles". The slot is a control — the 2026-10-12 ruling made it a §5 vocabulary entry of its own rather than stretching the icon button's range — and its nearest neighbour in §5, the glyph-only icon button it is deliberately larger than, is `--radius-md`. NOTHING IS INCONSISTENT BETWEEN THE TWO RENDERERS: `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html` draws the same 8px, so the drawing and the product agree, and the drawing's slot is deliberately excluded from the parity module's copied-element list (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts`), so no gate reads the value at all. WHAT IS UNESTABLISHED IS THE INTENT: §4 steps radius by role rather than by size, so a 36px control carrying a larger radius may be exactly the intent, or 8px may be the value that was never brought down when the slot's size was. OWNER: whoever owns the rail slot's radius; the two candidates are §5's own row — which now states `--radius-lg`, because that is what renders — and §4's control assignment. SEVERITY: low and visual only, and reversing it is a two-file edit (the product's slot rule and the drawing's five spans).
